כאן רושמים תוצאות. המערכת מעריכה כל תוצאה (accepted/rejected) לפי נתוני האב. זמין גם ייצוג גרפי וערכים היסטוריים.
לרישום: Transaction QE51N או Logistics • Quality Management • Quality Inspection • Worklist • Results Recording. Figure 3.6 — מסך הבחירה של ה-worklist, עם לשוניות. ניתן לחפש ולרשום תוצאות של סוגי בדיקה שונים (דגימות פיזיות, ציוד, functional locations).
הזינו Plant "1710", ‏Execute (Figure 3.7). מאפיין 10; לפי ה-sampling procedure, המערכת מחשבת 100 (טור Inspect) לשני המאפיינים (Visual Inspection, ‏Purity). מאחר שהם דורשים תוצאות מסוכמות, הזינו ב-Result. המערכת מעריכה כל ערך (accepted/rejected).

טבלה 3.2 — סטטוס מאפיינים (טור Status): 0 (ניתן לעיבוד); 1 (חובה לעבד); 2 (עובד); 3 (הוערך); 4 (Skip); 5 (העיבוד הושלם); 6 (העברה ל-subsystem); 7 (קבוע, לא לעיבוד); 9 (חסום להערכות); A (מאפיין חובה כשהבקרה accepted); B (מאפיין חובה כשהבקרה rejected).

**הערה:** חקרו את הסמלים. ‏Check לשלמות; ‏lock/unlock לרישום.
Figure 3.8 — מאפיין 10, ‏Details. הפרטים בשמאל (Specs: Fixed Insp. Scope). מאחר שדורש classed values — נרשמו 100, מהם 20 לא-מתאימים (10 מעל, 10 מתחת), 80 מקובלים. טור Val: ✓ ירוק = accepted, ‏X אדום = rejected; טור Defect Class מסווג כל דחייה.
Figure 3.9 — סקירת חמשת המאפיינים. מאפיין 30 (calculated): הנוסחה שוקלת את ממוצע 10 (95.0) × 1.15 = 109.250. מאפיין 50 (האחרון): מפרט ייחודי לספק 9980000067 (לפי ה-dependent characteristic מפרק 2).
**Tips and Tricks:** ניתן ליצור פגמים ברישום ב-Defect Class (Figure 3.9).
בחרו את המאפיין הראשון, אז Run Values (Run Chart) (Figure 3.10) — ייצוג גרפי של מאפיין 10.
**Tips and Tricks:** זמינים עוד תצוגות — control chart, ‏histogram, ‏results history.
Figure 3.11 — אפליקציית Display Results History עם מדדים (mean, ‏variance, ‏Cp, ‏Cpk) וגרפים. ‏Cp ו-Cpk הם מדדי יכולת תהליך: ‏Cp — פיזור התהליך (האם מבוקר — כמה צמוד לגבולות ביחס לשונות הטבעית); ‏Cpk — מיקום הממוצע ביחס לגבולות (האם התהליך מסוגל; התאמה ל-Cp להתפלגות לא-ממורכזת). לתהליך מבוקר ומסוגל — שניהם > 1.33. בתעשיות רבות המינימום כעת 2.0+! (פרק 19).
מאפיין 40 (Figure 3.9) — המערכת מפעילה אוטומטית יצירת notification ברישום פגם (Figure 3.12). הפגם מסומן בטור Charac. Defects. לאחר הזנת Code ו-Defect Loc., בחרו Activate Notification. ניתן עוד פרטים (notification type, בעיה), ‏Continue.
Figure 3.13 (Transaction QM03) — המערכת יצרה notification 200000061 וה-lot 10000000702.
**Tips and Tricks:** וריאנטים לרישום (Logistics • Quality Management • Quality Inspection • Worklist • Variants for Results Recording): דגימות פיזיות — Transaction QE52; כל ה-lots — QE72; ‏inspection points — QE71; ‏MICs — QE73. ניתן גם QA32 (Worklist for Inspection Lots) (פרק 18).
**הערה:** נשתמש ב-Transaction QE01 בהמשך הספר.

**הערת יועץ:** results-recording (QE51N; גם-QE01/QE11 per-lot) — הזנת-תוצאות + הערכה אוטומטית/ידנית (accepted/rejected לפי-האב). מנקודת-מבט-מעשית, QE51N = worklist מרכזי; גרפיקה+היסטוריה זמינות. יועץ מנוסה מבין: ההערכה נשענת על-סבולות-ה-MIC — אב-שגוי = הערכה-שגויה. ההבחנה הערכה-אוטומטית (מהסבולות) מול-ידנית (שיקול-בודק). תיעוד ברמת-characteristic/sample. הבנת-ה-recording חיונית — הנתון-הגולמי של-כל-האיכות.

sections.title: Usage Decision
sections.en: 3.1.3 Usage Decision Now that results and defects (if any) are recorded for an inspection lot, the final steps are to make a decision to use the material, which is known as the usage decision, and to perform a stock posting of an inspection lot. The stock posting transfers the stock placed in quality inspection into either an unrestricted-use stock or any other stock type. The stock posting depends on the inspection type and inspection origin. To record the usage decision of an inspection lot, use Transaction QA11 or follow menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Quality Inspection  Inspection Lot  Usage Deci- sion  Record. The screen that appears provides an option to enter a usage decision for a single inspection lot. However, there are several other options available to efficiently manage the task of performing a usage decision. The various icons (discussed in Sec- tion 3.2) located in the menu bar are as follows:  Mass Usage Decisions This ensures that for all inspection lots for which the quality management (QM) user needs to assign a single “accepted” code to several inspection lots, the user can do so on a single screen and with one transaction.  Quantity Posting Required The entire activity of recording a usage decision stipulates two steps: the first step is to assign a usage decision code to an inspection lot, and the second step is to per- form stock posting. This option is available to business users; the usage decision code is already assigned to an inspection lot (the first step is already performed), but 3 Quality Inspection 122 the user still needs to perform the important step of stock posting (the second step). All such open inspection lot quantities are available in the form of a worklist to work on.  UD Not Taken Yet This option brings up a complete worklist of all the inspection lots for which the QM user needs to make usage decisions.  Inspection Lots without Completion This option offers a complete worklist of all inspection lots that are incomplete in one form or another and are therefore open. For this example, enter inspection lot “10000000702” and press (Enter) so that the screen in Figure 3.14 appears. Here you see the Defects tab, which appears only when the system records any defects during results recording. Moreover, you can also record defects during a usage decision by choosing Defects located on the top menu bar or cre- ate and activate a quality notification by choosing Notification. Defect recording is cov- ered in detail in Section 3.1.5. On this screen, choose the Characteristics tab to see the summarized results recording available for evaluation before the user makes a usage decision. You can expand the characteristic details by choosing All Characteristics. Figure 3.14 Characteristics in Usage Decision Select the box to the right of UD Code and press (F4) or choose the dropdown option. The popup that appears provides a list of options available to the user to choose a usage decision code. Each usage decision code valuates the inspection lot as either accepted or rejected. The usage decision code also internally assigns a quality score to help in © 123 3.1 Business Processes in Quality Inspection overall quality calculation of supplier-delivered material. These quality scores form the basis of future procurement decisions with a supplier. Quality scores are automatically updated with each usage decision. The relevant quality score isn’t shown until the user selects the usage decision code. Choose UD Code A, and the system automatically also assigns its associated catalog or selected set, 01. With usage decision code A assigned, the system automatically assigns the corresponding quality score of 100 (see Chapter 19 for more information on quality scores). Depending on the settings made in the material master, the system automatically cal- culates and incorporates the shelf-life expiration date/best-before date (SLED/BBD), or you can enter it manually. You also have the option to enter the long text of the usage decision by choosing the Long Text icon located next to Code Valuation to enter any additional details.
sections.he:
עם התוצאות והפגמים, הצעדים האחרונים — ה-usage decision ו-stock posting. ה-stock posting מעביר את המלאי מ-quality inspection ל-unrestricted (או אחר); תלוי בסוג ובמקור הבדיקה.
לרישום: Transaction QA11 או Logistics • Quality Management • Quality Inspection • Inspection Lot • Usage Decision • Record. אפשרויות בסרגל (3.2):
• **Mass Usage Decisions:** הקצאת קוד "accepted" יחיד למספר lots במסך אחד.
• **Quantity Posting Required:** הקוד כבר הוקצה (צעד 1) אך נדרש stock posting (צעד 2) — worklist.
• **UD Not Taken Yet:** worklist של lots ללא usage decision.
• **Inspection Lots without Completion:** worklist של lots פתוחים.
בדוגמה, הזינו "10000000702", ‏Enter (Figure 3.14). לשונית Defects מופיעה רק אם נרשמו פגמים. ניתן לרשום פגמים גם כאן (Defects) או ליצור notification (3.1.5).
בחרו לשונית Characteristics לתוצאות המסוכמות. ‏All Characteristics להרחבה.
בתיבת UD Code, ‏F4/dropdown — רשימת קודי ה-usage decision. כל קוד מעריך accepted/rejected, ומקצה פנימית quality score (בסיס להחלטות רכש עתידיות; מתעדכן בכל החלטה).
בחרו UD Code A — המערכת מקצה גם catalog/selected set 01 ו-quality score 100 (פרק 19). לפי אב החומר, המערכת מחשבת SLED/BBD (או ידני). ניתן Long Text.

לאחר-שתוצאות ופגמים (אם-היו) תועדו ל-inspection-lot, השלבים-הסופיים הם-קבלת החלטה על-שימוש-בחומר — ה-usage-decision — וביצוע stock-posting של-ה-lot. ה-stock-posting מעביר את-המלאי שהוצב ב-quality-inspection ל-unrestricted-use-stock או-לכל-סוג-מלאי אחר, בהתאם-ל-inspection-type ול-inspection-origin. לתיעוד-ה-usage-decision משתמשים ב-Transaction-QA11 או-menu-path (Logistics • Quality-Management • Quality-Inspection). עבור-היועץ, ה-usage-decision הוא-רגע-ההכרעה של-כל-הבדיקה: כל-מה-שקדם (lot, results, defects) מתנקז להחלטה-אחת — לקבל (accept) או-לדחות (reject) — המתועדת בקוד-UD מקטלוג-type-3. ההבחנה בין-ה-UD (ההחלטה-הלוגית — מה-דין-החומר) ל-stock-posting (הפעולה-הפיזית — לאן-המלאי-עובר) מהותית: הן-קשורות אך-נפרדות, וב-lots מסוימים (לא-מבוססי-מלאי) אין-stock-posting כלל. קוד-ה-UD קובע גם-follow-up-actions (אוטומציה: מייל, שינוי-סטטוס) וגם-את-ה-quality-score המשפיע על-vendor-evaluation ועל-dynamic-modification. לאחר-UD לא-ניתן-עוד לתעד-פגמים — נקודת-אל-חזור. הבנת-ה-usage-decision חיונית — היא-ההחלטה שסוגרת את-הבדיקה ומניעה את-כל-ההשלכות (מלאי, ספק, quality-level). יועץ מנוסה מגדיר קטלוג-UD-codes ברור עם-follow-up-actions מתאימים, ומדריך שה-UD אינו-פורמליות אלא-החלטה בעלת-השלכות-רוחב.

**הערת יועץ:** usage-decision (QA11; QA32 worklist) — רגע-ההכרעה: accept/reject בקוד מקטלוג-type-3. מנקודת-מבט-מעשית, UD ≠ stock-posting (החלטה-לוגית מול-תנועה-פיזית). יועץ מנוסה מבין: קוד-UD מפעיל follow-up-actions + מעדכן quality-score (vendor-eval, dynamic-modification). ⚠️ אחרי-UD אין-defects. ההבחנה UD (דין-החומר) מול-posting (יעד-המלאי). הבנת-ה-UD חיונית — סוגר-בדיקה, מניע-השלכות-רוחב.

sections.title: Stock Posting
sections.en: 3.1.4 Stock Posting In the Inspection Lot Stock tab shown in Figure 3.15, you enter the inspection lot quan- tity into one of the several options available to perform the stock posting. These options are as follows:  To Unrestricted Use The quantity placed in quality inspection is available as free to consume.  To Scrap The company destroys some or all of the quantity placed in quality inspection due to the defective quality of the material. The scrapped quantity is charged to the rele- vant cost center that you assigned in configuration.  To Sample Consumptn Either the system or the user can enter some quantity of material consumed as sam- ples.  To Blocked Stock Some or all of the quantity placed in quality inspection is placed in blocked/ restricted-use stock. This stock isn’t available to use.  To New Material You can perform transfer posting of one material into another material after evalu- ating that the material fits more with the new/different material than the original material.  To Reserves You can assign some quantity to reserve stock for subsequent use.  Return Delivery (not shown) You decide to return complete or partial quantity to the supplier due to defective quality or noncompliance with specifications. 3 Quality Inspection 124 Tips and Tricks Right next to each stock type, you can choose details to view or change default infor- mation. For example, you can choose the Document button (which will show Details when you hover over it) of the To Scrap field and change the default cost center. In Figure 3.15, the system shows that out of 100 PC of inspection lot quantity (Insp. Lot Qty), you can post up to a quantity of 90 PC to unrestricted-use stock (or any other stock type available), while the system automatically calculates the sample use of 100 PC. Figure 3.15 Inspection Stock Posting This sample calculation is based on the settings that you made for the relevant master inspection characteristic. You can enter any combination here that reflects the actual stock posting that you want to perform. For example, you can delete the sample-use quantity of 10 PC, and post the entire 100 PC of inspection lot quantity to unrestricted- use or blocked stock. For this example, enter To Unrestricted Use as “90” and To Sample Consumptn as “10”. Choose the Document button, and Figure 3.16 appears. If you need to change the docu- ment or posting dates, then you can do so here; otherwise, this step is unnecessary. © 125 3.1 Business Processes in Quality Inspection Figure 3.16 Usage Decision Header Data If a material is batch-managed, then you can also change the batch status to restricted or unrestricted, as deemed necessary. Otherwise, you can separately change the status of a batch using Transaction MSC2N (Change Batch).
sections.he:
בלשונית Inspection Lot Stock (Figure 3.15), הזינו את כמות ה-lot לאפשרויות ה-posting:
• **To Unrestricted Use:** זמין לצריכה חופשית.
• **To Scrap:** השמדה בשל איכות פגומה; מחויב למרכז העלות בתצורה.
• **To Sample Consumptn:** כמות שנצרכה כדגימות.
• **To Blocked Stock:** מלאי חסום/מוגבל (לא זמין).
• **To New Material:** transfer posting לחומר אחר.
• **To Reserves:** מלאי שמור לשימוש עוקב.
• **Return Delivery:** החזרה לספק (איכות פגומה/אי-התאמה).
**Tips and Tricks:** ליד כל סוג, ‏Document לפרטים (למשל שינוי מרכז העלות ב-To Scrap).
ב-Figure 3.15, מתוך 100 PC (Insp. Lot Qty), ניתן עד 90 PC ל-unrestricted, והמערכת מחשבת sample use 100 PC. הדגימה לפי ה-MIC. ניתן כל צירוף (למשל מחיקת 10 PC sample-use ורישום כל 100 ל-unrestricted/blocked).
בדוגמה, ‏To Unrestricted Use "90", ‏To Sample Consumptn "10". בחרו Document (Figure 3.16) לשינוי תאריכים (אחרת מיותר).
אם מנוהל-אצווה, ניתן לשנות סטטוס אצווה (restricted/unrestricted), או בנפרד ב-Transaction MSC2N.

בלשונית-ה-Inspection-Lot-Stock (Figure 3.15) מזינים את-כמות-ה-inspection-lot לאחת-מהאפשרויות לביצוע-ה-stock-posting: **To-Unrestricted-Use** — הכמות שהוצבה ב-quality-inspection זמינה-לצריכה-חופשית; **To-Scrap** — החברה משמידה חלק-מהכמות או-כולה עקב-איכות-פגומה, והכמות-הגרוטה מחויבת ל-cost-center הרלוונטי שהוקצה-בתצורה; **To-Sample** — כמות-המדגם שנצרכה-בבדיקה; ואפשרויות-נוספות (blocked-stock, return-to-vendor, new-material). עבור-היועץ, מסך-ה-stock-posting הוא-המקום שבו-החלטת-האיכות הופכת לתנועת-מלאי בפועל: כל-שורה מייצרת material-document עם-movement-type מתאים (321 QI→unrestricted, 350 QI→blocked, 553 scrap-מ-QI וכו'). ההבחנה בין-היעדים מהותית תפעולית-וחשבונאית: unrestricted משחרר-לשימוש; scrap מחויב-ל-cost-center (עלות-כשל!); return-to-vendor פותח תהליך-החזרה-לספק; sample מתעד-צריכת-בדיקה. פיצול-כמויות אפשרי (חלק-מאושר, חלק-נדחה) — קריטי ב-lots-גדולים. הבנת-ה-stock-posting חיונית — הוא-נקודת-המפגש בין-QM ל-inventory-management (MM-IM), והוא-שמבטיח שהמלאי-הפיזי משקף את-החלטות-האיכות. יועץ מנוסה מוודא שה-movement-types וה-cost-centers מוגדרים-נכון בתצורה, ומדריך את-הבודקים לפצל-כמויות נכון במקום-להכריע-הכל-לכיוון-אחד.

**הערת יועץ:** stock-posting — QI-stock → יעדים: unrestricted (321), blocked, scrap (חיוב-cost-center!), sample, return-to-vendor. מנקודת-מבט-מעשית, פיצול-כמויות אפשרי (חלק-מאושר/חלק-נדחה). יועץ מנוסה מוודא movement-types+cost-centers בתצורה, ומדריך פיצול-נכון. ההבחנה בין-יעדים = תפעולית-וחשבונאית. נקודת-מפגש QM↔MM-IM. הבנת-ה-posting חיונית — המלאי-הפיזי משקף את-החלטת-האיכות. scrap = עלות-כשל גלויה.

sections.title: Defect Recording
sections.en: 3.1.5 Defect Recording During results recording, the quality inspector finds quite a few defects, and the need to record these defects becomes evident for subsequent action by either returning the defective material to the supplier or requesting replacement (or rework, in the case of in-house-produced material). As already explained, you perform defects recording during results recording and usage decision. Once a usage decision for an inspection lot is made, you can no longer record defects. To record defects, use Transaction QF11 or use menu path Logistics  Quality Manage- ment  Quality Inspection  Defects  Record for Inspection Lot. On the initial screen that appears, enter inspection lot “10000000701” and report type “00000010”. Whenever a user enters the defects of an inspection lot, it’s mandatory for the user to choose the relevant report type. A report type denotes that when the user runs the corresponding defects reports in the system, the relevant information is available for display and analysis purposes. Several standard defect report types are available, or you can config- ure new report types to cater to any specific business processes (see more about report- ing in Chapter 18). Some of the options available for report types are in several combinations of defect types, number of defects, defect locations, causes of defect, and activities for the QM user to perform on recording the defects. Press (Enter), and the system offers three options through a popup to record the defect data at the inspection-lot level, operation level, or master inspection characteristic level. The defects recording at the inspection lot stipulates that the quality inspector found the defects in the entire inspection lot. At the operation level, it’s the specific operation or stage/phase in which the quality inspector found the defects. At the char- acteristics level, it’s the particular master inspection characteristic for which the qual- ity inspector intends to record defects. 3 Quality Inspection 126 Tips and Tricks You can also use Transaction QF21 for operation defect recording and Transaction QF31 for characteristics defect recording. Select the Inspection Lot radio button and then choose Continue, so that Figure 3.17 appears. Figure 3.17 Defects Recording To begin recording defects, first choose Defects from the top menu bar. In the popup that appears, choose the Code Group column, and press (F4). A code group and its asso- ciated codes represents the logical grouping of different defect types available in a cat- alog. A few examples of different defect code groups and types of different defects in pumps are combined together in one code group, and all types of electrical defects are combined in one defect code group. All supplier-related defects, which the company normally observes or handles, are grouped together in one defect code group, and all the production-related defects on one machine or group of machines are combined into one defect code group. The quality inspector can enter the number of defects against each defect code. However, these defective quantities aren’t directly related to or integrated with the inspection lot quantity or goods receipt quantity. For this example, enter a Code group of “QM-E” and Code of “1” (Defect Type: Out of Specification). When the user selects a defect code, the system automatically assigns a defect class to it to categorize the nature of the defect. A defect class denotes the sever- ity of the defect. Some of the defect classes are critical defect, major defect, and minor defect. These defect classes are available as standard options in the system, but you can also configure and make available new defect classes to meet your business needs. © 127 3.1 Business Processes in Quality Inspection The user can also enter a short description for each defect code in the corresponding Description column, as well as a long text. When the necessary entries are made, Figure 3.17 shows three defects along with other details such as the defect type, number of defects for each defect type, and defect class.
sections.he:
ברישום, הבודק מוצא פגמים שיש לרשום לפעולה (החזרה לספק/החלפה, או rework לחומר פנימי). רושמים פגמים ברישום וב-usage decision. לאחר ה-usage decision, אי אפשר עוד.
לרישום: Transaction QF11 או Logistics • Quality Management • Quality Inspection • Defects • Record for Inspection Lot. הזינו lot "10000000701" ו-report type "00000010". חובה לבחור report type — קובע אילו נתונים זמינים בדוחות (פרק 18). אפשרויות — צירופי defect types, מספר פגמים, מיקומים, סיבות, ופעולות.
‏Enter — שלוש אפשרויות (חלון): רמת lot (פגמים בכל ה-lot), רמת operation (שלב ספציפי), או רמת מאפיין.
**Tips and Tricks:** Transaction QF21 (operation), ‏QF31 (characteristics).
בחרו רדיו Inspection Lot, ‏Continue (Figure 3.17).
בחרו Defects (סרגל), אז Code Group, ‏F4. ‏code group + קודיו = קיבוץ לוגי של סוגי פגמים ב-catalog (פגמי משאבות יחד, פגמי חשמל יחד, פגמי ספק יחד, פגמי מכונה יחד). ניתן להזין מספר פגמים לכל קוד (לא משולב ישירות עם כמות ה-lot/GR).
בדוגמה, ‏Code group "QM-E", ‏Code "1" (Out of Specification). בבחירת קוד, המערכת מקצה אוטומטית defect class (חומרת הפגם — critical/major/minor; ניתן להגדיר חדשים). ניתן תיאור קצר ו-long text. Figure 3.17 — שלושה פגמים עם type, מספר, ו-defect class.

במהלך-ה-results-recording, בודק-האיכות מוצא לעתים פגמים-רבים, והצורך לתעדם מתבהר — לפעולת-המשך: החזרת-החומר-הפגום לספק, בקשת-החלפה, או-rework (בחומר-מיוצר-פנימית). את-תיעוד-הפגמים מבצעים במהלך-ה-results-recording וה-usage-decision; לאחר-שהתקבלה usage-decision ל-inspection-lot, לא-ניתן-עוד לתעד-פגמים. לתיעוד-פגמים משתמשים ב-Transaction-QF11 או-menu-path. עבור-היועץ, defect-recording הוא-גשר בין-הבדיקה לעולם-הטיפול-בכשלים: הפגם מתועד עם-defect-code מקטלוג-type-9 (מובנה, לא-טקסט-חופשי), defect-class (critical/major/minor), ומיקום — ומכאן ניתן-להסלים ל-quality-notification (QM01) לטיפול-מלא (8D, root-cause). ההבחנה בין-רמות-התיעוד מהותית: defect ברמת-characteristic (איזה-מאפיין-נכשל), ברמת-operation, או-ברמת-lot. חלון-הזמן קשיח — עד-ה-UD בלבד (אחריו-הבדיקה-סגורה) — ולכן-יש-לתעד מיד-עם-הגילוי. ה-defect-codes המובנים מזינים ניתוח-Pareto של-כשלים (אילו-פגמים-חוזרים, מאילו-ספקים). הבנת-defect-recording חיונית — הוא-שממיר ממצא-שלילי לנתון-מובנה בר-פעולה, ומזין את-מעגל-ה-quality-improvement. יועץ מנוסה מגדיר activation של-defect-recording אוטומטי בדחיית-מאפיין (בחריגת-סבולת), כך-שאף-כשל לא-נעלם ללא-תיעוד.

**הערת יועץ:** defect-recording (QF11; גם-QF01) — פגם מובנה: defect-code (catalog-9) + class (critical/major/minor). מנקודת-מבט-מעשית, חלון-קשיח: עד-ה-UD בלבד. יועץ מנוסה מפעיל auto-defect בדחיית-מאפיין + הסלמה ל-quality-notification (QM01) לטיפול-8D. ההבחנה defect (ממצא-מובנה) מול-notification (תהליך-טיפול). מזין ניתוח-Pareto (פגמים-חוזרים/ספקים). הבנת-ה-recording חיונית — ממיר-כשל לנתון-בר-פעולה. גשר ל-quality-improvement.

sections.title: Inspection Report
sections.en: 3.1.6 Inspection Report The inspection report displays the inspection results and comments of every charac- teristic on the screen as a print preview or in the form of a printout. This means it can also be used to provide an overview of the inspection carried out, or it can be referred to as a basis for the usage decision. It can also serve as an attachment to a quality noti- fication to the supplier or to internal departments to describe in detail the deviations of individual characteristics according to type and scope, in the case of defects. To display the inspection report, use Transaction QGA3 or follow menu path Quality Management  Quality Inspection  Inspection Result  Print. The system displays the Results Print selection screen. If you know the inspection lot number, you can enter it directly. Otherwise, the selection allows you to set limits through known parameters such as material number, supplier, and date, among others. Figure 3.18 shows an exam- ple of a print preview (selective) of an inspection report for inspection lot 10000000701 for material RM17. Figure 3.18 Inspection Report 3 Quality Inspection 128
sections.he:
ה-inspection report מציג את תוצאות והערות כל מאפיין (preview או הדפסה) — לסקירה כללית, כבסיס ל-usage decision, או כצירוף ל-notification לספק/מחלקות לתיאור הסטיות.
להצגה: Transaction QGA3 או Quality Management • Quality Inspection • Inspection Result • Print. במסך Results Print, הזינו מספר lot ישירות, או הגבילו (חומר, ספק, תאריך). Figure 3.18 — preview של דוח ל-lot 10000000701, חומר RM17.

ה-inspection-report מציג את-תוצאות-הבדיקה וההערות של-כל-מאפיין על-המסך כ-print-preview או-כפלט-מודפס. הוא-משמש לסקירת-הבדיקה שבוצעה, כבסיס ל-usage-decision, וכן-כנספח ל-quality-notification לספק או-למחלקות-פנימיות — לתיאור-מפורט של-סטיות מאפיינים-בודדים לפי-סוג-והיקף במקרה-של-פגמים. עבור-היועץ, ה-inspection-report הוא-מסמך-התקשורת של-הבדיקה: בעוד-הנתונים חיים-במערכת (results, defects), ה-report מרכז-אותם למסמך-קריא המשמש שלושה-קהלים — הבודק (סקירה-לפני-UD), הספק (נספח-לתלונה: הנה-בדיוק-מה-חרג), והרגולטור/לקוח (הוכחת-בדיקה). ההבחנה בין-ה-inspection-report (תיעוד-תוצאות פנימי/תפעולי) ל-quality-certificate (תעודת-איכות רשמית ללקוח, QC01) מהותית: הראשון-מפורט-וגולמי, השני-מעוצב-ומחייב. ה-report נשלף לפי-lot וכולל כל-מאפיין עם-ערכיו והערכתו. הבנת-ה-inspection-report חיונית — הוא-שמתרגם נתוני-בדיקה למסמך-פעולה: בסיס-להחלטה, ראיה-לתלונת-ספק, ותיעוד-לביקורת. יועץ מנוסה מטמיע את-שליפת-ה-report בשגרת-ה-UD (סקירה-לפני-החלטה) ומצרפו אוטומטית ל-notifications לספקים, לחיזוק-עמדת-החברה בתלונות.

**הערת יועץ:** inspection-report — תוצאות+הערות כל-מאפיין (preview/הדפסה). מנקודת-מבט-מעשית, שלושה-קהלים: בודק (בסיס-UD), ספק (נספח-לתלונה), רגולטור (הוכחת-בדיקה). יועץ מנוסה משלב בשגרת-UD + מצרף ל-notifications. ההבחנה report (פנימי, מפורט) מול-quality-certificate (QC01, רשמי-ללקוח). הבנת-ה-report חיונית — מתרגם-נתונים למסמך-פעולה. ראיה בתלונות-ספק.

sections.title: Optimization Features of Inspection Planning and Quality
sections.en: 3.2 Optimization Features of Inspection Planning and Quality Inspection Just as we covered the standard QM business processes in the specific sequence in which they occur, this section covers optimization and other productivity enhance- ment options available in the following areas:  Master data  Inspection lot  Digital signature  Results recording  Usage decision  Engineering Workbench
sections.he:
כפי שכיסינו את התהליכים התקניים ברצף, סעיף זה מכסה מיטוב ושיפור פרודוקטיביות:
• נתוני אב (Master data)
• Inspection lot
• חתימה דיגיטלית (Digital signature)
• רישום תוצאות (Results recording)
• Usage decision
• Engineering Workbench

כפי-שכיסינו את-תהליכי-ה-QM הסטנדרטיים ברצף-התרחשותם, סעיף-זה מכסה אפשרויות-אופטימיזציה ושיפור-פרודוקטיביות בתחומים: master-data, inspection-lot, digital-signature, results-recording, usage-decision, ו-Engineering-Workbench. עבור-היועץ, סעיף-זה הוא-'רמה-שנייה' של-יישום-QM: לאחר-שהתהליכים הבסיסיים (3.1) רצים-ויציבים, מגיע-שלב-הייעול — צמצום-הקלדות, אוטומציה של-החלטות-שגרתיות, ובקרות-מתקדמות. ההבחנה בין-שלב-ההטמעה (להריץ-את-הבסיס) לשלב-האופטימיזציה (לייעל-את-הרץ) מהותית למתודולוגיית-יישום: אין-לאופטימיזציה מקום לפני-שהבסיס-יציב — אוטומציה של-תהליך-שבור רק-משכפלת-שבירות. ששת-התחומים מכסים את-כל-מחזור-הבדיקה: תחזוקת-אב המונית (QS27-replace, Engineering-Workbench), תיקוני-lot (QAC1/QAC2/QAC3), חתימות-דיגיטליות (בקרה-רגולטורית), העתקת-תוצאות (חיסכון-בהקלדה), ו-UD-קולקטיבי/אוטומטי (חיסכון-בהחלטות). הבנת-מפת-האופטימיזציות חיונית — היא-שמאפשרת ליועץ להציע ללקוח-בשל שיפורי-פרודוקטיביות מדורגים. יועץ מנוסה חוזר-ללקוח כ-3-6 חודשים אחרי-go-live ומיישם את-האופטימיזציות-הללו על-בסיס-נתוני-שימוש אמיתיים (אילו-בדיקות-חוזרות, איפה-צוואר-הבקבוק).

**הערת יועץ:** optimization-features — רמה-שנייה: אחרי-שהבסיס-יציב. מנקודת-מבט-מעשית, שישה-תחומים: master-data (QS27), lot (QAC1), digital-signature, results-copy, UD קולקטיבי/אוטומטי, Engineering-Workbench. יועץ מנוסה חוזר 3-6 חודשים אחרי-go-live ומיישם לפי-נתוני-שימוש. ⚠️ אוטומציה על-תהליך-שבור משכפלת-שבירות. ההבחנה הטמעה (בסיס) מול-אופטימיזציה (ייעול). הבנת-המפה חיונית — שיפורים-מדורגים ללקוח-בשל.

sections.title: Master Data
sections.en: 3.2.1 Master Data Let’s begin with master data. We started with the fundamentals in Chapter 2; the fol- lowing information represents specific optimization. Replace Inspection Characteristic or Inspection Method To replace characteristics, master inspection characteristics, or inspection plans, use Transaction QS27 or follow menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Quality Plan- ning  Basic Data  Inspection Characteristic  Replace. Figure 3.19 shows the initial screen where you enter the original or existing characteristic number and its plant. Figure 3.19 Master Inspection Characteristic and Inspection Method Replacement © 129 3.2 Optimization Features of Inspection Planning and Quality Inspection In the Replacement Master Inspection Characteristic with Inspection Method area, you can enter only the new characteristic or the new characteristic and its associated inspection method. Choose Continue (not shown, but located on the bottom right hand side of the screen) and the screen in Figure 3.20 appears. Here, you can choose to replace some or all of the characteristics listed online or as a batch input (background job). Choose Start Replacement located on the bottom-right side of the screen (not shown) to start the replacement process. Figure 3.20 Replace Master Inspection Characteristic Warning You need to engage an ABAP resource to activate user exit QPAA0004 to be able to use this replace characteristic functionality. However, implementing this user exit in isola- tion leads to other problems, such as not being able to incorporate inspection charac- teristics in an inspection plan. We suggest that while implementing this user exit, you also implement dependent and subsequent user exits or function modules that your ABAP resource should be able to manage. Where-Used List At any time, you can leverage the where-used list to find the inspection plan in which a specific characteristic is used. For this, use Transaction QS26 or follow menu path Logis- tics  Quality Management  Quality Planning  Basic Data  Inspection Characteristic  Where-Used List. List Inspection Characteristic You can view a complete list of inspection characteristics and all their settings in the form of a list or report. To view this characteristic list, use Transaction QS28 or follow menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Quality Planning  Basic Data  Inspection Characteristic  List. 3 Quality Inspection 130 Delete Task List (Inspection Plan) To delete obsolete or wrongly created inspection plans, use Transaction CA98. Be sure to choose Task List Type Q, which is specific to inspection plans. Note Although we cover only limited change, replace, delete, or report options for quality planning master data, we suggest that you explore these options available for every QM master data element. The relevant options are available in the same menu paths that you use to create or change any QM master data, such as inspection plan, inspec- tion method, work center, class characteristic, or inspection characteristic.

sections.title: Inspection Lot
sections.en: 3.2.2 Inspection Lot Let’s now cover the inspection lot and its various business scenarios. Correct Errors To correct quantity-related errors of an inspection lot, use Transaction QAC1 or follow menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Quality Inspection  Inspection Lot  Pro- cessing  Lot Quantity  Correct Errors. You can use this option to correct or change both stock-based and non-stock-based inspection lots. The stock-based quantity update is especially helpful when the system automatically creates an inspection lot on receipt of goods for a purchase or process order and accordingly suggests an inspection lot quantity, which you can change, if needed. Stock Transfer Let’s say that you receive a quality stock of material, and on inspection, you conclude that you need to keep it in a separate storage location or transfer it to a different plant. In this case, you use the stock transfer option. When you use this option, the stock that’s transferred to a different plant or storage location still remains in quality inspec- tion until you record results, make a usage decision, and perform stock posting. To transfer stock plant-to-plant or store-to-store for an inspection lot, use Transaction QAC2 or follow menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Quality Inspection  Inspec- tion Lot  Processing  Lot Quantity  Stock Transfer. On the initial screen that appears, enter the stock of which you want to transfer-post in the inspection lot, and press (Enter). The Transfer Posting Insp. Lot Stock area shows the current location of the quality stock. You can enter a different plant for stock for plant-to-plant stock transfer, or simply keep the same plant (as in this example) and change the storage location of inspection stock from 0001 to 0002 (see the St.Loc.ILotStock field) in the Stock Transfer Based On area. © 131 3.2 Optimization Features of Inspection Planning and Quality Inspection Cancel Sample Calculation On inspection lot creation (manual or automatic), the system assigns an inspection plan or material specification and calculates a sample size. If you realize that you or the system incorporated an incorrect or obsolete inspection plan and therefore calculated a wrong sample size, you can cancel the sample calculation. Canceling the sample cal- culation also enables you to reassign a new or different inspection plan and accord- ingly recalculate the sample size. In other words, you have to cancel the sample calculation before the system allows you to reassign an inspection plan and then recal- culate the sample size. To cancel a sample calculation, use Transaction QAC3 or follow menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Quality Inspection  Inspection Lot  Processing  Cancel Sample Calculation. On the initial screen that appears, enter the inspection lot of the sample you want to cancel, press (Enter), and then simply save. Tips and Tricks To cancel, you can also use Transaction QA02 (Change Inspection Lot); on the initial screen, enter the inspection lot number, and choose Cancel Sample. Inspection Lots with Outstanding Quantities It’s of interest to the quality inspector to have a complete list of inspection lots for which a usage decision may or may not be made, but for which stock posting is still pending or outstanding. To access inspection lots with outstanding quantities and be able to make usage decisions on the same screen, use Transaction QVM2 or follow menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Quality Inspection  Worklist  Inspection Lot Completion  Inspection Lot with Stock. In Figure 3.21, notice that the system sta- tuses of a few inspection lots stipulate that the usage decision has already been made, but its stock posting remains. Figure 3.21 Outstanding Inspection Quantities 3 Quality Inspection 132 Tips and Tricks Transaction QVM1 is for inspection lots with inspection completion, whereas Transac- tion QVM3 is for inspection lots without a usage decision. Cancel Inspection Lot If you or the system has created an inspection lot that you no longer want to inspect or use, you’ll want to cancel it. This option is helpful when you’ve mistakenly activated an inspection type against which the system created an inspection lot. To cancel, first go to Transaction QA02 (Change Inspection Lot), then navigate to Inspection Lot  Func- tions  Cancel Lot. The system sets the status of the inspection lot to LTCA. Similarly, if you want to reset an inspection lot cancellation, navigate to Inspection Lot  Functions  Reset Cancellation. Block Inspection Lot To temporarily block an inspection lot so that you can perform additional tests, or to prevent the quality inspector from making its usage decision or stock posting, you can block the inspection lot. To do so, first go to Transaction QA02 (Change Inspection Lot), and then navigate to Inspection Lot  Functions  Block Lot. The system sets the status of the inspection lot to LKD. Similarly, to unblock an inspection lot, navigate to Inspection Lot  Functions  Unblock Lot.

sections.title: Digital Signature
sections.en: 3.2.3 Digital Signature The digital signature functionality reduces the number of printed documents that need to be signed within an organization. You can define and then assign digital signatures in an SAP system during various transaction processes, such as recording results and mak- ing usage decisions in QM, changing the status of a document in Document Manage- ment System (DMS), or completing a process instructions sheet in production planning (PP). Digital signatures can be internal, such as an SAP system user’s password, or even use external devices, such as fingerprint readers or card slides. Digital signatures can confirm important business decisions in QM, such as according approval to the quality inspection lot, validating the correctness of shift reports in plant maintenance (PM), or simply confirming the values of process parameters in production planning for process industries (PP-PI). They do all of this electronically, saving significant time and effort, eventually bringing about improvements in business processes and saving money. The following are some of the areas in QM in which you can integrate digital signatures with relevant business processes:  Inspection lot approval  Results recording © 133 3.2 Optimization Features of Inspection Planning and Quality Inspection  Usage decisions  Physical-sample drawing  Header or item level of QM notification Note Throughout this book, we’ve highlighted the business processes in which you can inte- grate digital signatures. It’s important to highlight that the digital signature configuration that you undertake here for QM is directly assigned at the material level (we’ll show this later). Hence, from the implementation consideration point of view, consider some or all of the preceding combinations of business processes in which you’ll use the same digital signature strategy. For example, will a material require a digital signature for approval of only the inspection lot, or will it also need a digital signature at the time of results recording? If the latter, then a combination of a single QM material authorization group that encom- passes both the business processes (inspection lot approval and results recording) will suffice. If the business process requires a digital signature on physical sample with- drawal, then configuring a separate QM material authorization group to cater to this business need and then assigning it to the material master serves the needed purpose. Note If you further integrate digital signature functionality with SAP Business Workflow, then the person responsible for digitally signing a particular SAP system object auto- matically receives the relevant information via the SAP system inbox. This section begins by covering the important steps you need to take to configure dig- ital signatures. Then, we’ll run the entire end-to-end business process in QM to show how digital signatures work. Note The concepts and flows that we’ll cover for digital signatures in QM are equally appli- cable to all the other areas of SAP S/4HANA that digital signatures apply to. Configuration Basics Following are the six important steps in configuring a digital signature: 1. Define authorization groups. 2. Define individual signatures. 3. Define a signature strategy. 3 Quality Inspection 134 4. Create authorization groups for QM master data. 5. Configure the material authorization group, inspection lot approval, digital signa- ture. 6. Create a signature method. Tips and Tricks Although this section focuses on digital signatures in QM, the general menu path for digital signatures is SAP IMG  Cross-Application Components  General Application Functions  Digital Signature. We’ll now discuss each of the steps for configuration in the following sections. Define Authorization Groups An authorization group is used to limit the authorization of a transaction or group of transactions to a specific user or group of users performing the same role. Once config- ured, this authorization group can be controlled through authorization object C_SIGN_ BGR. You need to coordinate with your SAP NetWeaver (Basis) team members to get the right authorization group assigned to the right user. To create an authorization group, follow SAP system menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  Environment  Central Functions  Signature Strategy  Define Authoriza- tion Groups. Here, you can see the initial screen for the creation of an authorization group for digital signatures (see Figure 3.22). Choose the New Entries button (not shown) to create a new authorization group, UD, and enter a description (“Digital Signa- ture for UD”, in this example). Save the authorization group. Figure 3.22 Creating New Authorization Group Define Individual Signatures An individual signature is a unique identification in the SAP system to which a user is assigned. To create a new individual signature, follow menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  Environment  Central Functions  Signature Strategy  Define Individual Signatures. In the screen that appears (see Figure 3.23), choose New Entries, and define two individual signatures—UD01 and UD02—with descriptions. © 135 3.2 Optimization Features of Inspection Planning and Quality Inspection Figure 3.23 Two Individual Signatures Both individual signatures are assigned to the same authorization group—UD—as shown in Figure 3.23. Save the entries. Define a Signature Strategy A signature strategy is the combination of different individual signatures that are assigned to an authorization group. A signature strategy also defines the sequence and flow of individual signatures and maintains the predecessor-successor relationships. The signature strategy is used to control the level to which the document can be con- sidered released. A Released status denotes that the digital signature process is com- plete in every respect. Tips and Tricks If you don’t have a business need to configure and define a digital signature strategy, then you can skip all the steps that we’ve covered in this section and move on to the following sections. These digital signature settings are specific only to QM objects, such as inspection lot approval, results recording, and usage decision. To create a signature strategy, follow menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  Envi- ronment  Central Functions  Signature Strategy  Define Signature Strategy (see Figure 3.24). Figure 3.24 Signature Strategy 3 Quality Inspection 136 Before we show you how to create a new signature strategy, we need to explain some of the columns in Figure 3.24 and their functions. The third column, Signature Method, stipulates how the SAP system verifies a signature. The three possible options are as fol- lows:  System signature with authorization, using an SAP system username and password  User signature with external security product with verification  User signature with external security product without verification The Comment column enables a user to enter comments when they execute the digital signature. In the Remark column, users can enter a short text before signing. The Doc- ument column is an option to allow or disallow viewing of a document. The Verifica- tion column, with the checkbox, verifies the sequence of the digital signature, known as the signature strategy, before the system marks the document as complete. Choose the newly created SigStrat UD in Figure 3.24, and then choose Assign individual signatures. Then, in Figure 3.25, maintain the entries of two individual signatures pre- viously created in Figure 3.23. To define a new signature strategy, choose New Entries at the top of the screen shown in Figure 3.24. Figure 3.25 Assigning Individual Signatures to a Signature Strategy In the second screen of the same figure, define the signature strategy UD with the description “Usage Decision Auth. Group”. Then, select System Signature and Password to be the signature option, and make the Displ. Comment box, Display Remark box, and Disp. Document required entries. Finally, select the Verify checkbox to require verifica- tion of the signature strategy. Figure 3.26 shows the summary of all the settings made. Next, select the signature strategy UD in the SigStrat field, and double-click the Assign individual signatures folder. Choose New Entries (see Figure 3.26), and add the previ- ously created individual signatures UD01 and UD02 to the signature strategy UD. Save and then choose Back to return to the overview screen. © 137 3.2 Optimization Features of Inspection Planning and Quality Inspection Figure 3.26 Signature Sequence of a Signature Strategy Figure 3.24, shown earlier, displays the signature strategy overview screen, but now with a new entry, UD. Select the newly created signature strategy, UD, and choose the Signatures button on the right side. Figure 3.27 shows the Release States of Signature St... screen, in which individual signa- ture UD01 must be signed before individual signature UD02. In other words, UD01 is the predecessor (denoted as the predecessor in the UD01 column), and UD02 is the suc- cessor. Choose Continue to go to the screen shown previously in Figure 3.26. Figure 3.27 Individual Signature for Signature Strategy Select the signature strategy UD in Figure 3.26, and choose Release from the popup that appears. Select the checkbox that denotes the release status of the document, as well as the completion of the signature strategy. A completion strategy means that the required sequence of digital signatures is ensured. For this example, select the checkbox 3 Quality Inspection 138 in the second row, in which both individual signatures, UD01 and UD02, must be marked for the signature strategy to declare it as complete. Choose Continue and save. The configuration needed to enable the SAP system digital signature is complete. However, for the digital signature to work in the desired busi- ness process, you need to assign the newly created signature strategy UD to the rele- vant material master, which we’ll cover in the next section. Create Authorization Groups for Quality Management Master Data To create an authorization group for QM master data, follow menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  Environment  Central Functions  Authorization Management  Define Authorization Groups and Digital Signature. Choose the first option Authorization Group for QM Master Data. Choose New Entries, define AuthGroup as UD000001, enter a Short Text description, and save (see Figure 3.28). Figure 3.28 Authorization Group Configure the Material Authorization Group, Inspection Lot Approval, and Digital Signature In Figure 3.29, choose New Entries to bring up the option to make detailed settings for digital signature for some or all of the four QM objects: inspection lot approval, results recording, usage decision, and physical sample drawing. Let’s review the three available digital signature options for each of the four QM objects:  Not Required There will be no need to digitally sign the QM object.  Required for Making Digital Signature of the Object This option provides for a single digital signature, with no provision to incorporate a signature strategy (multiple digital signatures).  Required for “New” Digital Signature This option is used to select either a synchronous signature process (digitally sign- ing the QM object only in the logical and sequential order) or an asynchronous sig- nature process with and without a changeable signatory. Finally, in the last field, © 139 3.2 Optimization Features of Inspection Planning and Quality Inspection which is Sig. (Signature) Strategy, you can enter the signature strategy that you’ve already created in the previous steps in this chapter. In the case of synchronous sig- nature selection, all users have to digitally sign the QM object one after the other until the entire signature process is complete. In the case of the asynchronous option, different users can digitally sign the QM object at different times. Figure 3.29 QM Material Authorization In this example, choose the Required for “New” Digital Signature option for results recording. As soon as you do this, the system brings up the option to select the asyn- chronous signature process with changeable history for signature type. Finally, enter the signature strategy UD that you created previously. In addition, for the usage decision, choose option 1, which requires a digital signature at the time of making a usage decision. Create a Signature Method To create a signature method for QM master data, follow menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  Environment  Central Functions  Authorization Management  Define Authorization Groups and Digital Signature  Specify Signature Method for Approval Using Simple Signature (see Figure 3.30). Here, first check whether the Object is already 3 Quality Inspection 140 available on the screen. If it’s available, then simply select the Signature Method as a System Signature with an SAP username and password. If the signature object type isn’t available, then you can choose New Entries and select the relevant object from the large number of objects available for the signature method. With this, we conclude the necessary digital signature configuration and proceed to assigning the configured QM material authorization group in the material master. Figure 3.30 Signature Method for Simple Signature Digital Signature in Quality Management Business Processes In this section, we’ll assign the configuration that we undertook for the digital signa- ture. It’s only a single step of assigning the configured QM material authorization group to the relevant material. Next, we create a manual inspection lot, record results to see if the digital signature is correctly configured and available, and finally record a usage decision to see if the digital signature pops up again (refer to the settings we made in Figure 3.29). Assigning the Quality Management Material Authorization Group in the Material Master To assign the QM authorization group UD0001, use Transaction MM02, enter material number “RM17” in the Material field, and select the Quality management view. On the Organizational Levels prompt (not shown), enter plant “1710”, and then press (Enter). © 141 3.2 Optimization Features of Inspection Planning and Quality Inspection The screen in Figure 3.31 appears. In the QMatAu field, choose the just configured option UD0001 from the dropdown menu shown on the right side of the screen, and save the settings. Figure 3.31 Assignment of QM Material Authorization in the Material Master Tips and Tricks You can also use the QM Material Auth.. field in Figure 3.31 to control authorization of who is allowed to perform necessary business functions. For example, you have one group of quality inspectors who are responsible for inspecting raw and packaging materials. You have another group of quality inspectors who inspect semifinished and finished goods. To restrict relevant inspectors to performing QM tasks such as results recording and usage decisions that are specific to their material type (e.g., raw materi- als or finished goods), you can create two different authorization groups and assign them in the QM Material Auth. field of the relevant material masters. Then, also assign these objects to the individual inspectors’ user profiles to restrict their authorizations and working rights. We suggest that you engage a Basis/SAP NetWeaver consultant to restrict authoriza- tions. Inspection Lot Creation To create a new manual inspection lot, use Transaction QA01; on the initial screen, enter Material “RM17”, Plant “1710”, and Inspection Type “89” (for manual inspection). 3 Quality Inspection 142 On the inspection lot creation screen, enter the inspection lot quantity as “10”, and save the inspection lot. The system creates an inspection lot and assigns an internal inspec- tion lot number, which in this example is 10000000704. Digital Signature in Results Recording To record results, use Transaction QE01, and enter the same inspection lot number, “10000000704”, and its operation, “0010”. Figure 3.32 shows that after entering the results of inspection lot 10000000704, the system brings up the popup window for you to digitally sign. Here, enter the short text, the signatory, and the SAP system password. On successful completion of the digital signature, the system displays an information message at the bottom of the screen. Figure 3.32 Digital Signature Popup during Results Recording Digital Signature in Usage Decision On successful completion of results recording and digitally signing the results, use Transaction QA11 to record the usage decision of the same inspection lot, 10000000704. As soon as you enter the usage decision code and save, the system prompts you to enter the SAP system password. This process is exactly the same as that covered in the previous section. Digital Signature Logs The SAP system provides a comprehensive log that you can view to ensure complete visibility of all the activities undertaken for digital signatures. © 143 3.2 Optimization Features of Inspection Planning and Quality Inspection Note This digital signature log is also available in all the applications and areas in which dig- ital signatures are used, which includes PM, QM, engineering change management, and PP-PI. To access the digital signature logs, use Transaction DSAL or follow menu path Quality Management  Quality Inspection  Info System  Digital Signature  Logs. This takes you to the initial screen to enter relevant parameters. In the Applic. (application) field, choose LOT (Inspection Lot); in the lower half of the screen, under the Inspection Lot tab, enter the inspection lot as “10000000704”. Press (F8) or choose Execute. The screen in Figure 3.33 provides a comprehensive log of digi- tal signatures for inspection lot 10000000704. Figure 3.33 Digital Signature Log The bottom half of the screen provides details about who executed the digital signa- tures and when. It also provides details of the individual signatures (UD01 and UD02), as well the signature strategy UD. Further, the system also maintains a complete log of all attempts, whether successful or not, to digitally sign an object. Notice that in the upper half of the same figure, there are a few red dots on the left side, which denotes an unsuccessful attempt to digitally sign inspection lot 10000000703. Tips and Tricks To access the digital signature worklist, use Transaction QEDS or follow menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Quality Inspection  Worklist  Signature Process. 3 Quality Inspection 144
sections.he:
החתימה הדיגיטלית מפחיתה מסמכים מודפסים לחתימה. מקצים אותה בתהליכים — רישום תוצאות, ‏usage decision ב-QM, שינוי סטטוס ב-DMS, או השלמת PI sheet ב-PP. יכולה להיות פנימית (סיסמת משתמש) או חיצונית (קורא טביעת-אצבע, כרטיס). מאשרת החלטות (אישור lot, אימות shift reports ב-PM, אישור פרמטרים ב-PP-PI) — אלקטרונית.
אזורים ב-QM לשילוב:
• אישור inspection lot
• רישום תוצאות
• usage decisions
• משיכת דגימה פיזית
• רמת כותרת/פריט של notification
**הערה:** התצורה כאן מוקצית ברמת החומר. שקלו צירופי תהליכים. למשל, אם חומר דורש חתימה לאישור ה-lot וגם לרישום — group הרשאות חומר QM יחיד מספיק. למשיכת דגימה — group נפרד.
**הערה:** בשילוב עם SAP Business Workflow, האחראי מקבל מידע ב-inbox.

**יסודות התצורה:** שישה צעדים:
1. Define authorization groups.
2. Define individual signatures.
3. Define a signature strategy.
4. Create authorization groups for QM master data.
5. Configure material authorization group, inspection lot approval, digital signature.
6. Create a signature method.
**Tips and Tricks:** הנתיב הכללי — SAP IMG • Cross-Application Components • General Application Functions • Digital Signature.

**Define Authorization Groups:** מגביל הרשאת טרנזקציה למשתמש/קבוצה. נשלט ב-authorization object C_SIGN_BGR (תאמו עם Basis). ל-SAP IMG • Quality Management • Environment • Central Functions • Signature Strategy • Define Authorization Groups (Figure 3.22). ‏New Entries, צרו group UD ותיאור. שמרו.

**Define Individual Signatures:** זיהוי ייחודי שאליו מוקצה משתמש. ל-... • Define Individual Signatures (Figure 3.23). ‏New Entries — UD01 ו-UD02, שניהם ל-group UD. שמרו.

**Define a Signature Strategy:** צירוף individual signatures המוקצה ל-group; מגדיר רצף ויחסי קודם-עוקב; שולט ברמת השחרור (Released = התהליך הושלם). ל-... • Define Signature Strategy (Figure 3.24). טורים: ‏Signature Method (כיצד המערכת מאמתת — System signature with authorization [שם/סיסמה]; ‏User signature עם external security product, עם/בלי אימות); ‏Comment/Remark (הערות); ‏Document (הצגה); ‏Verification (אימות הרצף).
בחרו SigStrat UD ו-Assign individual signatures (Figure 3.25) — תחזקו UD01, ‏UD02. ל-strategy חדש, ‏New Entries (Figure 3.24): הגדירו UD עם תיאור "Usage Decision Auth. Group", בחרו System Signature and Password, וסמנו Displ. Comment, ‏Display Remark, ‏Disp. Document, ו-Verify (Figure 3.26). בחרו SigStrat UD ו-Assign individual signatures, ‏New Entries — UD01, ‏UD02. שמרו, ‏Back.
בחרו UD ו-Signatures (Figure 3.27 — Release States): ‏UD01 חייב להיחתם לפני UD02 (UD01 קודם, ‏UD02 עוקב). ‏Continue (Figure 3.26). בחרו UD ו-Release, סמנו את הסטטוס וההשלמה. בדוגמה, השורה השנייה — שניהם (UD01, ‏UD02) חובה. ‏Continue, שמרו.

**Create Authorization Groups for QM Master Data:** ל-SAP IMG • Quality Management • Environment • Central Functions • Authorization Management • Define Authorization Groups and Digital Signature. בחרו Authorization Group for QM Master Data, ‏New Entries — AuthGroup UD000001 ותיאור (Figure 3.28). שמרו.

**Configure Material Authorization Group, Inspection Lot Approval, Digital Signature:** ב-Figure 3.29, ‏New Entries להגדרות לארבעת אובייקטי QM (אישור lot, רישום, usage decision, משיכת דגימה). שלוש אפשרויות לכל אובייקט:
• **Not Required:** ללא חתימה.
• **Required for Making Digital Signature:** חתימה יחידה (ללא strategy).
• **Required for "New" Digital Signature:** סינכרוני (לפי הרצף) או א-סינכרוני (עם/בלי signatory ניתן-לשינוי). בשדה Sig. Strategy הזינו את ה-strategy. בסינכרוני, כל המשתמשים חותמים בזה אחר זה; בא-סינכרוני — בזמנים שונים.
בדוגמה, ‏Required for "New" Digital Signature לרישום, וא-סינכרוני עם changeable history, ‏strategy UD. ל-usage decision, אפשרות 1 (חתימה בעת ההחלטה).

**Create a Signature Method:** ל-... • Define Authorization Groups and Digital Signature • Specify Signature Method for Approval Using Simple Signature (Figure 3.30). אם ה-Object זמין — בחרו System Signature (שם/סיסמה); אחרת New Entries.

**חתימה דיגיטלית בתהליכים:** ‏(הקצאת ה-group, יצירת lot, רישום, החלטה.)
**הקצאת group באב החומר:** Transaction MM02, חומר "RM17", תצוגת Quality management, ‏plant "1710". בשדה QMatAu בחרו UD0001, שמרו (Figure 3.31).
**Tips and Tricks:** ‏QM Material Auth. שולט גם במי מורשה. למשל, group אחד לבודקי גלם/אריזה, אחר לחצי-גמורים/גמורים — שני groups והקצאה לפרופילי המשתמשים (ערבו Basis).
**יצירת lot:** Transaction QA01 — חומר "RM17", ‏plant "1710", ‏Inspection Type "89" (ידני). כמות "10", שמרו (lot 10000000704).
**חתימה ברישום:** Transaction QE01 — lot "10000000704", פעולה "0010". לאחר הזנת התוצאות, חלון לחתימה (Figure 3.32) — טקסט קצר, signatory, סיסמה.
**חתימה ב-usage decision:** Transaction QA11 — lot 10000000704. בהזנת הקוד ושמירה, המערכת מבקשת סיסמה.
**יומני חתימה:** ל-Transaction DSAL או Quality Management • Quality Inspection • Info System • Digital Signature • Logs. בשדה Applic. בחרו LOT, הזינו lot "10000000704", ‏F8 (Figure 3.33) — יומן מקיף (מי/מתי, UD01/UD02, ‏strategy UD, וכל הניסיונות; נקודות אדומות = ניסיון כושל ל-lot 10000000703).
**Tips and Tricks:** ל-worklist — Transaction QEDS או ... • Worklist • Signature Process.

**הערת יועץ:** digital-signature — מפחית-נייר, בקרה רגולטורית (21-CFR-Part-11!). מנקודת-מבט-מעשית, נקודות-חתימה: results, UD, DMS-status, PI-sheet (PP). חתימה = סיסמת-משתמש-SAP או-התקן-חיצוני. יועץ מנוסה מטמיע ב-pharma/מזון: signature-strategy (מי-חותם, כמה-חתימות), לוג-מלא. ההבחנה חתימה-בודדת מול-אסטרטגיה-מרובת-חותמים. הבנת-ה-signature חיונית — תאימות-רגולטורית + audit-trail. שקיפות-ובקרה בתהליכים-קריטיים.

sections.title: Results Recording
sections.en: 3.2.4 Results Recording Let’s now cover results recording and its various business scenarios—specifically, copying inspection results of one inspection lot to another as well as copying inspec- tion results into batch classification. Copy Inspection Results of an Inspection Lot The SAP S/4HANA system provides an option to copy inspection results of an inspec- tion lot into subsequent inspection lots, based on the configuration and master data settings, which we’ll cover in the following sections. The configuration settings are inspection-type-specific for a particular plant in which available copy controls are at the inspection-lot-creation level and at the results-recording level. You can copy the inspection results during inspection lot creation or results recording. While this functionality is more commonly used in recurring inspections (inspection type 09), you can also use this functionality for any other inspection type/plant combi- nation, as this example shows. Configuration Settings To set up the necessary configuration settings for copying inspection results, follow menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  Quality Inspection  Results Recording  Make Settings for Copy of Inspection Results. Review Figure 3.34 and Figure 3.35 together: these are part of the same screen, in which you copy inspection results set- tings. This example shows configuration settings of inspection type 89 (manual inspec- tion) for plant 1710. Figure 3.34 Copy Inspection Results: Screen 1 Table 3.3 explains the fields and settings of Figure 3.34 and Figure 3.35. © 145 3.2 Optimization Features of Inspection Planning and Quality Inspection Figure 3.35 Copy Inspection Results: Screen 2 Field Column Details Inspection Type Inspection type to which copy inspection results are applicable. Plant Plant of the inspection type for which the copy inspection results apply. Control in Insp. Lot (inspection lot) Option to control the mode of data transfer or data copy. The available options are as follows:  No data transfer at the inspection-lot-creation level  Automatic data transfer on sample calculation  Manual and automatic data transfer In the case of manual data transfer, the system prompts you to enter the inspection lot number of the data that you want to copy or transfer (see Figure 3.34). Note: The source and target master inspection characteristics must both be available and consistent to ensure successful data transfer. Control in RR (results recording) Option to control the mode of data transfer or data copy. The available options are the same that are available for inspection lot creation. Close This checkbox, if selected, closes the master inspection charac- teristics on successful data transfer. Table 3.3 Copy Inspection Results 3 Quality Inspection 146 While you can choose the relevant configuration settings that best meet your business needs, this example shows the exact settings that you see in Figure 3.34 and Figure 3.35. Origin TL (task list) The option to assign the task list’s origin (or source) for data transfer (see Figure 3.34). The available options are as follows:  Quality certificate  Previous inspection lot  Batch values  Previous inspection point  Copied from the subsystem using the inspection data inter- face in QM  From mobile data recording  Quality certificate transmission Origin RR (results recording) The option to assign data origin (or source) for data transfer for results recording. Once again, the available options are the same as those available for the task list. Selection An option to define a procedure to select suitable results for the target characteristics. The options available are as follows:  Recurring inspection for batch  Recurring inspection for equipment  Recurring inspection for physical sample  Recurring inspection for functional location  Data from inspections for preliminary product  Custom selection of inspection lot If there’s a unique copy procedure, then the QEC_SELECTION business add-in (BAdI) is available. Mapping An option to define the mapping of suitable results to the target master inspection characteristics. The available options are as follows:  Usage of task list key  Master inspection characteristic and method  Characteristic ID For any unique mapping procedure, the QEC_MAPPING BAdI is available. Del.Days (deletion days) Number of days after transfer log generation before the system deletes the transfer log. Log When this checkbox is selected, the system displays the transfer log immediately of successful or unsuccessful data transfers. Field Column Details Table 3.3 Copy Inspection Results (Cont.) © 147 3.2 Optimization Features of Inspection Planning and Quality Inspection Master Data Setup After configuration settings are in place, you need to make a single master data setting for the master inspection characteristics in the inspection plan of the material-plant combination to define the data origin to copy inspection results from. Figure 3.36 shows the inspection plan (Transaction QP02) for material RM17 and plant 1710. For Characteristic 10 of Activity 0010, choose Results Data Origin as 02 Previous inspection lot. This setting enables the system to look for the last (previous) inspection lot to copy inspection results to the just-created inspection lot. As with the inspection lot, you can choose to copy batch results of an inspection lot to the just-created inspec- tion lot. Let’s now delve into the business side of this process. Figure 3.36 Origin of Results Data Business Process of Copy Inspection Results Figure 3.37 shows a previously created inspection lot 890000000350, with the results of five characteristics, which you use as a reference to copy it to the next (or another) inspection lot (see Figure 3.38). 3 Quality Inspection 148 Figure 3.37 Original Inspection Lot Figure 3.38 Copy Results from Another Inspection Lot Figure 3.38 shows the popup that prompts you to enter a reference inspection lot, the results of which will be copied to the new inspection lot. Create a new inspection lot using Transaction QA01 for material RM17, plant 1710, and inspection type 89. The system creates inspection lot number 890000000351, and the © 149 3.2 Optimization Features of Inspection Planning and Quality Inspection popup prompts the user to enter the reference of the inspection lot to be used for copy- ing results into the newly created inspection lot. For this example, enter inspection lot number “890000000350”; the system displays the log shown in Figure 3.39. Figure 3.39 shows the Display Logs screen of a successful (or unsuccessful) copy of inspection results from one inspection lot to another. Here, the system also shows the copied-to inspection lot 890000000351 in the External ID column. As you can see here, it’s not possible to copy inspection results of a classed characteristic as well as that of a calculated characteristic from one inspection lot to another. Figure 3.39 Display Logs of Copied Inspection Results Figure 3.40 shows that inspection lot 890000000351 comprises the copied results, and the Origin is 02 Previous Inspection Lot, which you set up in the characteristic of the inspection plan. If there is any specific or unique business need, you can still make changes to the copied-to results by selecting the relevant characteristic and selecting the Unlock icon. 3 Quality Inspection 150 Figure 3.40 Inspection Results Copied from Previous Inspection Lot to New Inspection Lot Access Figure 3.41, which is the results recording screen (Transaction QE01) of inspec- tion lot number 890000000351. Because your configuration settings stipulate that you can also use the manual option to copy inspection results, choose Edit  Copy Inspection Results. When you do this, the system brings up the inspection lot selection popup. Enter the previous (or other) inspection lot number, and choose Continue. The system brings up operation(s) within the inspection lot for you to choose. Figure 3.41 Copy Options for Results Recording © 151 3.2 Optimization Features of Inspection Planning and Quality Inspection Copy Inspection Results into Batch Classification Now that you’re familiar with how to manually or automatically copy inspection results of one inspection lot to another, you can also copy inspection results into batch classifications. In this business process, the results of an inspection lot are directly transferred as characteristic values of a batch. The following sections explain the steps involved. Configuration Setting You need to make the following two settings: 1. Go to SAP IMG  QM  Basic Settings  Maintain Settings at Plant Level  Inspection Lot Completion  Transfer Inspection Results to Batch, and execute this program. The system automatically activates the necessary settings. 2. Go to SAP IMG  QM  Basic Settings  Maintain Settings at Plant Level  Inspection Lot Completion, and ensure that in the plant settings, the Batch Valuation without Material Spec checkbox is selected. You may also go to Section 3.6.2 (Figure 3.88) for this configuration setting. Master Data Settings The following is the master data that you need to maintain: 1. Create a class characteristic (Transaction CT04). 2. Create a batch class (Transaction CL01) of class type 023 (batch class). 3. Assign the newly created classed characteristic to the batch class at the time of batch class creation (Transaction CL01). 4. Assign a batch class to the material master in the classification view (Transaction MM01). Remember to use class type 023, which is specific to batch class. 5. Assign the inspection type in the material master (Transaction MM01). Choose either inspection plan or material specification. 6. Create a master inspection characteristic with reference to the previously created class characteristic (Transaction QS21). 7. Create an inspection plan with the previously created master inspection characteris- tic (Transaction QP01) or create a material specification (Transaction QS61). Note We suggest that you also read Chapter 9, which explains how to create classes and characteristics. Further, Chapter 9, Section 9.6, covers most of the master data settings that you need to run this business process. All examples in this book are for quantitative characteristics. But if you want to copy a qualitative characteristic of an inspection lot to a batch classification, then while creat- ing the class characteristic (Transaction CT04), go to the Values tab, choose Other 3 Quality Inspection 152 Value Check, and select the Catalog Char. radio button. Here, you can enter the selected set and the associated plant. Business Processes of Copy Inspection Results into Batch Classification The business processes are as follows: 1. Create a manual inspection lot of lot origin 89 (Transaction QA01). In addition, create a new batch number during inspection lot creation. 2. Record the results (Transaction QE01). 3. Record a usage decision (Transaction QA11). When you save the usage decision, a message appears at the bottom of the screen to inform you about transfer of inspec- tion results to batch classification. 4. Display the batch of the material (Transaction MSC3N). In the Classification tab, you’ll find the inspection results transferred as batch characteristics.
sections.he:
כאן — העתקת תוצאות מ-lot ל-lot, ול-batch classification.
**העתקת תוצאות מ-lot ל-lot:** המערכת מאפשרת העתקה ל-lots עוקבים. ההגדרות ספציפיות-סוג-מפעל, ברמת יצירת ה-lot וברמת הרישום. שכיח ב-recurring (type 09), אך גם לכל צירוף.
**תצורה:** SAP IMG • Quality Management • Quality Inspection • Results Recording • Make Settings for Copy of Inspection Results (Figures 3.34, 3.35; דוגמה type 89, מפעל 1710).

טבלה 3.3 — העתקת תוצאות:
| **Inspection Type** | הסוג שעבורו ישימה ההעתקה. |
| **Plant** | המפעל. |
| **Control in Insp. Lot** | מצב ההעברה ברמת היצירה: ללא; אוטומטי בחישוב דגימה; ידני ואוטומטי (ידני — המערכת מבקשת מספר lot). המקור והיעד חייבים להיות זמינים ועקביים. |
| **Control in RR** | מצב ההעברה ברמת הרישום (אותן אפשרויות). |
| **Close** | סוגר את ה-MICs בהעברה מוצלחת. |
| **Origin TL** | מקור ה-task list להעברה: quality certificate; ‏previous inspection lot; ‏batch values; ‏previous inspection point; מ-subsystem (QM data interface); מ-mobile data recording; ‏quality certificate transmission. |
| **Origin RR** | מקור ההעברה לרישום (אותן אפשרויות). |
| **Selection** | נוהל בחירת תוצאות: recurring לאצווה/ציוד/דגימה/functional location; ‏data from preliminary product; ‏custom. ל-unique — BAdI‏ QEC_SELECTION. |
| **Mapping** | מיפוי תוצאות ל-MICs: usage of task list key; ‏MIC and method; ‏characteristic ID. ל-unique — BAdI‏ QEC_MAPPING. |
| **Del.Days** | ימים עד מחיקת יומן ההעברה. |
| **Log** | הצגת יומן ההעברה מיד. |

**נתוני אב:** הגדרה יחידה ל-MICs ב-plan. Figure 3.36 (Transaction QP02, חומר RM17, מפעל 1710): למאפיין 10 בפעולה 0010, ‏Results Data Origin "02 Previous inspection lot" — המערכת מחפשת את ה-lot הקודם להעתקה.
**תהליך:** Figure 3.37 — lot 890000000350 עם תוצאות חמישה מאפיינים, כ-reference. צרו lot חדש (Transaction QA01, ‏RM17, ‏1710, type 89) — lot 890000000351, וחלון לבקשת ה-reference (Figure 3.38). הזינו "890000000350" (Figure 3.39 — יומן; ה-External ID = 890000000351). אי אפשר להעתיק classed/calculated characteristic.
Figure 3.40 — lot 890000000351 עם התוצאות המועתקות, ‏Origin "02 Previous Inspection Lot". לשינוי — בחרו מאפיין ו-Unlock.
Figure 3.41 (Transaction QE01, lot 890000000351) — מאחר שמוגדר ידני, בחרו Edit • Copy Inspection Results, חלון, הזינו את ה-lot הקודם, ‏Continue.

**העתקה ל-batch classification:** התוצאות מועברות כערכי מאפיין של אצווה.
**תצורה:** (1) SAP IMG • QM • Basic Settings • Maintain Settings at Plant Level • Inspection Lot Completion • Transfer Inspection Results to Batch — הריצו (הפעלה אוטומטית). (2) ... • Inspection Lot Completion — סמנו Batch Valuation without Material Spec (גם 3.6.2, ‏Figure 3.88).
**נתוני אב:** (1) class characteristic (Transaction CT04). (2) ‏batch class (Transaction CL01) של class type 023. (3) הקצו את ה-class characteristic ל-batch class (CL01). (4) הקצו batch class לאב החומר בתצוגת Classification (Transaction MM01, ‏class type 023). (5) הקצו inspection type (MM01) — plan או spec. (6) MIC בהפניה ל-class characteristic (Transaction QS21). (7) ‏plan עם ה-MIC (Transaction QP01) או spec (Transaction QS61).
**הערה:** ראו פרק 9 (classes, ‏9.6). לאיכותי — ב-CT04, לשונית Values, ‏Other Value Check, רדיו Catalog Char.
**תהליך:** (1) ‏lot ידני origin 89 (QA01) + אצווה חדשה. (2) רישום (QE01). (3) ‏usage decision (QA11) — בשמירה, הודעה על ההעברה. (4) הצגת האצווה (Transaction MSC3N), לשונית Classification — התוצאות כמאפייני אצווה.

**הערת יועץ:** results-copy — העתקת-תוצאות בין-lots עוקבים + ל-batch-classification. מנקודת-מבט-מעשית, תצורה per-inspection-type + master-data. יועץ מנוסה מפעיל להעברת-תוצאות ל-batch (בסיס-ל-batch-determination לפי-איכות!) ולחיסכון-הקלדה ב-lots-חוזרים. ההבחנה copy-בין-lots (חיסכון) מול-copy-ל-batch (שרשרת-ערך: תוצאה→מאפיין-אצווה→בחירה-במכירה). הבנת-ה-copy חיונית — מחבר QM ל-batch-management. פחות-הקלדות, פחות-טעויות.

sections.title: Usage Decision
sections.en: 3.2.5 Usage Decision Let’s now cover the different types of usage decisions, including collective usage deci- sions and automatic usage decisions:  In collective usage decisions, several inspection lots that are already accepted during the results recording processes are accepted via assignment of a single usage deci- sion code (accepted) to multiple inspection lots.  In automatic usage decision, the system reduces the time and effort required from business users to record usage decisions of accepted inspection lots by automati- cally assigning a usage decision code (accepted) to these inspection lots. We’ll also cover how to reset a usage decision, as well as two ways of reversing one. Collective Usage Decision If you’ve inspected several inspection lots and found the results acceptable, then you can release the material placed in quality inspection to the next processing step. It makes sense to assign an accepted usage design code to all the accepted inspection lots at once, instead of one at a time, saving you time and effort. To perform a collective usage design, use Transaction QA16 or follow menu path Logis- tics  Quality Management  Quality Inspection  Worklist  Inspection Lot Completion  Collective Usage Decision (General) (see Figure 3.42). Enter a specific inspection type, such as inspection type 89, so that the system displays only inspection lots created manually. For the Usage Decision to Be Made area, enter the UD Selected Set “UD89”, UD Plant “1710”, UD Code Group “UD89”, and UD Code “A” (for accepted). © 153 3.2 Optimization Features of Inspection Planning and Quality Inspection Figure 3.42 Collective Usage Decision: Initial Screen Choose Execute (not shown) to go to the screen in Figure 3.43, which consists of a list of quality inspection lots for which you can perform a collective usage design. You have three options for performing collective usage design: 1. UD (Background) The system performs all actions in the background; finally, a message appears at the bottom of the screen to inform you when it saves the usage design code for the inspection lot. 2. UD (Foreground) You have to keep pressing (Enter) to validate each action that the system under- takes. For example, you press (Enter) when the system selects the inspection lot, incorporates the usage design code to the inspection lot, and prompts you to save the changes made. 3. Manual UD You select an inspection lot and manually assign the usage design code. For this example, choose Inspection Lot 80000000353, and then choose More  UD (Background). Once you successfully incorporate the usage design code, the system dis- plays the message at the bottom of the screen that says Usage Decision for Lot 1710 80000000353 Is Saved. 3 Quality Inspection 154 Figure 3.43 Collective Usage Decision and Log Let’s check out whether the system automatically and correctly assigns UD Code A to Inspection Lot 80000000353. To view an inspection lot, use Transaction QA03, and enter the inspection lot number, which in this example is “80000000353”. Figure 3.44 1 shows the display view of Inspection Lot 80000000353 with UD Code A automati- cally assigned, and the long text 2 that the system automatically creates to maintain the log of automatic usage design. Figure 3.44 Collective Usage Decision © 155 3.2 Optimization Features of Inspection Planning and Quality Inspection Tips and Tricks You can select multiple inspection lots in Figure 3.43 and perform a collective usage design function. To do so, choose Select All or choose selected inspection lots and per- form a collective usage design function. Automatic Usage Decision Consider a business scenario in which your reliable, long-time supplier routinely sup- plies material that meets your company’s specification. To bring efficiency to the qual- ity inspection process, as well as reward the supplier for reliably supplying quality product, you can use automatic usage design functionality. Similarly, after a major plant upgrade, the quality of the in-house-produced goods has greatly improved. In this case, you repeatedly end up recording the same acceptable results of the inspected material. If the supplier regularly supplies satisfactory goods and all inspection lots are accepted, then the company starts skipping the results recording step in QM until a problem in any of the inspection lots arises. In the SAP system, these inspection lots have the SKIP status. To optimize the entire business process in QM, you can perform an automatic usage decision for all the inspection lots with the SKIP status, as follows: 1. In the plant settings, maintain the time lapse for automatic usage decisions. A time lapse is the time that the system must wait before it proceeds with automatic usage decision business process. See Figure 3.88 later in this chapter to see where you need to maintain the requisite configuration settings. 2. You also need to ensure that the Automatic UD checkbox is selected in Inspection Setup of the inspection type of the material-plant combination for which you want to perform an automatic usage decision. 3.
