ה-dynamic modification rule מבטל את הצורך לרשום שגרתית את כל התוצאות של כל גלם נכנס או ייצור גמורים באיכות מקובלת. שילובו ברכש ובייצור מביא מיטוב משמעותי. מדלג על מספר מוגדר-מראש של lots לרישום, ומחייב רק usage decision. אך lot שנדחה מפעיל אוטומטית בדיקה רגילה או מוחמרת (Figure 3.59) — שמירה על checks and balances.
(Figure 3.59 — inspection stages: ‏Skip / Reduced / Normal / Tightened; כללי שינוי השלב לאורך זמן.)
ברכש, מביא את הגלם/האריזה מהר לקו אם הספק עומד בבקרה. בדיקות במרווחים; בבעיה — חזרה לרגילה/מוחמרת. יתרונות — פחות הזנה, ‏lead time מופחת לאישור, מלאי מופחת, ותנאי תשלום/מחיר טובים לספק. תורם ל-annual/periodic supplier evaluation (פרק 19).
הסעיף מכסה נתוני אב (sampling scheme, ‏sampling procedure) ותהליכים.
**הערה:** הדוגמה לייצור, אך אותם עקרונות לרכש.

כלל-ה-dynamic-modification מבטל את-הצורך לתעד-שגרתית את-כל-תוצאות-הבדיקה של-כל-חומר-גלם-נכנס מספק או-של-ייצור-רציף של-מוצרים-מוגמרים באיכות-מקובלת. שילוב-הכלל בתהליכי-רכש-וייצור מבטיח אופטימיזציה-ויעילות משמעותיות: הוא-מדלג על-מספר-מוגדר-מראש של-inspection-lots לצורכי-results-recording ודורש-מהמשתמש רק-usage-decision. עבור-היועץ, ה-dynamic-modification הוא-מנוע-ההתאמה של-נטל-הבדיקה לביצועים-בפועל: ספק-שמספק-איכות-עקבית 'מרוויח' מעבר-ל-reduced-inspection או-skip (דילוג-על-בדיקות), וספק-שנכשל 'נענש' ב-tightened-inspection (בדיקה-מוגברת). ההבחנה בין-שלוש-הרמות — tightened (מחמיר), normal (רגיל), reduced/skip (מקל/מדלג) — מהותית: ה-quality-level (רמת-האיכות המצטברת) של-שילוב-חומר-ספק קובע את-הרמה-הנוכחית, וכל-UD מעדכן-אותה. הכלל מגדיר את-תנאי-המעבר (כמה-accepted-רצופים לעלייה, כמה-rejected לירידה). היתרון-הכלכלי עצום: במקום-לבדוק-הכל-תמיד, בודקים-לפי-סיכון — חיסכון של-עשרות-אחוזי-עבודת-מעבדה. הבנת-ה-dynamic-modification חיונית — הוא-האופטימיזציה החשובה-ביותר ברכש-שוטף, מבוסס-תקן (ISO-2859 switching-rules). יועץ מנוסה מטמיע-אותו אחרי-שנצבר-בסיס-נתוני-איכות (לא-מיום-ראשון), עם-כללים-שמרניים תחילה.

**הערת יועץ:** dynamic-modification — התאמת-נטל-בדיקה לביצועים: tightened/normal/reduced/skip לפי-quality-level. מנקודת-מבט-מעשית, ספק-עקבי מרוויח-skip, ספק-כושל נענש-tightened; מבוסס ISO-2859-switching-rules. יועץ מנוסה מטמיע אחרי-שנצבר-בסיס-נתונים (לא-מיום-1), כללים-שמרניים תחילה. ההבחנה שלוש-רמות + תנאי-מעבר (רצף-accepted/rejected). חיסכון עשרות-אחוזי-מעבדה. הבנת-הכלל חיונית — האופטימיזציה החשובה-ברכש-שוטף.

sections.title: Master Data Maintenance
sections.en: 3.4.1 Master Data Maintenance You need to make two quick checks of your master data to ensure that the dynamic modification rule is effectively implemented when conducting transactions. The checks are in the material master and master inspection characteristic, which we’ll dis- cuss in the following subsections. Material Master The material has previously been created, but you need to activate its QM view at the organizational level (plant). In addition, you need to activate inspection type 01 for goods receipt against a purchase order. If the dynamic modification rule is imple- mented in the production process, then make the relevant settings for inspection type 04 for process or production order. Choose the Inspection Type detail for inspection type 01. Select the Skips Allowed checkbox. This ensures that when the dynamic modification rule is working for inspec- tion type 01, it allows skipping of inspection results recording. Inspection type 01 is used to activate QM for goods receipts against a purchase order. Save your settings. Note If you intend to use the dynamic modification rule for goods receipt against the pro- duction process, then you need to make the same Skips Allowed check in the material master for inspection type 04. Inspection type 01 is the QM activation for goods receipt for a purchase order or scheduling agreement with a supplier. You can also activate this check in any other inspection type for which you want to integrate the dynamic modification rule process. Sampling Procedure in the Master Inspection Characteristic You need to ensure that the Sampling Procedure checkbox is checked in the master inspection characteristic. Just like the master inspection characteristic, the sampling © 171 3.4 Dynamic Modification Rule procedure is also QM master data, and you use it to define the sample size of an inspec- tion lot and how the system calculates it. To change the master inspection characteristic, use Transaction QS23 or menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Quality Planning  Basic Data  Inspection Characteris- tic  Change. Choose Control Indicators, and select the Sampling Procedure checkbox. Save your settings. To effectively implement the dynamic modification rule in the production process, maintain the QM master data in the sequence we’ll specify in the following sections. Define a Sampling Scheme In a sampling scheme, sample size is defined based on the total quantity of the goods receipt. The sampling scheme also incorporates the information related to the number of samples that can be accepted or rejected in a sample size to help decide whether the quality inspector should accept or reject an inspection lot. To create a sampling scheme, use Transaction QDP1 or menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Quality Planning  Basic Data  Sampling  Sampling Scheme  Create. On the initial screen, enter the sampling scheme (“QSS” in this example), and press (Enter) to see the header data for the sampling scheme. Select the Valuation Parameters as Attributive Insp. to ensure that the system automatically valuates all master inspection characteristics within the tolerance limits as accepted and that the nonconforming master inspection characteristics have the rejected valuation. Select the Sampling Tables For as Severity/AQL. Note Acceptable quality level (AQL) is the international industry standard to define the total percentage of samples that are either accepted or rejected from an overall sample cal- culation. Hence, an AQL level of 3.5% allows defects of 3.5% of the overall sample size calculation. If the system calculates the sample size of an inspection lot to be 100 and its AQL is 3.5%, then not more than 3.5 samples out of the 100-sample lot can be rejected for the system to consider the inspection lot as acceptable. Although various international AQL standards, such as those of ISO, are available in SAP as standard offerings and you can immediately begin using them, we’ll cover how to create an AQL in detail, just in case there is a business need that is company-specific. Choose Continue to define the inspection severity and AQL value. Choose the Inspec- tion Severity dropdown, and the system brings up the four different severity levels. Choose inspection severity 002, which denotes a reduced inspection; enter an AQL Value of “3.000”; press (Enter) or choose QSS; and the screen in Figure 3.60 appears. 3 Quality Inspection 172 Figure 3.60 Sampling Table for Inspection Severity 2 (Reduced Inspection) and AQL Value of 2.000 Here, you see the sampling table for sampling scheme QSS with an inspection severity of 002 and an AQL value of 3.000. Note that it’s standard SAP system behavior that all leading zeros are eliminated, but up to three decimal places are shown. Therefore, in Figure 3.60, the inspection severity of 002 has been changed to 2. Although the AQL value is defined as 3.0 in Figure 3.60, the system shows up to three decimal places. Here, define that the sample size is five units for an inspection lot quantity up to 500 units. Of that, a minimum of two units (column c1) has to be accepted, while a maxi- mum of three units (column d1) is allowed for rejection. This is applicable for all the inspection lots for which there is a reduced inspection. For an inspection lot of 10,000 units or more, the sample size is 10 units, while the number of acceptable samples is 4. A maximum of 6 rejections is acceptable. Choose Other Table to go to the screen in Figure 3.61. The same process for creating another set for inspection severity and AQL is repeated for an inspection severity of normal, which is denoted by 004 and with an AQL level of 4.000. This screen defines that for an inspection lot quantity of 500 units, there is a sample size of five units, out of which a minimum of three units (column c1) has to be accepted, while a maximum of four units (column d1) is allowed for rejection. For an inspection lot of 10,000 or greater, the sample size is 10, and the number of acceptable samples should be five. A maximum of seven rejections is acceptable. Save the sam- pling scheme. © 173 3.4 Dynamic Modification Rule Figure 3.61 Sampling Table for Inspection Severity 4 and Acceptable Quality Limit Value of 4.000 Depending on business requirements, there can be several variations for defining reduced, normal, and tightened inspections in SAP S/4HANA. For example, with a reduced inspection, there can be fewer sample sizes to inspect, while the acceptance and rejection samples stay the same. In this example, we’ve kept the sample size for reduced and normal inspection the same, which is 5 units for an inspection lot up to 500 units, but defined that for a reduced inspection, the acceptable samples should be at least 2 units, and the maximum rejected samples should be 3 units. For a normal inspection, at least 3 units must be acceptable, and a maximum of 4 units can be rejected. You can use the same process to define a tightened inspection. The produced good is then monitored more frequently for quality checks until it’s able to maintain and sus- tain the acceptable quality products over a longer period of time. Once this is achieved, the tightened inspection can be brought back to normal inspection or even reduced inspection. The option to define a tightened inspection with an inspection severity code of 006 is defined. All subsequent steps remain the same as for reduced or normal inspections. Configuration Tip To set up an inspection severity that meets your company’s business needs, follow the configuration menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  Quality Planning  Basic Data  Sample, SPC  Define Inspection Severities. 3 Quality Inspection 174 Setting Up a Sampling Procedure A sampling procedure is the QM master data that helps you define how the system cal- culates the sample size of an inspection lot. To create a sampling procedure, use Trans- action QDV1 or menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Quality Planning  Basic Data  Sampling  Sampling Procedure  Create. On the initial screen of the sampling procedure, define the sampling procedure (in this example, it’s “QMSP”) and press (Enter) to bring up the screen in Figure 3.62, the assignments screen of the sampling procedure. Here, assign the Sampling Type as Use sampling scheme, which you just cre- ated in the previous step. Other sampling types available are Fixed Sample, which entails that regardless of the inspection lot size, the sample size is fixed, and Percent- age, which entails that the sample size is calculated based on a defined percentage of the inspection lot. For Valuation Mode, select Attributive inspection nonconf. units to ensure that the sys- tem valuates a master inspection characteristic as accepted if the results are within the specified tolerance limits. If any result is not, then the system valuates the master inspection characteristic as rejected. As Sampling Type is selected as Use sampling scheme, assign the relevant sampling scheme, which in this example is QSS. Figure 3.62 Sampling Procedure with Sampling Type and Valuation Mode © 175 3.4 Dynamic Modification Rule In the Inspection Points area, choose Others so you can enter any relevant identifier as an inspection point. If you’re creating a sampling procedure for eventual use in PM or sample management, then choose the relevant radio button. Note Chapter 7 provides information on integrating QM with PM, and Chapter 10 discusses sample management. In both chapters, use the relevant inspection points that we dis- cuss here. Choose Continue to go to the screen in Figure 3.63, assign the previously created sam- pling scheme QSS, and then choose Additional Data to go to Figure 3.64. Figure 3.63 Assigning Sampling Scheme in Sampling Procedure Figure 3.64 Sampling Procedure QMSP with Inspection Severity of 002 and AQL Value of 2.000 3 Quality Inspection 176 Figure 3.64 requires you to assign the inspection severity and the AQL value for the pre- viously created sampling scheme QSS. Press (F4) or choose the dropdown box to the right of the Inspection Severity field (not shown). The system brings up two options for sampling scheme QSS from which to choose—namely, reduced inspection with an AQL of 3.000 and normal inspection with an AQL of 4.000. Choose Reduced Inspection with an AQL value of 3.000, and then choose Continue to go to Figure 3.64. Save your entries, and the system opens a popup that asks if you want to create an allowed relationship between the sampling scheme and a dynamic modifi- cation rule. As you have yet to create a dynamic modification rule that meets your business needs, which we’ll cover in the next section, choose No in the popup. Dynamic Modification Rule The dynamic modification rule consists of user-defined rules that define the factors that trigger a move from normal inspection to reduced inspection or vice versa. The dynamic modification rule also enables you to define when the system should skip results recording of inspection lots. The dynamic modification rule defines the number of inspection lots that have the accepted or rejected statuses before the system switches inspection stages from normal to reduced to tightened or vice versa. To create a dynamic modification rule, use Transaction QDR1 or menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Quality Planning  Basic Data  Sampling  Dynamic Modification Rule  Create. On the initial screen, enter “DMR” (in this example), and press (Enter). On the header data screen for the dynamic modification rule, enter the short descrip- tion, and select the dynamic modification rule as For Usage Decision. This option ensures that the basis for the system to trigger the dynamic modification rule is a usage decision of an inspection lot; that is, if an inspection lot has been accepted during the usage decision, the dynamic modification rule decides whether there is a need for an inspection stage change. Warning We suggest that you use the dynamic modification rule for usage decisions because, in this case, the system only updates quality scores based on the usage decision, and in the case of rejections and/or partial acceptance, the system updates the quality score accordingly. To use the dynamic modification rule at an inspection lot level, it entails that there will be hardly any rejections, and the system updates the quality scores based only on inspection lot creation. If you reject the material, the system doesn’t update the quality scores, even though you run the cancellation process of the usage decision and results recording. © 177 3.4 Dynamic Modification Rule Choose Continue to bring up the detailed screen to define inspection stages of a dynamic modification rule (see Figure 3.65). An inspection stage enables the user to define the number of accepted or rejected inspection lots that lead to an inspection stage change. Inspection stages are also referred to as stages. For this example, there are two stages: 1 and 2. For stage 1, define an inspection severity of 2, which is the normal inspection. Also acti- vate the ISt checkbox (initial stage) to ensure that the dynamic modification rule pro- cesses always start with normal inspection (stage 1) before the stage changes to reduced inspection (stage 2). In stage 2, activate the checkbox for Skip inspection, which means that system allows skips in results recording for the inspection stage 2 (reduced inspec- tion). Next, select the row of inspection Stage 1 shown in Figure 3.65, and choose Stage Change. This leads to Figure 3.66. Figure 3.65 Dynamic Modification Rule with Details about Inspection Stages Figure 3.66 1 shows the detailed screen for inspection stage changes for inspection stage 1. Here, define that at least one inspection lot must have the usage decision OK or Accepted so that inspection stage 1 changes to stage 2. If there is a single rejection 1 with Not OK or a rejection in the Rejections field, then the next inspection stage is 1, which is the normal inspection and requires results recording. Choose Continue, which leads back to Figure 3.65. Repeat the same process from the screen in Figure 3.65 by selecting Stage 2 and Stage Change to go to the screen in Figure 3.66 2, which stipulates that there can be a maxi- mum of two skips before the system considers stage change. If there is a skipped inspection lot during results recording (for which no result recording is needed in the first place), the system still creates the next inspection lot with the skip status on goods receipt against the process order. Similarly, if there is one rejection (Not OK), then the next stage remains 1, which is a normal inspection. In the case of infrequent inspec- tions, you can define the maximum skip duration in days, after which the system must take inspections into account. Choose Continue to go to the screen in Figure 3.67. 3 Quality Inspection 178 Figure 3.66 Stage Changes in Dynamic Modification Rule Figure 3.67 Overview of Inspection Stages’ Change of Dynamic Modification Rule Figure 3.67 shows that after you incorporate all the necessary details for individual stage changes, the system reflects the same in various columns. Choose Check (for con- sistency check) in Figure 3.67 to see whether there is any error in the dynamic modifi- cation rule creation. Save your settings, and you’ll see a popup that allows you to create a relationship between the dynamic modification rule and the sampling procedure. Choose Yes so that you can maintain the relationship between the dynamic modification rule and the sampling procedure. © 179 3.4 Dynamic Modification Rule Dynamic Modification Rule with the Sampling Procedure One of the requirements for dynamic modification rule use is to maintain a relation- ship between the dynamic modification rule and the sampling procedure. Although the option to maintain this relationship appears while you’re creating the dynamic modification rule in this example, you can also create this relationship independently. To do so, use Transaction QDB1 or menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Quality Planning  Basic Data  Sample  Sampling Procedure  Assign Dynamic Modification Rule. On the initial screen to maintain the relationship of the dynamic modification rule with the sampling procedure, choose New Entries, which leads to Figure 3.68. Here, maintain a new relationship between sampling procedure QMSP and DynModRule DMR and save the settings. Figure 3.68 Dynamic Modification Rule DMR Relationship with Sampling Procedure QMSP Inspection Plan An inspection plan is the task list referred to whenever an inspection lot against a pro- cess order is created, and it consists of previously created master inspection character- istics. To create an inspection plan, use Transaction QP01 or menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Quality Planning  Inspection Planning  Inspection Plan  Create. On the initial screen to create or change an inspection plan, enter material “RM17” and plant “1710”. Press (Enter), and the screen in Figure 3.69 appears. Here, the header information you assign the usage is 5, which is for goods receipt, and the status of the inspection plan is set to 4, which is released. The Dynamic Modif. Level option allows you to define the dynamic modification rule in the inspection plan with the following three options:  Activate the dynamic modification rule on the entire inspection type—which means, for example, the system activates the dynamic modification rule on all the incoming inspection lots against the purchase order (inspection type 01).  Let the system evaluate whether each and every individual inspection lot qualifies for the dynamic modification rule process.  Trigger the dynamic modification rule at the individual Inspection Lot Level. 3 Quality Inspection 180 Figure 3.69 Header Data of Inspection Plan For this example, choose the option to have the dynamic modification rule at the inspection lot level, as shown in Figure 3.69, and also assign the previously created dynamic Modification Rule “DMR”. Also assign inspection point 100 to the inspection plan. Next, in the operations view of the inspection plan, assign the inspection charac- teristics for which you’ve activated the sampling procedure and assign the sampling procedure QMSP. Save your entries.
sections.he:
שתי בדיקות נתוני אב — אב החומר וה-MIC.
**אב חומר:** הפעילו את תצוגת ה-QM ברמת המפעל, ו-inspection type 01 (GR מול הזמנת רכש). לייצור — type 04. בחרו Inspection Type detail ל-01, סמנו Skips Allowed (מאפשר דילוג ברישום). שמרו.
**הערה:** לייצור, סמנו Skips Allowed ל-type 04.
**Sampling Procedure ב-MIC:** ודאו Sampling Procedure מסומן. ל-Transaction QS23 או Logistics • Quality Management • Quality Planning • Basic Data • Inspection Characteristic • Change. בחרו Control Indicators, סמנו Sampling Procedure, שמרו.

**Define a Sampling Scheme:** גודל הדגימה לפי כמות ה-GR; כולל מספר הדגימות לקבלה/דחייה. ל-Transaction QDP1 או ... • Sampling • Sampling Scheme • Create. הזינו "QSS", ‏Enter. בחרו Valuation Parameters "Attributive Insp." ו-Sampling Tables For "Severity/AQL".
**הערה:** ‏AQL (acceptable quality level) — תקן בינלאומי לאחוז הדגימות המקובל/נדחה. ‏AQL 3.5% מתיר 3.5% פגמים. דגימה 100 ב-AQL 3.5% → לא יותר מ-3.5 דחיות. תקני ISO זמינים; נכסה יצירה למקרה ייחודי.
‏Continue להגדרת severity ו-AQL. ב-Inspection Severity, ארבע רמות. בחרו 002 (reduced), ‏AQL Value "3.000", ‏Enter / QSS (Figure 3.60).
ה-sampling table ל-QSS (severity 002, ‏AQL 3.000). (SAP מסיר אפסים מובילים, מציג עד שלושה עשרוניים — 002 → 2.) הגדירו: ל-lot עד 500 — דגימה 5, מינימום 2 לקבלה (c1), מקסימום 3 לדחייה (d1). ל-lot 10,000+ — דגימה 10, ‏4 מקובלים, מקסימום 6 דחיות. בחרו Other Table (Figure 3.61).
חזרו על התהליך ל-normal (004, ‏AQL 4.000): ל-500 — דגימה 5, מינימום 3 (c1), מקסימום 4 (d1); ל-10,000+ — דגימה 10, ‏5 מקובלים, מקסימום 7 דחיות. שמרו.
ניתן וריאציות. ל-tightened — ניטור תכוף יותר עד שמירת איכות לאורך זמן, ואז חזרה ל-normal/reduced. ה-severity ל-tightened הוא 006.
**Configuration Tip:** להגדרת severity: SAP IMG • Quality Management • Quality Planning • Basic Data • Sample, SPC • Define Inspection Severities.

**הקמת Sampling Procedure:** ל-Transaction QDV1 או ... • Sampling • Sampling Procedure • Create. הזינו "QMSP", ‏Enter (Figure 3.62). הקצו Sampling Type "Use sampling scheme" (אחרים — Fixed Sample, ‏Percentage). ‏Valuation Mode "Attributive inspection nonconf. units". הקצו את ה-scheme QSS.
ב-Inspection Points בחרו Others (או רדיו ל-PM/sample management).
**הערה:** פרק 7 (PM), פרק 10 (sample management).
‏Continue (Figure 3.63), הקצו QSS, ‏Additional Data (Figure 3.64). הקצו severity ו-AQL. ‏F4 ב-Inspection Severity — שתי אפשרויות ל-QSS (reduced AQL 3.000, ‏normal AQL 4.000). בחרו Reduced (AQL 3.000), ‏Continue. שמרו — חלון ליצירת קשר עם dynamic modification rule; בחרו No (טרם נוצר).

**Dynamic Modification Rule:** כללים המגדירים מעבר normal↔reduced ומתי לדלג. מגדיר את מספר ה-lots המקובלים/נדחים לפני מעבר.
ל-Transaction QDR1 או ... • Sampling • Dynamic Modification Rule • Create. הזינו "DMR", ‏Enter. הזינו תיאור ובחרו For Usage Decision (הבסיס למעבר — ה-usage decision).
**אזהרה:** השתמשו ב-For Usage Decision — המערכת מעדכנת quality scores לפי ה-usage decision (כולל דחיות/קבלה חלקית). ברמת lot — כמעט אין דחיות, והעדכון רק לפי יצירת ה-lot; בדחייה ה-score אינו מתעדכן גם בביטול.
‏Continue (Figure 3.65) — הגדרת שלבים (stages). בדוגמה שניים: 1 ו-2. לשלב 1, ‏severity 2 (normal), והפעילו ISt (initial stage — תמיד מתחיל ב-normal). לשלב 2, סמנו Skip inspection (דילוג ברישום). בחרו שורת שלב 1, ‏Stage Change (Figure 3.66).
Figure 3.66 (שלב 1): לפחות lot אחד עם usage decision OK/Accepted למעבר לשלב 2. דחייה יחידה (Not OK / Rejections) → השלב הבא 1 (normal, רישום). ‏Continue.
חזרו לשלב 2, ‏Stage Change (Figure 3.66): מקסימום שני skips לפני מעבר. ב-lot מדולג, המערכת עדיין יוצרת את הבא ב-skip ב-GR. דחייה (Not OK) → השלב הבא 1. בבדיקות נדירות, הגדירו maximum skip duration בימים. ‏Continue (Figure 3.67).
Figure 3.67 — סיכום השלבים. בחרו Check (עקביות). שמרו — חלון ליצירת קשר עם sampling procedure; בחרו Yes.

**DMR עם Sampling Procedure:** דרישה — קשר בין ה-DMR ל-sampling procedure. ניתן עצמאית: Transaction QDB1 או ... • Sample • Sampling Procedure • Assign Dynamic Modification Rule. ‏New Entries (Figure 3.68) — קשר בין QMSP ל-DMR. שמרו.

**Inspection Plan:** ל-Transaction QP01 או ... • Inspection Plan • Create. הזינו material "RM17", ‏plant "1710", ‏Enter (Figure 3.69). ‏usage 5 (GR), ‏status 4 (released).
ה-Dynamic Modif. Level — שלוש אפשרויות: הפעלה על כל ה-inspection type (כל ה-lots מול הזמנת רכש, type 01); הערכה לכל lot בנפרד; הפעלה ברמת ה-Inspection Lot Level.
בדוגמה, ‏Inspection Lot Level, הקצו DMR "DMR", ‏inspection point 100. בתצוגת הפעולות, הקצו את המאפיינים עם ה-sampling procedure QMSP. שמרו.

**הערת יועץ:** master-data dynamic-mod — שתי-בדיקות: מאסטר (QM-view, inspection-type-01 + DMR מוקצה) ו-MIC (dynamic-modification-indicator ברמת-characteristic). מנקודת-מבט-מעשית, הכלל (QDR1) מגדיר-stages+תנאי-מעבר; ההקצאה במאסטר/plan קובעת-היקף. יועץ מנוסה מבין: רמת-ה-dynamic (lot מול-characteristic) קובעת-גרנולריות. ⚠️ ראה-2.11.9 — skip-levels לא-תואמים שוברים calculated-characteristics. הבנת-האב חיונית — שתי-חוליות, שתיהן-חובה.

sections.title: Business Processes
sections.en: 3.4.2 Business Processes Now that you’re familiar with the QM master data you need, let’s review the end-to-end business process flow to show how the dynamic modification rule actually works. Cre- ate a process order for the previously covered material for which the dynamic modifi- cation rule is active, and perform its goods receipt. On goods receipt, the system creates an inspection lot. Use Transaction QA03 to display the inspection lot, which in this example is 10000000716 (see Figure 3.70). Notice that the dynamic modification rule applies © 181 3.4 Dynamic Modification Rule successfully to inspection lot 10000000716. In addition, the system correctly calcu- lates the sample size of 5 based on the goods receipt quantity of 100 PC. Figure 3.70 Sampling Procedure and Dynamic Modification Rule in Inspection Lot The next steps are to undertake results recording, followed by usage decision and stock posting. For the usage decision, enter the acceptance code to accept the inspection lot and undertake its stock posting. As soon as the usage decision is undertaken as an accepted decision, further goods receipts against the same or different purchase order have inspection lots with SKIP status. This means there’s no need for results recording, and the usage decision alone is sufficient. The system denotes such an inspection lot with the SKIP status. Figure 3.71 shows inspection lot number 10000000718, with the SKIP status that the system assigned using the dynamic modification rule. Tips and Tricks If your organization needs to record results of an inspection lot with SKIP status, you can still do so. The standard process of results recording prevails, although the system issues an information message that a specific inspection lot has SKIP status. 3 Quality Inspection 182 Figure 3.71 Inspection Lot with SKIP Status You can further check whether the dynamic modification rule setup is correct or com- plete. Select two inspection lots with SKIP status, enter results, and then reject by assigning a usage decision code as rejected for both inspection lots. When you undertake subsequent goods receipt against the process order, the system doesn’t trigger the dynamic modification rule with SKIP, and normal results recording is required. We just covered the functional aspects of dynamic modification rule functionality in this section. However, Figure 3.72 shows the Quality Level History app, which leverages the dynamic modification rule functionality to evaluate quality levels and history to make more informed business decisions. The stage changes for the past several inspec- tion lots are shown here. © 183
sections.he:
צרו הזמנת תהליך לחומר עם ה-DMR הפעיל, ובצעו GR — המערכת יוצרת lot.
Transaction QA03 — lot 10000000716 (Figure 3.70). ה-DMR חל; המערכת מחשבת דגימה 5 לפי GR 100 PC.
הצעדים — רישום, ‏usage decision, ‏posting. בקבלה (accepted), ‏GRs עוקבים מקבלים lots ב-SKIP — אין צורך ברישום, ה-usage decision מספיק. Figure 3.71 — lot 10000000718 ב-SKIP (מ-DMR).
**Tips and Tricks:** אם צריך לרשום תוצאות ל-lot ב-SKIP — ניתן (הודעת מידע על ה-SKIP).
לבדיקת ההקמה: בחרו שני lots ב-SKIP, הזינו תוצאות, ודחו (קוד rejected) לשניהם. ב-GR עוקב, המערכת אינה מפעילה SKIP — נדרש רישום רגיל.
Figure 3.72 — אפליקציית Quality Level History, המנצלת את ה-DMR להערכת רמות איכות והיסטוריה. שינויי השלבים של ה-lots האחרונים מוצגים.

כעת, כשמוכרים נתוני-האב הנדרשים, נסקור את-זרימת-התהליך מקצה-לקצה להמחשת פעולת-ה-dynamic-modification-rule: יוצרים process-order לחומר שעבורו-הכלל-פעיל, ומבצעים goods-receipt. ב-GR, המערכת יוצרת inspection-lot; משתמשים ב-Transaction-QA03 להצגת-ה-lot (בדוגמה, 10000000716), ורואים שכלל-ה-dynamic-modification חל. עבור-היועץ, נקודת-האימות המרכזית היא-מסך-ה-lot: בלשונית-הרלוונטית רואים את-ה-inspection-stage הנוכחי (tightened/normal/reduced/skip) שהמערכת קבעה לפי-ה-quality-level המצטבר. אם-השלב-הוא-skip, ה-lot נוצר אך-מדלג-על-results-recording — נדרשת רק-usage-decision (או-אף-היא-אוטומטית, בשילוב-auto-UD). ההבחנה בין-lot-רגיל (results מלאים) ל-lot-ב-skip (ללא-recording, רק-UD) נראית-בבירור בתהליך — וזו-ההמחשה שהכלל-עובד. כל-UD מעדכן את-ה-quality-level: רצף-accepted מקדם לעבר-skip, כשל-בודד עלול-להחזיר ל-normal או-tightened (לפי-הכלל). מעקב דרך-אפליקציית-Quality-Level-History מציג את-מסלול-השלבים לאורך-זמן. הבנת-התהליך חיונית — היא-שמאפשרת לאמת שההטמעה-עובדת ולנטר את-התנהגות-הכלל. יועץ מנוסה בודק אחרי-ההטמעה כמה-lots-עוקבים ומוודא שהשלבים-מתקדמים כמצופה, לפני-הרחבה לכל-החומרים.

**הערת יועץ:** תהליך dynamic-mod — GR → lot (QA03) → רואים-stage נוכחי; skip = אין-recording, רק-UD. מנקודת-מבט-מעשית, כל-UD מעדכן quality-level; רצף-accepted מקדם-ל-skip, כשל מחזיר. יועץ מנוסה מאמת כמה-lots-עוקבים אחרי-הטמעה + מנטר ב-Quality-Level-History-app. ההבחנה lot-רגיל (results מלאים) מול-skip (UD בלבד). שילוב-auto-UD = זרימה-ללא-מגע. הבנת-התהליך חיונית — אימות-שההטמעה-חיה.

sections.title: New Inspection Types
sections.en: 3.5 New Inspection Types Figure 3.72 Quality Level History App 3.5 New Inspection Types In Chapter 2, we explained that creating new inspection types to meet business needs normally doesn’t serve the purpose because the functions and functionality offered are the same as you find with standard inspection types. However, in unique business sce- narios, when you need to distinguish a quality inspection process from a routine or normal inspection, you proceed with the necessary configuration of a new inspection type and its associated dependent configuration that enables you to run the business process. The example in this section shows that you want to create a new inspection type to attend to special inspection needs for tea leaves that come from specific tea gardens— Darjeeling and Kenya gardens. Here, you perform step-by-step configuration and assign the configured objects to master data that lets you run the business process. Let’s get started.
sections.he:
בפרק 2 הוסבר שיצירת inspection types חדשים לרוב אינה משרתת (הפונקציות זהות לתקניים). אך בתרחישים ייחודיים, כשצריך להבחין בין תהליך בדיקה לרגיל, מבצעים תצורה חדשה.
הדוגמה — inspection type חדש לעלי תה מגנים ספציפיים (Darjeeling, ‏Kenya). תצורה צעד-אחר-צעד והקצאה לנתוני אב.

כפי-שהוסבר בפרק 2, יצירת-inspection-types חדשים לצורכי-עסק בדרך-כלל אינה-משרתת-מטרה — הפונקציות זהות לאלה של-ה-types הסטנדרטיים. אולם, בתרחישים-עסקיים ייחודיים, כשנדרש להבחין תהליך-בדיקת-איכות מבדיקה-שגרתית, מבצעים את-התצורה הנדרשת של-inspection-type חדש והתצורות-התלויות. עבור-היועץ, זהו-כלל-החלטה חשוב: קודם-כל, נצלו את-הסטנדרט (01-GR-מרכש, 03-in-process, 04-GR-מייצור, 06-returns, 10-delivery, 14-calibration, 89-manual) — הם-מכסים 95% מהצרכים. inspection-type חדש מוצדק רק-כשנדרשת הפרדה אמיתית: זרימת-אישור-שונה, דיווח-נפרד, או-תהליך-מובחן (למשל, בדיקת-פיילוט מול-בדיקה-שגרתית באותו-אירוע-עסקי). ההבחנה בין-'שימוש-חוזר-בסטנדרט' (זול, מתוחזק) ל-'יצירת-חדש' (תקורת-תצורה: task-list-usage, origin-assignment, defaults) מהותית לעלות-תחזוקה ארוכת-טווח — כל-type-חדש הוא-אובייקט-תצורה שחי-לנצח. המבנה: ה-type החדש (כמו-8901) נגזר-מ-origin קיים (89-manual) ויורש את-מנגנוניו. הבנת-שיקול-ההחלטה חיונית — היא-שמונעת התפוצצות-types מיותרת. יועץ מנוסה דורש הצדקה-עסקית-מפורשת לכל-type-חדש, ומתעד את-ייעודו — הסעיפים-הבאים מדגימים את-ארבעת-שלבי-התצורה, האב, והתהליך.

**הערת יועץ:** new-inspection-types — כלל-החלטה: קודם-סטנדרט (01/03/04/06/10/14/89 = 95% מהצרכים); חדש רק-להפרדה-אמיתית (זרימה/דיווח-נפרד). מנקודת-מבט-מעשית, type-חדש (8901) נגזר-מ-origin קיים (89) ויורש-מנגנון. יועץ מנוסה דורש הצדקה-עסקית לכל-type + מתעד-ייעוד. ההבחנה שימוש-בסטנדרט (זול) מול-חדש (תקורת-תצורה לנצח). הבנת-הכלל חיונית — מונע התפוצצות-types. ארבעה-שלבי-תצורה בהמשך.

sections.title: Configuration Settings
sections.en: 3.5.1 Configuration Settings You need to perform the following four configuration steps: 1. Create a task list usage. 2. Maintain the inspection type. 3. Maintain the inspection lot origins, and assign inspection types. 4. Define the default values for the inspection type. 3 Quality Inspection 184 Create a Task List Usage You’re already familiar with the concept of inspection types from Chapter 2. If an inspection type is active, the system creates an inspection lot after a particular event, even if there is no inspection plan yet. This event can be a goods receipt for the goods movement for a purchase order or simply a manual inspection lot creation. When the system creates an inspection lot, it looks for the relevant task list usage that you’ve assigned in the inspection plan. You create a new task list usage to distinguish it from your regular inspection or standard task list usage available in the system. To create a new task list usage, follow menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  Qual- ity Planning  Inspection Planning  General  Define Task List Usage for Inspection Plans. Create a new task list usage 890; enter its description, which later helps you clearly identify its usage; and stipulate that the task list usage will be available for material only by choosing 001 in the DCr field. Maintain the Inspection Type QM uses inspection types to control the inventory movement—for example, for a material purchased, produced, or transferred when receiving the material in inventory. Inspection types can keep the inventory from becoming available for further use. Figure 3.73 Inspection Type Details © 185 3.5 New Inspection Types To create a new inspection type, follow menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  Quality Inspection  Inspection Lot Creation  Maintain Inspection Types. You’ll see the inspection type overview, where you can create new inspection type 8901 by using the copy function to copy from inspection type 89. Enter the short text of the newly cre- ated inspection type. Choose inspection type 8901, and then choose Details (or double- click inspection type 8901), which leads to the screen in Figure 3.73. Table 3.4 explains the details of each field of Figure 3.73. A few fields in the Remarks col- umn are intentionally left blank because the explanation provided in the Details col- umn is sufficient. Field Details Remarks Inspection Lot Processing Status profile A status profile provides greater con- trol over activities while performing business transactions. A status profile, for example, can allow or disallow results recording while hav- ing a specific status. Chapter 14 covers the status profile that you create first and assign in this field. Order type These are QM-specific order types (QL01 and QL02) for appraisal cost recording. Sample Type Various physical sample types are avail- able that directly correlate with the area of working. For example, inspec- tion type 04, which is for goods receipt against production, has the option of physical sample type 02, which is for sample from production. Chapter 10 covers sam- ple management. UD selected set An option to assign a selected set for a usage decision to an inspection. This ensures that only relevant codes and code groups appear while recording usage decision. Selected Set in Same Plant This checkbox, if selected, brings up only the plant-specific selected set. Print Control Print sample drawing instr. immed. This checkbox, if selected, immediately prints sample-drawing instructions upon creation of an inspection lot. Chapter 10 covers sam- ple management. Table 3.4 Field Details of Inspection Type 3 Quality Inspection 186 Print Insp. instruction immediately This checkbox, if selected, immediately prints inspection instructions upon cre- ation of an inspection lot. Display detailed notifi- cations This checkbox, if selected, immediately displays a popup with detailed reasons for the print failure. Inspection Results Recording view There are several available options to choose from for how you’d like to see and let the system function during inspection results recording. Notification type A notification type is assigned in case defects are recorded during results recording. The system automatically creates these notifications while recording defects. Chapter 12 covers qual- ity notification. One Q-notification per insp. lot This checkbox, if selected, creates one complete quality notification for the entire inspection lot, instead of creat- ing it for each defect within the same inspection lot. Inspection Planning Task list usage A unique identifier for a routing or master recipe, which is considered during inspection planning. Assign task list usage 890, which you created in the previous step. Operations Data for Material Specification Control key A control key has to be assigned by default in case inspection is under- taken by the material specification (and not the task list). A value given here is then used as the default. Activity A default operation number is assigned for material specification (and not in the case of a task list). Opr. short text Short text of the operation. Field Details Remarks Table 3.4 Field Details of Inspection Type (Cont.) © 187 3.5 New Inspection Types Maintain Inspection Lot Origins and Assign Inspection Types When you create a new inspection type, you need to assign it to the inspection origin. An important point in the context of inspection planning is that you can assign multi- ple inspection types to an inspection lot origin, but you can’t assign one inspection type to different inspection lot origins at the same time. It’s also important to note that you can’t add a new inspection lot origin (unlike with inspection types and inspection plan usage) because these tables are located in the SAP namespace. To assign a newly created inspection type to an inspection origin, follow menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  Quality Inspection  Inspection Lot Creation  Maintain Inspection Lot Origins and Assign Inspection Types. Figure 3.74 consists of various inspection lot origins. The LO (lot origin) column is the inspection lot origin, while the No column represents the number range that is associated with the inspection origin. All the inspection types that you assign to a particular inspection origin will have the same number range. The TLT (task list type) column and value Q represent the task list type inspection plan. Choose inspection origin LO 89, and then choose Inspection Types for the Origin on the left side of the figure, wherein you create a new entry of the newly created inspection type (InspType) 8901. The inspection origin 89 already has two inspection types—89 and 8914—assigned to it, to which you’re now adding the second inspection type (8901). Figure 3.74 Assignment of Inspection Type to Inspection Origin Define Default Values for Inspection Type For each inspection type, you can make default settings that are then available when you assign them to the material master. These defaults can then save time and effort in individually assigning or unassigning values or selecting or deselecting checkboxes. Typically, you use SAP defaults. To set default values for inspection types, follow menu path SAP IMG  Quality Manage- ment  Quality Inspection  Inspection Lot Creation  Define Default Values for Inspec- tion Types. In the screen that appears, choose inspection type 8901, and then choose Details. 3 Quality Inspection 188 The screen that appears (see Figure 3.75) consists of all the fields that we already cov- ered for inspection types in Chapter 2, Section 2.1. This brings us to the end of the configuration settings and steps that you need to ensure exist for the new inspection type. The next section covers assigning these con- figuration settings to your master data. Figure 3.75 Default Values for Inspection Type
sections.he:
ארבעה צעדי תצורה:
1. יצירת task list usage.
2. תחזוקת ה-inspection type.
3. תחזוקת inspection lot origins והקצאת types.
4. הגדרת ברירות מחדל.

**יצירת Task List Usage:** אם ה-type פעיל, המערכת יוצרת lot לאחר אירוע (GR או יצירה ידנית), גם ללא plan. ביצירה, המערכת מחפשת את ה-task list usage שב-plan. ל-SAP IMG • Quality Management • Quality Planning • Inspection Planning • General • Define Task List Usage for Inspection Plans. צרו usage 890, תיאור, וקבעו 001 בשדה DCr (זמין לחומר בלבד).

**תחזוקת Inspection Type:** ה-types שולטים בתנועת המלאי (נרכש/מיוצר/מועבר) — יכולים למנוע זמינות. ל-SAP IMG • Quality Management • Quality Inspection • Inspection Lot Creation • Maintain Inspection Types. צרו type 8901 בהעתקה מ-89, הזינו טקסט. בחרו 8901, ‏Details (Figure 3.73).

טבלה 3.4 — שדות ה-inspection type (Figure 3.73):
| **Status profile** | בקרה רבה יותר על הפעילויות (למשל מתיר/אוסר רישום בסטטוס; פרק 14). |
| **Order type** | סוגי QM (QL01, ‏QL02) לרישום עלויות appraisal. |
| **Sample Type** | סוגי דגימה פיזית (למשל type 04 → physical sample type 02; פרק 10). |
| **UD selected set** | selected set ל-usage decision (רק קודים רלוונטיים). |
| **Selected Set in Same Plant** | רק selected set ספציפי-מפעל. |
| **Print sample drawing instr. immed.** | הדפסה מיידית של sample-drawing ביצירת lot (פרק 10). |
| **Print Insp. instruction immediately** | הדפסה מיידית של הוראת בדיקה. |
| **Display detailed notifications** | חלון עם סיבות כשל הדפסה. |
| **Recording view** | אפשרויות לתצוגת רישום התוצאות. |
| **Notification type** | סוג ה-notification בפגמים (יצירה אוטומטית; פרק 12). |
| **One Q-notification per insp. lot** | notification אחד לכל ה-lot (במקום לכל פגם). |
| **Task list usage** | מזהה routing/recipe. הקצו usage 890. |
| **Control key** | ברירת מחדל ל-material specification. |
| **Activity** | מספר פעולה לברירת מחדל ל-material specification. |
| **Opr. short text** | טקסט קצר של הפעולה. |

**תחזוקת Inspection Lot Origins והקצאה:** יש להקצות את ה-type ל-origin. ניתן מספר types ל-origin אחד, אך לא type אחד ל-origins שונים. אי אפשר להוסיף origin חדש (טבלאות ב-SAP namespace). ל-SAP IMG • Quality Management • Quality Inspection • Inspection Lot Creation • Maintain Inspection Lot Origins and Assign Inspection Types (Figure 3.74). טור LO = origin, ‏No = טווח המספרים (כל ה-types באותו origin עם אותו טווח), ‏TLT "Q" = inspection plan. בחרו LO 89, ‏Inspection Types for the Origin, צרו InspType 8901 (ל-89 כבר 89 ו-8914).

**הגדרת ברירות מחדל:** ל-SAP IMG • Quality Management • Quality Inspection • Inspection Lot Creation • Define Default Values for Inspection Types. בחרו 8901, ‏Details (Figure 3.75) — השדות מ-2.1.

**הערת יועץ:** config new-type — ארבעה-שלבים: task-list-usage → maintain-inspection-type → הקצאת-type ל-origin → default-values. מנקודת-מבט-מעשית, type פעיל = lot נוצר-אחרי-אירוע גם-בלי-plan. יועץ מנוסה מקפיד על-הרצף — כל-שלב תלוי-בקודם (usage לפני-type, type לפני-origin-assignment). ההבחנה origin (קטגוריית-אירוע, קבוע) מול-type (וריאנט, מותאם). הבנת-ארבעת-השלבים חיונית — שרשרת-תצורה שלמה, חוליה-חסרה = type-לא-עובד.

sections.title: Master Data Setup
sections.en: 3.5.2 Master Data Setup Access the screen in Figure 3.76 for material RM17 and plant 1710 (Transaction MM02), and assign the newly created inspection type 8901. In addition, notice that the previ- ously assigned inspection type 89 is also activated. You’ll see how these two inspection types become available while creating a manual inspection lot. Be sure to select the Active checkbox for both inspection types (89 and 8901); otherwise, these won’t be available during inspection lot creation. Figure 3.77 shows the inspection plan of material RM17 and plant 1710 (Transaction QP01). Here, you assign the newly created usage 890 and set the status of the inspec- tion plan to 4 Released (General). The system saves this inspection plan as Group 8 and Group Counter 2. Although not shown here, you need to ensure that you completely maintain the inspection plan as part of your master data maintenance, which was cov- ered in detail in Chapter 2. This completes the minimal master data that you need to maintain to put the newly created inspection type to use. The next section covers the business process. © 189 3.5 New Inspection Types Figure 3.76 Inspection Setup Data for Inspection Type Figure 3.77 Inspection Plan: Header Details 3 Quality Inspection 190
sections.he:
Figure 3.76 (Transaction MM02, חומר RM17, מפעל 1710) — הקצו type 8901; גם 89 פעיל. סמנו Active לשניהם (אחרת לא זמינים).
Figure 3.77 (Transaction QP01) — הקצו usage 890, ‏status 4 Released (General). נשמר כ-Group 8, ‏Group Counter 2. תחזקו את ה-plan במלואו (פרק 2).

הקמת-נתוני-האב: ניגשים למסך (Transaction-MM02) לחומר-RM17 ו-plant-1710, ומקצים את-ה-inspection-type החדש 8901; שימו-לב שה-inspection-type 89 שהוקצה-קודם גם-הוא-פעיל. שני-ה-types יהיו-זמינים בעת-יצירת-inspection-lot ידני. חובה לסמן את-תיבת-ה-Active לשני-ה-types (89 ו-8901) — אחרת לא-יהיו-זמינים ביצירת-lot. כמו-כן, ב-inspection-plan של-החומר יש-לוודא task-list-usage תואם. עבור-היועץ, שני-מלכודות-קלאסיות כאן: הראשונה — ה-Active-checkbox: הקצאת-type במאסטר בלי-סימון-Active נראית-תקינה אך-ה-type פשוט-לא-מופיע ביצירת-lot (תקלה-שקטה מתסכלת); השנייה — ה-task-list-usage: ה-plan חייב-לשאת usage תואם ל-type החדש, אחרת ה-lot נוצר בלי-plan (אין-מאפיינים, אין-results). ההבחנה בין-הקצאה (ה-type-מופיע-במאסטר) להפעלה (Active מסומן) דקה-אך-קריטית. שני-types פעילים לאותו-origin (89+8901) יוצרים popup-בחירה ביצירה-ידנית — התנהגות-רצויה כאן (המשתמש-בוחר את-סוג-הבדיקה). הבנת-הקמת-האב חיונית — היא-החוליה שמחברת את-התצורה (3.5.1) לתהליך (3.5.3), ורוב-כשלי-ה-'type-לא-עובד' נעוצים-בה. יועץ מנוסה בונה checklist: type-מוקצה, Active-מסומן, plan-עם-usage-תואם — שלושתם, תמיד.

**הערת יועץ:** master-data new-type — MM02: הקצאת-8901 + ⚠️ Active-checkbox לשני-ה-types (בלעדיו — לא-מופיע ביצירת-lot, תקלה-שקטה!). מנקודת-מבט-מעשית, מלכודת-שנייה: plan חייב task-list-usage תואם (אחרת lot בלי-מאפיינים). יועץ מנוסה: checklist — מוקצה, Active, usage-תואם. ההבחנה הקצאה מול-הפעלה (Active). שני-types פעילים = popup-בחירה (רצוי). הבנת-האב חיונית — רוב-כשלי-'type-לא-עובד' כאן.

sections.title: Business Process
sections.en: 3.5.3 Business Process To manually create a new inspection lot, use Transaction QA01 or follow menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Quality Inspection  Inspection Lot Processing  Create. Figure 3.78 shows the Create Inspection Lot Manually: Init screen. Enter “RM17” for Material and “1710” for Plant, and when you enter the inspection lot origin (Insp. Lot Origin) as “89”, the system opens a popup that contains the two inspection lots that you assigned to this material in the previous step. Choose InspType 8901 from the list, which leads to the screen in Figure 3.79. Figure 3.78 New Inspection Type 8901 Figure 3.79 Inspection Type 8901 © 191 3.5 New Inspection Types Figure 3.79 shows the inspection type 8901 of inspection lot origin 89. Notice that the inspection lot number also begins with the number 89, and, in this case, the inspection lot number is 890000000356. Choose the Inspection Specifications tab, which shows the automatic assignment of Usage 890.
sections.he:
ליצירה ידנית: Transaction QA01 או Logistics • Quality Management • Quality Inspection • Inspection Lot Processing • Create. Figure 3.78 — הזינו Material "RM17", ‏Plant "1710", ‏Insp. Lot Origin "89" — חלון עם שני ה-types. בחרו InspType 8901 (Figure 3.79). מספר ה-lot מתחיל ב-89 (890000000356). בלשונית Inspection Specifications — הקצאת Usage 890 אוטומטית.

התהליך-העסקי: ליצירת-inspection-lot חדש ידנית משתמשים ב-Transaction-QA01 או-menu-path (Logistics • Quality-Management • Quality-Inspection • Inspection-Lot-Processing • Create). במסך-Create-Inspection-Lot-Manually מזינים Material=RM17, Plant=1710, וכשמזינים Insp.-Lot-Origin=89, המערכת פותחת popup עם-שני-ה-inspection-types שהוקצו-לחומר; בוחרים InspType-8901 מהרשימה. עבור-היועץ, זרימת-היצירה-הידנית ממחישה את-מבנה-origin-מול-type: ה-origin (89) הוא-קטגוריית-האירוע (בדיקה-ידנית/אחרת), וה-types תחתיו (89, 8901) הם-הווריאנטים — ה-popup מציג את-כל-ה-types הפעילים של-אותו-origin לבחירה. ההבחנה בין-origin (קבוע, מובנה-במערכת, קובע-מנגנון) ל-type (מותאם, נגזר-מ-origin, קובע-התנהגות-ספציפית) היא-הליבה-המושגית של-כל-פרק-3.5. לאחר-הבחירה, ה-lot נוצר עם-ה-plan המתאים (דרך-ה-task-list-usage) ומוכן-ל-results-recording רגיל. הבנת-התהליך חיונית — הוא-מוכיח שהשרשרת-כולה (תצורה→אב→תהליך) עובדת: ה-type-החדש זמין, נבחר, ומייצר lot-תקין. יועץ מנוסה מדגים ללקוח בדיוק-את-הזרימה-הזו כ-acceptance-test של-ה-type-החדש, כולל-וידוא שה-plan נמשך-נכון וה-characteristics מופיעים.

**הערת יועץ:** תהליך new-type — QA01 ידני: material+plant+origin-89 → popup עם-ה-types הפעילים → בחירת-8901. מנקודת-מבט-מעשית, ה-popup מציג כל-types-של-אותו-origin. יועץ מנוסה מריץ את-הזרימה כ-acceptance-test: type-זמין, plan-נמשך, characteristics-מופיעים. ההבחנה origin (מנגנון) מול-type (התנהגות) — ליבת-הפרק. הבנת-התהליך חיונית — מוכיח שהשרשרת תצורה→אב→תהליך עובדת. הדגמה-ללקוח בדיוק-כך.

sections.title: Inspection Lot Processing
sections.en: 3.5.4 Inspection Lot Processing Access the screen in Figure 3.80 using Transaction QA32, which is the inspection lot worklist and which you can use for inspection processing, such as results recording or making usage decisions. On the parameter selection screen, you’ll only find Insp. Lot Origin, but no provision to enter an inspection type. For this, first choose Display/Hide Dynamic Selections, and then in the Inspection Lot folder that you see on the left side of the screen, choose Inspection Type by double-clicking it. This brings up the provision of Inspection Type that you see on the right side of the screen. Enter inspection type “8901”, and choose Execute (not shown) to go to the screen in Figure 3.81. Figure 3.80 Inspection Lots: Initial Screen Figure 3.81 shows an inspection lot worklist that contains two inspection lots with Insp. Type (inspection type) 8901. Here, you can choose an inspection lot, record its results, record defects, or record a usage decision. 3 Quality Inspection 192 Figure 3.81 Inspection Lots: Worklist Note Refer to Chapter 18 on reporting, which also covers inspection lot worklists (Transac- tion QA32). The next section covers the configuration basics of quality planning and quality inspection.
sections.he:
Transaction QA32 — ה-worklist (Figure 3.80). במסך, רק Insp. Lot Origin (ללא type). בחרו Display/Hide Dynamic Selections, ובתיקיית Inspection Lot לחיצה כפולה על Inspection Type — מופיע שדה Inspection Type. הזינו "8901", ‏Execute (Figure 3.81). שני lots עם type 8901 — ניתן רישום, פגמים, או usage decision.
**הערה:** פרק 18 (worklists, ‏QA32).

עיבוד-ה-inspection-lot: ניגשים למסך דרך-Transaction-QA32 — worklist של-inspection-lots לעיבוד (results-recording, usage-decisions). במסך-בחירת-הפרמטרים מופיע רק-Insp.-Lot-Origin, ללא-שדה-inspection-type; לכן בוחרים תחילה Display/Hide-Dynamic-Selections, ואז-בתיקיית-Inspection-Lot משמאל בוחרים Inspection-Type בלחיצה-כפולה — וכך-נפתחת האפשרות לסנן לפי-type. עבור-היועץ, זהו-טיפ-תפעולי חשוב ל-QA32 (טרנזקציית-העבודה המרכזית של-הבודקים): מסך-הבחירה הסטנדרטי מציג-origin בלבד, ומי-שיצר-type-מותאם (8901) לא-ימצא איך-לסנן-אליו — עד-שיכיר את-ה-Dynamic-Selections. ההבחנה בין-שדות-הבחירה הסטנדרטיים (מוצגים-תמיד) ל-dynamic-selections (מאגר-שדות מורחב שנפתח-לפי-דרישה) היא-דפוס-כללי ב-SAP-reporting — רלוונטי להרבה-טרנזקציות-worklist. לאחר-הוספת-הסינון, הבודק בונה-worklist ממוקד ל-type-הספציפי — חיוני כשה-type-החדש נועד-בדיוק להפרדת-זרימות. ניתן-לשמור את-הבחירה כ-variant לשימוש-חוזר. הבנת-עיבוד-ה-worklist חיונית — QA32 הוא-'שולחן-העבודה' היומי של-הבודק, וסינון-נכון בו קובע את-יעילות-העבודה. יועץ מנוסה יוצר variants שמורים לכל-צוות (לפי-types/plants שלהם) ומצרפם להדרכת-המשתמשים.

**הערת יועץ:** lot-processing (QA32) — worklist מציג רק-origin; לסינון-לפי-type: Display/Hide-Dynamic-Selections → Inspection-Lot → Inspection-Type. מנקודת-מבט-מעשית, טיפ-חיוני — בלעדיו לא-מוצאים את-ה-type-המותאם. יועץ מנוסה שומר variant לכל-צוות (types/plants שלהם). ההבחנה שדות-סטנדרטיים מול-dynamic-selections (דפוס-כללי ב-SAP-reporting). QA32 = שולחן-העבודה של-הבודק. הבנת-ה-worklist חיונית — סינון-נכון = יעילות-יומית.

sections.title: Configuration Basics: Quality Planning and Quality Inspection
sections.en: 3.6 Configuration Basics: Quality Planning and Quality Inspection This section covers configuration basics of quality planning and quality inspection. Note If you see a few configuration objects not covered in this chapter while navigating the configuration menu paths in quality planning or quality inspection, don’t worry. We’ve covered them in this book where it makes sense to maintain a logical link between con- figuration objects, assigning them to master data, and showing their impacts on busi- ness processes. Similarly, several configuration objects—for example, status profile or fields selection—apply to various business processes. To avoid repetition, we cover them once in this book, and you can apply them to your relevant business processes. We do, however, provide extensive cross-referencing to help you quickly find relevant details in this book.
sections.he:
סעיף זה מכסה יסודות תצורה.
**הערה:** אם תראו אובייקטי תצורה שלא כוסו — הם כוסו במקום ההגיוני. אובייקטים החלים על תהליכים רבים (status profile, ‏fields selection) מכוסים פעם אחת עם cross-referencing.

סעיף-זה מכסה את-יסודות-התצורה של-quality-planning ו-quality-inspection. הערה: אם-נתקלים באובייקטי-תצורה שלא-כוסו-בפרק-זה בניווט-בתפריטי-התצורה — הם-כוסו-בספר במקום-שבו-הגיוני לשמר קשר-לוגי בין-אובייקט-התצורה, הקצאתו-לנתוני-אב, והשפעתו על-תהליכים. עבור-היועץ, סעיף-3.6 הוא-'חדר-המכונות' של-כל-מה-שנראה-בפרק: כל-התנהגות שנצפתה (מתי-נוצר-lot, איך-מוערכת-תוצאה, אילו-קטלוגים-זמינים) נשלטת מהתצורה-כאן. ההבחנה המבנית בין-שלוש-רמות-התצורה מהותית: client-level (הגדרות-על גלובליות — versioning, multiple-specs), plant-level (ברירות-מחדל תפעוליות לכל-plant שבו-QM-פעיל), ואובייקטי-quality-planning/inspection ספציפיים (defect-classes, catalogs, quality-score, follow-up-actions). סדר-הקריאה הנכון: client → plant → אובייקטים — מהכללי לפרטי. עיקרון-הספר — לקשור-תצורה→אב→תהליך — הוא-גם-העיקרון-המתודולוגי הנכון ליועץ: לעולם-אל-תגדיר-אובייקט-תצורה בלי-להבין איפה-הוא-פוגש נתוני-אב ואיזה-תהליך הוא-משנה. הבנת-מפת-התצורה חיונית — היא-שמבדילה יועץ-מיישם (מגדיר-לפי-מדריך) מיועץ-אדריכל (מבין-את-שרשרת-ההשפעה). הסעיפים-הבאים: client-settings, plant-settings, quality-planning, ו-quality-inspection.

**הערת יועץ:** config-basics — חדר-המכונות: כל-התנהגות שנצפתה נשלטת-מכאן. מנקודת-מבט-מעשית, שלוש-רמות: client (גלובלי — versioning, multiple-specs), plant (ברירות-מחדל per-plant), אובייקטים (catalogs, quality-score, follow-ups). יועץ מנוסה קורא מהכללי-לפרטי + לעולם קושר תצורה→אב→תהליך. ההבחנה יועץ-מיישם (לפי-מדריך) מול-אדריכל (שרשרת-השפעה). הבנת-המפה חיונית — הבסיס להבנת-כל-התנהגות. הסעיפים: 3.6.1-3.6.4.

sections.title: Client Settings
sections.en: 3.6.1 Client Settings After a client is created in the SAP system and default settings are transferred, you can customize the settings to each individual client level. To maintain version control, save older versions of master inspection characteristics and inspection methods before add- ing newer versions. You can also leave the remaining options at their default settings. To maintain settings at the client level, follow menu path SAP IMG  Quality Manage- ment  Basic Settings  Maintain Settings at Client Level. Table 3.5 explains some of the fields of Figure 3.82, Figure 3.83, and Figure 3.84, which are part of the same screen. © 193 3.6 Configuration Basics: Quality Planning and Quality Inspection Field Description Replace Master Inspection Character- istic A control function which if selected enables the system to trigger replacement of the master inspection characteristic of the latest ver- sion in the inspection plan and material specification. Replace Inspection Method A control function that if selected enables the system to trigger replacement of the inspection method of the latest version in the inspection plan and material specification. Distribute Inspection Charac. Application Link Enabling (ALE) acts as an interface between SAP and other third-party software or programs. If selected, ALE distributes master inspection characteristic data between the SAP system and third-party QM programs. Distribute Inspection Method If selected, this distributes the inspection method between the SAP system and third-party QM programs. Distribute Code Group If selected, this distributes the code group between the SAP system and third-party QM programs. Unplanned Charac- teristics The number range of unplanned or additional master inspection characteristics that you add to an existing inspection lot, prior to its results recording. Chars from Spec./ Config./Batch The number range of unplanned or additional master inspection characteristics that you can add to an existing inspection lot, prior to results recording. Multiple Specs A control function that, when checked, allows the system to valuate the material or inspection lot differently, depending on specific busi- ness requirements. See Section 3.3 on multiple specifications for more information. Highest Quality Score The highest quality score that forms the basis of quality score calcu- lations. It can’t be greater than 100. Lowest Quality Score The lowest quality score that forms the basis of quality score calcula- tions. This score can’t be less than 1. Lower Limit for Good Quality Minimum threshold value for quality supplier scores that meet the company’s quality criteria. Valn Rule for Lot- Based Dyn.Mod. A standard SAP system function module to calculate the valuation mode for an inspection-lot-based dynamic modification rule. BOM Usage The bill of materials (BOM) usage, such as PP01, that automatically integrates with QM. Table 3.5 Client Settings 3 Quality Inspection 194 Figure 3.82 Settings at the Client Level (1/3) Figure 3.83 More QM Settings at Client Level (2/3) © 195 3.6 Configuration Basics: Quality Planning and Quality Inspection If you scroll down the screens shown in Figure 3.82, Figure 3.83, and Figure 3.84, you’ll see options to activate many more QM functionalities as you need. After reading the entire book, revisit Figure 3.83 and Figure 3.84 to gain a better comprehension of the available functionalities. More checkboxes shown in Figure 3.84 belong to audit man- agement and failure mode and effects analysis (FMEA), which we covered in Chapter 18 and Chapter 20, respectively. sections.title: Plant Settings
sections.en: 3.6.2 Plant Settings You can set plant-wise settings, such as inspection characteristics and inspection meth- ods, physical-sample location, report types, print control, and account assignment parameters. When the system is unable to find specific master data in quality planning, it refers to the information or settings maintained in the plant settings. You need to maintain plant-specific settings for each plant in which QM is active. To maintain settings at the plant level, follow menu path SAP IMG  Quality Manage- ment  Basic Settings  Maintain Settings at Plant Level. In the screen that appears, choose plant 1710, and you’ll see the following five tabs, which we’ll discuss in the fol- lowing sections:  Basic Data  Insp. Lot Creation  Results Recording  InspLot Completion  General Settings Basic Data With the Master Insp. Charcs with History and Inspection Methods with History check- boxes selected (see Figure 3.85), when you create or change master inspection charac- teristics and inspection methods, the system automatically assigns versions to them. Doing so preserves necessary historical information about the characteristic or inspec- tion method for record keeping. Figure 3.85 Basic Data Settings at Plant Level Inspection Lot Creation Table 3.6 explains the fields of Figure 3.86. © 197 3.6 Configuration Basics: Quality Planning and Quality Inspection Field Description Enter Container at GR Selecting this option makes it either optional or mandatory to define the number of physical containers used during inspection. See Chapter 10 on sample management, where we put this option to use. InspTypeForInspStock A special inspection type 0800 is assigned here to ensure that the system is able to create inspection lots for materi- als that were previously in quality inspection stock (but without QM active) but will now have to undergo quality inspection using QM. See Chapter 4, where we put this option to use. Order Type: Ind. Settlement This QM order type collects quality-related costs incurred on an individual basis. Order Type: Coll. Settlement This QM order type collects quality-related costs incurred on a collective basis. For example, instead of accumulating all costs for QM activities on one QM order, define a cost collec- tor here. Lot Inspection This is the highest plant-level sampling procedure assigned to an inspection lot. A sampling procedure is a defined way in which the sample of an inspection lot is calculated. A few sampling proce- dures are fixed sample, percentage sample, 100% inspec- tion, and using a sampling scheme. Free Inspection Pts The sampling procedure for free inspection points. Plant Maintenance A special sampling procedure for PM. You can provide a default value for it here. See Chapter 7 on QM integration with PM. Sample Management A sample management procedure in which a company- owned or competitor’s product samples are analyzed. See Chapter 10, where we put this option to use. Characteristic Weighting Default settings used by the system when you don’t specify a characteristic weight when you create a lot inspection. Defect Class Defects are classified as critical, major, and minor. The sys- tem uses the default value when you don’t enter the required value during defects recording. Table 3.6 Inspection Lot Creation 3 Quality Inspection 198 Figure 3.86 Settings at the Plant Level Results Recording Choose the Results Recording tab in the screen in Figure 3.86 to go to the screen in Figure 3.87. Table 3.7 explains the fields shown here. Field Details Summarized Recording for n=1 Always shows summarized results for all inspection lots during evaluation and reporting. Limit Marginal Classes Considers plausibility factors for quantitative characteris- tics. Immediate Creation of Change Docs This immediately creates change documents for all the changes made during results recording. Additional Decimal Places While the SAP system uses accurate internal calculations for statistical purposes, the value defined here allows a user to display the same value while executing QM reports. Table 3.7 Results Recording © 199 3.6 Configuration Basics: Quality Planning and Quality Inspection Sample Start Value Default start value that is internally assigned by the SAP system when multiple samples of an inspection lot are present. Plausibility Factor (%) A percentage value that the system uses in combination with upper and lower limits of quantitative characteris- tics. For example, a 200% plausibility factor means that a characteristic with an upper tolerance limit of 100 has a plausibility limit of 200 (twice), and those with a lower tolerance limit of 50 will have a plausibility limit of 25 (half). Sample Interval The default start value is internally assigned by the SAP system when multiple samples of a physical sample are present. Recording Configuration A sequence that occurs on completion of results record- ing of an inspection. An Automatic close option closes the characteristic as soon as the results are entered and the characteristic is valuated. MessageCat.DecimalPlaces Occurs when there are calculations involved. For example, in calculated master inspection characteristics, this field controls whether the system issues an error, warning, or informational message when an overflow in calculated values occurs. Insp. Pt. Field Combination Default value the system uses if it’s unable to find the required inspection point for an inspection lot. Partial Lot Assignment. A default value the system uses to look for supported and unsupported partial inspection lots. This value has lower precedence when the system is able to find a relevant value in the task list of the material. When it doesn’t, it looks for values in this field (plant level) and functions for both supported and unsupported partial lots. Plant The value given here can be used as a reference to another plant. For example, if plant 2200 needs to refer to plant 1000 for codes, a code group, or a selected set, then a Value 1000 must be assigned to Plant 2200. Selected Set Together with the plant value, you can use the selected set value as a reference to another selected set. Field Details Table 3.7 Results Recording (Cont.) 3 Quality Inspection 200 Figure 3.87 Results Recording in Plant Settings Choose the InspLot Completion tab shown in Figure 3.87 to get to the screen in Figure 3.88. Inspection Lot Completion Table 3.8 explains the fields of Figure 3.88. We recommend that you engage your man- agement accounting or controlling resource to help you decide which values go in these fields, which will eventually have costing or financial impacts. Code Default code proposed by the system when it’s unable to find the code in the inspection point. Code group A code group automatically suggested for evaluating the inspection point. Field Details Table 3.7 Results Recording (Cont.) © 201 3.6 Configuration Basics: Quality Planning and Quality Inspection Figure 3.88 Inspection Lot Completion in Plant Settings Choose General Settings in Figure 3.88. Field Details Controlling Area Default controlling area to go with the plant value. Cost Center: Scrap Default cost center for scrapping the material during a usage decision. Cost Center: Destroyed Default cost center for destroying the material during a usage decision. Stor.Loc. for Reserves Default storage location to move material or reserve stock during a usage decision. Delay Time for Skip Lot An inspection lot must wait a minimum time (enter value in this field) before the system considers it for a SKIP inspection lot automatic usage decision. Waiting Time (Hrs) Waiting time, in hours, before an automatic usage deci- sion begins. Waiting Time (Mins) Together with the number of hours, a waiting time, in minutes, before the system makes an automatic usage decision. Table 3.8 Inspection Lot Completion 3 Quality Inspection 202 General Settings The system uses the value (in days) that you enter in the Selection Period field to calcu- late the starting date of the selected time period. You can override this default setting while executing a worklist or report. Although the SAP S/4HANA system delivers standard quality planning settings and standards right out of the box, you need to evaluate them to see if they fit your busi- ness requirements. If they don’t, you can modify the existing standards or create new ones.
