sections.title: Management of Changes
sections.en: 13.4 Management of Changes 13.4 Management of Changes Management of changes is a highly flexible and fully auditable process in SAP S/4HANA for requesting, monitoring, and implementing changes. For example, a change request can introduce a new chemical in the production process or modify operating condi- tions of a piece of equipment. This change management tool can be used to do the fol- lowing:  Automate identification of risk experts, approvers, and subject-matter experts.  Enable employees and contractors to request changes easily.  Streamline the change process and drive forward consistency and standardization.  Provide workflow and status management to ensure task completion. A change request is a requirement for an adjustment to be made within a company, a plant, or a process. When creating a change request, you first select the type of changes involved. This change request type defines the details of a change request to be queried—for example, related objects, activities, and questionnaires. A change request can be used by anyone in the company or in the plant to report an incident or a need for any improvement. Figure 13.43 Change Request Types in the Configuration Menu Path 13 Engineering Change Management 612 The lifecycle of a change request starts as soon as the change request is created. It’s based on the change request’s status network. This lifecycle can be managed by setting the appropriate status. Further, you can also automate status changes so that the status of the change request changes automatically when a certain activity has reached a cer- tain status. To configure a new change request type in SAP S/4HANA, follow menu path SAP IMG  Cross-Application Components  Management of Change. Figure 13.43 shows the configuration node for Management of Change. As you can see, several of these areas were already discussed in various sections and chapters of this book. For example, Chapter 2 discussed catalogs and code groups, Chapter 3 discussed digital signatures, and Section 13.1.1 discussed status profile maintenance (user status); hence, these and associated topics aren’t repeated here. Choose Define Change Request Types, shown in Figure 13.43, and the screen in Figure 13.44 appears. Figure 13.44 Change Request Type Figure 13.44 shows a new change request type (CR Type) MOC with the description MOC Change Request. Later, you’ll see that the system prompts the user to choose the change request’s description when creating a new change request. Other details, such as first creating and then assigning number range intervals (see Figure 13.43 again) for a change request, as well as for activities, are shown. The left side offers more options to customize each change request type, such as assigning the previously defined digital signature and automating the status change when a specific status of a change request has been reached. Access the screen shown in Figure 13.45 via the Create Change Request app. As you can see, the system offers the option to choose a change request’s description and not the change request type. Choose MOC Change Request, and the screen in Figure 13.46 appears. © 613 13.4 Management of Changes Figure 13.46 shows the partial display of the change request in which relevant details such as the object type, object reference, and date can be maintained. Notice that the status of the change request here is In Preparation. Figure 13.45 Create Change Request Figure 13.46 Object Information and Dates in Change Request It’s important to understand how the predecessor-successor relationship for a status network works in a change request. Table 13.2 shows that when a change request’s status is In Preparation, the next and the only available status is Submitted. When a change request is submitted, not only is the change request’s status automatically updated, but with a Submitted status, the next four (successor) statuses become available: Awaiting, Incomplete, Rejected, Not Applicable, and On Hold. As soon as the change request attains one of these five statuses, the system makes available the corresponding successors or next statuses, as shown in the Current Status column in Table 13.2. 13 Engineering Change Management 614 Current Status Description Possible Actions to Trigger Status Change New Status In Preparation Draft version is being created by a reporter. Save and submit Submitted Submitted The change request is sub- mitted by the reporter and can now be checked and reviewed. Review Complete Awaiting Approval Resubmit (Incom- plete) Incomplete Reject Rejected Not applicable Not applicable Hold On Hold Awaiting Approval All reviews have been final- ized, and the decision to go ahead with the change pro- cess or to reject the change can be made. Approve Approved Resubmit (Incom- plete) Incomplete Reject Rejected Not applicable Not applicable Hold On Hold Approved The change has been approved. Release and Cre- ate Activities In Process Hold On Hold In Process The change process is ongo- ing. The assigned activities are being processed. Permanently Close Change Request Closed Reject Rejected Hold On Hold Closed The change is completely processed. Reopen In Process Incomplete There is information missing in the submitted change request. Save and Submit Submitted Rejected The change is rejected—for example, because the change isn’t relevant any- more. Undo Rejection Status before Rejection Table 13.2 Status Network for Change Requests © 615 13.4 Management of Changes Scroll down in the screen in Figure 13.46 so that the screen in Figure 13.47 appears, which consists of a few text boxes to describe the required or desired changes and any proposed solutions. Here, it’s also possible to categorize the impact that a product or the process will have if the suggested change isn’t implemented. Scroll down in the screen in Figure 13.47, and the screen in Figure 13.48 appears. Figure 13.47 Change Definition in Change Request Figure 13.48 shows the Object Type Material and the associated Object (material num- ber in this case) that can be selected from the dropdown. Although this example only shows material as an option type to choose from, there are several other object types that can be made available in the dropdown and via the configuration option (refer to Figure 13.44). In the lower half of the screen, the Attachments and Links option enables On Hold The change process is stopped—for example, due to a missing budget—but it’s planned to recommence at a later point in time. Remove Hold Status before Set- ting Hold Not Applicable The requested change isn’t suitable for an official change process. Reopen Submitted Current Status Description Possible Actions to Trigger Status Change New Status Table 13.2 Status Network for Change Requests (Cont.) 13 Engineering Change Management 616 web links or other attachments that can be made part of a change request. Scroll down, and the screen in Figure 13.49 will appear. Figure 13.48 Related Objects in a Change Request Figure 13.49 shows the people or the stakeholders involved in enabling a change request; they can be reviewers, approvers, or business analysts. It’s important to note that the business partners must be previously created and can then be assigned here. If the digital signature is configured and assigned to a change request, then the option to digitally sign it is also available here. A digital signature will trigger when a change request has attained a specific status in which the stakeholder must digitally sign the change request to confirm the new status. Figure 13.49 People Involved and Digital Signature in a Change Request Save the change request by choosing Save and Submit located at the bottom-right side of the screen, and the screen in Figure 13.50 appears. A change request can also be saved as a draft and can be submitted later. Figure 13.50 shows the header of the change request, which now has the change request number 1000000001. Figure 13.51 shows the activities associated with this change request; in this example, the change request needs to be approved. Notice that though the change request num- ber is 1000000001, the activity number is 700000002. Each change number can have © 617 13.4 Management of Changes multiple activities, and every activity is uniquely identified by its own number. To make changes to a change number, choose Edit located at the top-left side of Figure 13.50. Figure 13.50 Change Request 1000000001 with In Preparation Status Figure 13.51 Activities in a Change Request Access Figure 13.52 via the Manage Change Request app, and you’ll see that the status of change request 1000000001 is Submitted. Other available statuses are shown via the dropdown, thus making it easier for the relevant stakeholders to quickly attend to change requests that need any subsequent action. Figure 13.52 Manage Change Requests Access the screen shown in Figure 13.53 via the Manage Change Activities app to set var- ious available filters so that the app only displays the relevant information, as well as 13 Engineering Change Management 618 display additional columns. You can also navigate to the detailed screen of an individ- ual activity of a change request. Figure 13.53 Manage Change Activities Figure 13.54 shows the Change Requests Dashboard app that provides complete and comprehensive visibility into all the change requests made so far and their statuses. If needed, users can navigate to the detailed screen by choosing the forward arrow located at the far-right side of the screen. The app shows a combination of tabular and graphical combinations for easier comprehension. Figure 13.54 Change Request Dashboard © 619

sections.title: Summary
sections.en: 13.5 Summary Note Visit http://s-prs.co/v492401 to learn more about management of changes in SAP S/4HANA. Be sure to choose the relevant or correct SAP S/4HANA version so that SAP Help brings up the required information. 13.5 Summary This chapter covered the necessary configuration needed for successfully integrating engineering change management with business processes. The user status (status profile) has greater relevance in the change master. The engineering change manage- ment information system provides in-depth and comprehensive details of all the changes made and enables the user to select status-based information for further necessary action. Newer master data change management tools to manage changes in SAP S/4HANA are change record, engineering record, and management of changes. The next chapter covers audit management in SAP S/4HANA. ©

sections.title: Overview
sections.en: 14.1 Overview Figure 14.1 shows an overview of the steps involved in audit management. Figure 14.1 Audit Management Set up audits within audit plan Create or assign question list to audit Print audit with question list Perform actual/ physical audit Enter info on audit’s questions Valuate and complete audit Set up audit plan Enter corrective/ preventive action for failed questions 14 Audit Management 622 During the audit planning stage, you prepare the necessary question lists and audit cri- teria, depending on the relevant standards, regulations, or rules of the auditable area. You can set up an audit plan and define the periodic schedule, taking into consider- ation the scope, audit object, and dates of the audits. When the audit is part of a pro- gram, you need to set up the audit plan and any relevant audit subplans. The subplans should contain information about the plan, a general description, and a validity period. This is often the case for obligatory audits, in which case, we recommend that you use the audit program. The audit program allows you to plan the type, scope, and fre- quency of audits, as well as the resource requirements. You can create an audit pro- gram by hierarchically structuring audit plans (Figure 14.1 1), which also allows you to combine certain types of audits. From a business perspective, it makes sense to group together an environment audit and health and safety audit, for example. During an actual audit, you collect evidence and record the findings. Prepare or set up the individual audits 2 by determining the question lists 3, identifying the partners involved, and preparing the required documents. This step involves the following actions: releasing the audit in the system, inviting the participants, providing the doc- uments, and examining the audit object with regard to the criteria, or performing interviews with the relevant stakeholders. Although audit management is designed for online, paperless applications, SAP sup- ports exporting and importing audit data and audit question lists 4 to allow for offline and mobile auditing through a standard XML interface. The XML file can then be trans- ferred to a Microsoft Excel file and loaded onto the auditor’s laptop so that the auditor can perform the actual audit 5 on this data. The auditor can then upload the file via the standard XML interface into audit management, where the auditor can process the remaining steps or complete the audit process. Based on the evidence entered in the previous step 6, the system valuates the ques- tions based on the question configuration settings (set up to meet your company’s business rules), so the system rates and automatically grades an audit object. Because you’re valuating the audit object, this stage is sometimes referred to as a grade audit or a grade object. The overall assessment and grading for the audit object is determined on the basis of the valuations of all items that have actually been assessed. To consoli- date the valuations across several hierarchy levels of the question list, the system uses the degrees of fulfillment or deviation from each hierarchy level for calculation in the standard SAP S/4HANA system. The valuation on the supreme hierarchy level is then used to grade the audit object. In the rating profile, you determine the degrees of fulfillment that must be achieved for separate audit objects. In this step, you create an audit report, which contains all important administrative data related to the audit, including comments, results, and the corrective/preventive actions taken 7. The audit report is an official document. © 623

sections.title: Setting Up Audit Objects
sections.en: 14.2 Setting Up Audit Objects After the assessment, you can create a preliminary audit report, which you can then use to discuss the findings, corrective actions, and overall results of the audit. The audit can then be signed (physically or using a digital signature), created, and distributed. The system represents the signature by the status of the audit. If the signature itself must be documented and verified, you can scan the signed report into the system and attach it to the audit 8. During an audit, if the auditors detect that there are inadmissible deviations, dangers, or room for improvement, they can note their findings and make recommendations, determine the need for a subsequent audit, or create corrective or preventive actions for the relevant items of the audit question list. The last step of audit management focuses on monitoring the outstanding actions and finalizing the audit report. Note We recommend that you also read Chapter 16 on failure mode and effects analysis (FMEA), which highly overlaps with the functionality and basics of audit management. In fact, FMEA is a specialized form of audit that finds greater application in the auto- motive industry. 14.2 Setting Up Audit Objects The following audit objects are used within audit management:  Audit plan  Audit  Question list  Question

sections.title: Set Up the Audit Plan
sections.en: 14.2.1 Set Up the Audit Plan An audit plan is used to keep an overview of the audits that the company undertakes and have them organized in a logical way. An audit plan is also known as an audit pro- gram. In the audit plan, you define the schema in the form of an annual schedule by taking into consideration the scope, object, and date of the audits. An audit plan can contain several subordinate audit plans and links to audits. You can access the audit management work area from Transaction PLMD_Audit or menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Audit Management  Audit Management. The resulting screen, shown in Figure 14.2, divides the entire audit management work area into three distinct sections. In the top-left work area (known as the structure tree), the system provides options to create new objects, such as an audit plan, audit, or 14 Audit Management 624 question list. You can also copy one audit item to another, delete an item within audit management, or even look up specific information. All of these options are available via the New icon’s dropdown list available at the top-left side of Figure 14.2. Figure 14.2 Audit Management Workbench The right side of the screen (known as the detail screen) is blank unless you’re already working on a specific audit object. The lower-left side (known as the worklist/template area) shows the audits or other objects that you’ve worked on in the recent past and is available in the work area’s history. To make more space in the work area, you can hide the details shown on the lower-left side of the screen by choosing Close (the blue cross—hidden behind the dropdown). Choose the New icon in Figure 14.2 to create a new audit plan, question list, or audit either from scratch or using a template. Choose Audit Plan from the dropdown list, and the system brings up the screen shown in Figure 14.3. Here, you see the basic data view of an audit plan. On the right side of the screen, enter “NSA” in the Audit Plan field (for the rest of this chapter, we’ll be using the audit plan NSA as an example to denote new suppliers’ audits), and enter its description. Notice the additional icons next to the Audit Plan field that enable you to add additional notes, attachments, or even web links for reference and records purposes. The option to attach documents or notes is also generally available while you’re creating all items of audit management. Similarly, you can keep an eye on the alerts and messages that are available at the top-right side. © 625 14.2 Setting Up Audit Objects Figure 14.3 Audit Plan Double-click the message icon, and details of the message appear at the bottom of the same screen. We suggest that you take time out to explore the tools and menus. Enter the valid from and valid to dates of your audit plan. At this time, the system status of the audit plan is Being Created. You need to release the audit plan before you can actu- ally begin working with it. In the Texts tab, you can incorporate more details about the audit plan, including add- ing a description and notes. You can even upload (and download) the content from some other data source, such as another drive on your laptop, and incorporate it in either the description or note areas of the audit plan. This is possible when you choose the relevant upload or download options. Note The option to enter various types of texts is generally available in the Texts tab of all items of audit management. Choose the Contact Person tab in Figure 14.3, and the system brings up the screen shown in Figure 14.4 1. Here, you enter the roles and names of the people who will be part of the audit plan team. You can assign responsibilities to the relevant persons, and then in all subsequent status updates or reporting, information on participants helps in finding whose tasks are pending or overdue, or even which resource/participant is assigned to what task(s). 14 Audit Management 626 Tips and Tricks Use Transaction BP to create or amend business partners (team members) who will be part of the audit management initiative. Choose the Status tab 2. Here, the current status of the audit plan is still in the creation phase. Save your audit plan. The next step is to create an audit. Figure 14.4 Contact Person and Status in Audit Plan

sections.title: Set Up Audit
sections.en: 14.2.2 Set Up Audit The audit (also known as an audit plan within ISO 19011, whereas an audit plan is known as an audit program) describes the audit type and audit triggers, as well as the audit object. The definition of audit objects makes it possible to analyze similar audits to determine best practices or trends. The structure of an audit consists of the following elements: © 627 14.2 Setting Up Audit Objects  Audit plan This is an optional element for reoccurring audits.  Audit This is the object being audited, such as the product or process, audit team, audit type and cause, deadlines, texts, valuation rule, result, or status.  Audit question list The question and/or question list gets assigned to the audit. As soon as you use a question list or create a question list or additional questions, these all are specific to the audit and contain both the question list header and items.  Corrective/preventive actions This is related to audit questions, which contain follow-up actions such as an addi- tional audit, or preventive, corrective, or improvement actions. To set up an audit, right-click audit plan NSA so that the system brings up the option to create an audit (see Figure 14.5). Choose Create and then choose Audit 1. Enter the name of the audit, together with its short description. The system prompts you to select the Audit Type, which can be a system, product, or process audit type available according to your configured objects. Refer to Section 14.6.2 on configuration objects for audit types. Figure 14.5 Audit Setup 14 Audit Management 628 Choose 51 System Audit at Vendor’s Site as the Audit Type 2, and then choose 60 Change of Manufacturing Process as the Audit Trigger. Enter Business Partner “9980000210” and QM System “ISO_9001”. Then, enter the planned start and end dates of the audit in the lower half of the screen. You can update the actual start and end dates of your audit in the bottom half of the screen when you actually start and then complete the audit. Choose the Texts tab in 2 so that you can incorporate more details about the audit, including adding its detailed description and notes. Choose the Result tab in Figure 14.6, and notice that because you’re creating a new audit, the Audit Result area reflects that the system hasn’t assessed the audit yet, nor the audit’s degree of fulfillment, so the fields are all blank. Later, you’ll see how the sys- tem automatically fills up these fields after it calculates the audit results. In the lower half of the screen (the Valuation Specifications area), select the procedure that you want to use as the valuation specification for the audit. For this example, set the valuation Procedure to Valuation Acc. to Fulfillment (Absol., Minimum Result Determines. Figure 14.6 Valuation Specification of Audit Before the system calculates the audit results, it asks the business process owner to assign a rating profile. A rating profile refers to the predefined segregation to valuate whether the audit results should valuate the supplier as, for example, low risk, high risk, or no risk at all. In addition, it’s important to note that you have to define the minimum result that the audit must achieve as 90.0. In other words, it acts a bench- mark to compare actual audit findings with minimum results and enables the system © 629 14.2 Setting Up Audit Objects to conduct Overall Assest. (assessment) to declare findings from the audit as a success or failure. Save your entries. The next step is to create an audit question list or questions.

sections.title: Set Up the Question List/Questions
sections.en: 14.2.3 Set Up the Question List/Questions A question list (also referred to as audit criteria) is usually required to execute an audit, and it stores the criteria against which the audit objects are assessed. Question lists contain the expertise of the auditor regarding the audit area. A question list can be cre- ated as an independent master data object with the purpose of reusing its contents. After you create an audit, you can assign this question list into the audit, which makes it part of the audit. This, however, is optional; you can also create the question list spe- cifically for a particular audit. In Figure 14.7, choose Audit on the left side of the screen. The system brings up the option to create an audit question list/question. Choose Audit Question List/Question 1, and a popup appears. The Hierarchy Prof. (profile) field 2 controls different levels of audit question lists or questions. For example, a question list or a question may have further parts or elements that form its overall structure. With hierarchy control, you can control this, as well as which question, part, or element the system should valuate during an audit valuation. Choose Question; Figure 14.8 shows the valuation details of the question. Figure 14.7 Question List 14 Audit Management 630 Figure 14.8 shows View Selection, which offers the option to maintain details of the question, whereas the Valuation view is the option that you use in the business process of audit management. At this time, you’re maintaining the setup for audit manage- ment, so maintain the question’s details, such as texts and valuation specifications. Choose Valuations Specs to go to the screen in Figure 14.9. Figure 14.8 Basic Data of the Question List Figure 14.9 1 consists of the calculation procedure, as well as the valuation of the ques- tion that you saw while creating the audit. Here, again, the Minimum Result for this question should be 90.0. You can control the weighting that this question can have. For example, a weighting of 2 enables the system to give twice the weight or importance to this question during audit calculation (valuation). Valuation Profile controls whether you can enter the result of the question as a percentage, quantity, or code (also contains either a percentage or valuation on a scale of 1 to 100). A ValuatnProposal (valuation pro- posal) of 90.0 automatically brings this value up for the business user as a default value, which may deviate from the actual audit finding/assessment of this question. Figure 14.9 also shows the dropdown options available for Procedures 2 and ValuatnProfile 3. Note The configuration details of procedures and the valuation profile are explained in Chapter 16. Tips and Tricks If you have a business need to print the audit question list at the time of conducting an actual or physical audit, then while in the audit, choose Print Preview. The system shows the print preview of the entire audit and enables you to print it directly or save it as a PDF file that you can print later. Refer to Figure 14.5 1 to check out the Print Pre- view option available for an audit. © 631

sections.title: Business Processes
sections.en: 14.3 Business Processes You can also create a question list in advance and then assign it when the actual audit is conducted so that the latest and most updated question list applies to the audit. The option to create a question list is available when you first create an audit plan or an audit. To assign an already-created question list to an audit, refer to Figure 14.7 1 and choose Assign Question List. Figure 14.9 Valuation Specifications for Question 14.3 Business Processes Audit management is suitable for a variety of audit usages, and you can easily combine audits where this is possible. The following are some examples in which you can use audit management: 14 Audit Management 632  ISO 9000 (quality management) is a group of standards developed by the Interna- tional Organization for Standardization (ISO), which provides guidance and tools for companies and organizations that want to ensure their products and services con- sistently meet customer requirements and quality consistently improves. It includes audit management, in which organizations must perform internal audits to check how its QM system is working. Audits can be related to systems, processes, or products, as well as FMEA.  Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) is a production and testing practice that helps to ensure a quality product. Many countries have legislations covering GMP proce- dures and guidelines specifically for pharmaceutical and medical device companies to safeguard the health of the patient, as well as produce good quality medicine, medical devices, or active pharmaceutical products.  ISO 14000 (environmental management) is another group of standards from ISO that provides practical tools for companies and organizations looking to identify and control their environmental impact and constantly improve their environmen- tal performance.  ISO 19000 (safety and security management) is a group of standards for geographic information, including concepts, principles of quality, quality assessment, specifica- tions, and metadata standards. ISO 19011 provides guidance on auditing manage- ment systems, the principles of auditing, management of an audit program, and the evaluation of competence of the individuals involved in the audit process. Example Textile, garments, and home furnishing buyers (e.g., Walmart, JCPenney, and the Gap) often require manufacturers to undergo rigorous rounds of multiple audits to ensure the safety and security of textile workers and to meet fire and safety hazard prevention requirements. These buyer-specific audits can be managed in audit management. The business processes in audit management begin with releasing the audit plan for all stakeholders to sign their consent to all elements of the audit plan. This is followed by releasing individual audits as and when they near. On releasing the audit, the auditor can actually start attending to each audit question and let the system valuate each audit question to see if it meets the audit standards or not. If not, then corrective/pre- ventive actions are put in place and their progress monitored. The audit is then valu- ated to see if it complies with the predefined audit clearance/passing criteria or not. All stakeholders sign off on the audit, which signals its completion, and finally an audit report is generated. We’ll look at each of these steps in the following sections. © 633 14.3 Business Processes
sections.he:
ניתן ליצור question list מראש ולהקצותה בעת ה-audit (הרשימה המעודכנת ביותר). זמין ביצירת audit plan/audit. להקצאת רשימה קיימת, ‏Figure 14.7 ‏(1), בחרו Assign Question List (Figure 14.9).
‏audit management מתאים למגוון שימושים, וניתן לשלב audits. דוגמאות:
• **ISO 9000** (quality management) — קבוצת תקנים של ISO, להבטחת עמידה עקבית בדרישות הלקוח ושיפור מתמיד. כולל audit management — בדיקות פנימיות של מערכת ה-QM. ל-systems, ‏processes, ‏products, וגם FMEA.
• **GMP** (Good Manufacturing Practice) — נוהל ייצור ובדיקה להבטחת איכות. במדינות רבות חקיקה ל-GMP לחברות פרמצבטיקה ומכשור רפואי.
• **ISO 14000** (environmental management) — כלים לזיהוי ובקרת ההשפעה הסביבתית ושיפורה.
• **ISO 19000** (safety and security management) — תקנים למידע גאוגרפי (מושגים, איכות, מפרטים, metadata). ‏ISO 19011 — הנחיות ל-auditing של מערכות ניהול, עקרונות, ניהול audit program, והערכת כשירות.
**דוגמה:** קוני טקסטיל, ביגוד, וריהוט בית (Walmart, ‏JCPenney, ‏Gap) דורשים מהיצרנים סבבי audits קפדניים לבטיחות העובדים ולמניעת סכנות אש. ה-audits הספציפיים-לקונה מנוהלים ב-audit management.
התהליך מתחיל בשחרור ה-audit plan לחתימת כל הגורמים, ואז שחרור ה-audits הבודדים בהתקרבם. בשחרור, ה-auditor מטפל בכל שאלה והמערכת מעריכה. אם נכשל — corrective/preventive actions ומעקב. ה-audit מוערך מול קריטריוני המעבר. כל הגורמים חותמים (השלמה), ונוצר audit report.

sections.title: Release Audit Plan
sections.en: 14.3.1 Release Audit Plan Referring back to Figure 14.3, first the default or current system status of an audit plan is created. Figure 14.10 shows the Status tab, in which you choose Set to set the status of the audit plan to Release. If you choose Set Approval Requirement, then the system offers options to either approve or reject the audit plan. Once the audit plan is approved, you then have to release it. Save your entries. Figure 14.10 Releasing the Audit Plan
sections.he: מ-Figure 14.3, הסטטוס הראשוני של audit plan הוא created. ‏Figure 14.10 — לשונית Status; בחרו Set לסטטוס Release. אם בוחרים Set Approval Requirement, המערכת מציעה אישור/דחייה. לאחר האישור, יש לשחרר. שמרו.

sections.title: Release Audit
sections.en: 14.3.2 Release Audit Similar to releasing the audit plan, you perform the same steps to release the audit in the Status tab of the audit. When you release the audit plan as well as the audit, the sys- tem enables more options via which you can maintain further details of the audit. With an audit released for further working—that is, the actual audit—you can valuate a question or question list.
sections.he: בדומה לשחרור ה-audit plan, אותם צעדים לשחרור ה-audit בלשונית Status. בשחרור שניהם, המערכת מאפשרת אפשרויות נוספות. עם audit משוחרר (ה-audit בפועל), ניתן להעריך שאלה/רשימה.

sections.title: Valuate Question
sections.en: 14.3.3 Valuate Question Figure 14.11 shows the Valuation view of a question. In the Valuation area, selecting the Not Relevant checkbox makes this question irrelevant for valuation during audit calcu- lation. To valuate a question, enter No. of Points as “50”, and choose Valuation Entered to confirm that you want to valuate the question. Remember that you set the mini- mum number of points for this question must as 90.0. The system automatically marks the question as Action Required. You can also add different texts about the 14 Audit Management 634 action by choosing ID from the dropdown and then entering the long text in the pro- vided text box. You can also see the Corrective and Preventive Action icon right below the question. Figure 14.11 Question Valuation At this time, the system only updates the status of the question as either valuated or not valuated. This is shown in Figure 14.12 with a red circle icon or a green square icon to denote that the system has completed the valuation of the question. Figure 14.12 Question Valuated After you valuate a question, and depending on the company’s business process, you can create a corrective or preventive action to attend to the failed audit question and provide another opportunity to valuate the question. If you have more audit questions, then you need to valuate each and every individual audit question so that during audit valuation, the system valuates the entire questions list too. © 635 14.3 Business Processes
sections.he:
Figure 14.11 — תצוגת Valuation של שאלה. סימון Not Relevant הופך אותה לבלתי-רלוונטית לחישוב. להערכה, הזינו No. of Points "50", ובחרו Valuation Entered. ה-minimum הוא 90.0. המערכת מסמנת אוטומטית Action Required. ניתן להוסיף טקסטים (בחרו ID והזינו טקסט ארוך). אייקון Corrective and Preventive Action מתחת לשאלה.
המערכת מעדכנת רק אם השאלה הוערכה/לא (Figure 14.12 — עיגול אדום או ריבוע ירוק).
לאחר ההערכה, ניתן ליצור corrective/preventive action לשאלה שנכשלה ולהעריך שוב. אם יש שאלות נוספות, יש להעריך כל אחת כדי שבהערכת ה-audit המערכת תעריך את כל הרשימה.

sections.title: Create Corrective and Preventive Action
sections.en: 14.3.4 Create Corrective and Preventive Action During an audit, you can determine follow-up activities based on the results of an audit, including actions to determine the necessity of a subsequent audit, or corrective, preventive, and improvement actions. You can assign persons responsible, monitor the subsequent steps, and verify the effectiveness of all actions by recording and reporting on the progress data. A corrective and preventive action defines the preven- tive measure that the audit team will put in place to ensure reduction or elimination of the cause of the defect and also prevent it from happening in the future. In the screen in Figure 14.11, choose Corrective and Preventive Action for a question so that the screen in Figure 14.13 appears. Figure 14.13 Corrective/Preventive Action Here, enter the action identification and its description of the correction/preventive action. In the Basic Data tab, enter the Planned Start Date and the To Be Completed By date. At this time, the system status of the action is Created. You need to continue updating the status of the action so that the system can valuate the question and, even- tually, the question list. You do this in the next step by choosing Status, and the screen in Figure 14.14 appears. Figure 14.14 1 shows the Status tab of the action, in which you choose Set, and then from the dropdown that appears, choose Open. The system sets the action’s status to Outstanding. In the Basic Data tab, enter the Actual Start Date and Actual End Date, as well as the Level of Completion as a percentage (%). Then, in the next step, choose Status. First con- firm the status, and then set the status as Complete 2. When you or the person assigned to complete the corrective/preventive action per- forms the correction/preventive action, you can update this information accordingly in the system. You update the information by adding relevant details in the different texts available for a corrective/preventive action. 14 Audit Management 636 Figure 14.14 Status Updates for Corrective/Preventive Action Note You can integrate a digital signature in either or both steps of corrective/preventive action—that is, at the time of confirming an action or on its completion. Chapter 3 dis- cusses digital signatures.
sections.he:
ב-audit, ניתן לקבוע follow-up לפי התוצאות — צורך ב-audit עוקב, או פעולות מתקנות/מונעות/משפרות. ניתן להקצות אחראים, לנטר, ולאמת יעילות ע"י רישום ודיווח. ה-corrective and preventive action מגדיר את האמצעי המונע להפחתת/ביטול הסיבה ומניעת הישנות.
ב-Figure 14.11, בחרו Corrective and Preventive Action לשאלה (Figure 14.13).
הזינו את הזיהוי והתיאור. בלשונית Basic Data, ‏Planned Start Date ו-To Be Completed By. הסטטוס Created. יש להמשיך לעדכן את הסטטוס. בחרו Status (Figure 14.14).
Figure 14.14 ‏(1) — לשונית Status; בחרו Set, ואז Open. הסטטוס Outstanding.
בלשונית Basic Data, הזינו Actual Start/End Date ו-Level of Completion (%). בחרו Status. אשרו, ואז קבעו Complete ‏(2).
בביצוע הפעולה, עדכנו את המידע בטקסטים השונים.
**הערה:** ניתן לשלב digital signature באחד או שני הצעדים (אישור/השלמה). פרק 3.

sections.title: Valuate Audit
sections.en: 14.3.5 Valuate Audit Choose Valuate in the screen in Figure 14.15 for the Audit, and the system updates all fields in the Audit Result area. The system calculates the Deg. of Fulfill (degree of fulfill- ment) at 50%. This is because you valuated the audit question with 50 points. Notice that the system assigns the Rating as 02 Medium Risk and assigns the Overall Assesst (assessment) as 0 Failed. Because the overall assessment of the audit has failed, the sys- tem automatically selects the Subsequent Audit Required checkbox, which you can manually override. If you choose not to override this, then you can enter the date of the next audit. Figure 14.16 shows more audit questions on the left side, with audit question NSA - Second Audit. Notice the red circle traffic light icon that denotes the question Overall Supplier’s Compliance Assessment failing to meet the minimum result. Note You can integrate digital signatures in the Signature step in Figure 14.16. Choose Sig- nature; because there is no digital signature in audit management, the system locks all fields from further changes. Refer to Chapter 3 where digital signature is covered in detail. © 637 14.3 Business Processes Figure 14.15 Audit Valuation Figure 14.16 Audit Valuation with More Questions Figure 14.16 shows that Deg. of Fulfill. does indeed improve to 100%, and has the Overall Assesst. status as 1 Passed (see the Minimum Result field in Figure 14.15, where you maintained 90%). Figure 14.17 shows the audit results of a third audit with an overall score of 95.0%. With your audit valuation complete, you can now create or sign the audit report. 14 Audit Management 638 Figure 14.17 Third Audit Valuation
sections.he:
בחרו Valuate (Figure 14.15) ל-Audit — המערכת מעדכנת את כל השדות ב-Audit Result. מחשבת Deg. of Fulfill 50% (כי השאלה הוערכה ב-50 נקודות). מקצה Rating "02 Medium Risk" ו-Overall Assesst "0 Failed". מאחר שנכשל, המערכת מסמנת אוטומטית Subsequent Audit Required (ניתן לדרוס ידנית). אם לא, הזינו את תאריך ה-audit הבא. ‏Figure 14.16 — שאלות נוספות (NSA - Second Audit). העיגול האדום מציין כשל ב-Overall Supplier's Compliance Assessment.
**הערה:** ניתן digital signatures בצעד Signature (Figure 14.16). בחרו Signature; מאחר שאין digital signature, המערכת נועלת את כל השדות. פרק 3.
Figure 14.16 — ‏Deg. of Fulfill. משתפר ל-100%, ו-Overall Assesst. "1 Passed" (Minimum Result 90% ב-Figure 14.15). ‏Figure 14.17 — audit שלישי בציון 95.0%.
עם השלמת ההערכה, ניתן ליצור/לחתום audit report.

sections.title: Audit Report
sections.en: 14.3.6 Audit Report In Figure 14.17, choose Create Report, and a popup appears to confirm that you want to print the audit report. Figure 14.18 Audit Report © 639 14.3 Business Processes Choose Yes, and Figure 14.18 appears, showing the standard audit form that contains all the relevant details of the audit after its valuation. You can engage an ABAP resource to custom-develop the audit report to meet your company’s business needs. Scroll down or press (Page Down), and the screen in Figure 14.19 appears, showing more details about the question list or question. It also contains the valuation and the correc- tive/preventive action that you need to take to ensure compliance with audit require- ments. Finally, when you complete the audit, you can set the audit’s status to Complete, and the system disables all fields to prevent any further changes or updates to it. Figure 14.19 Audit Questions in Audit Report 14 Audit Management 640
sections.he:
ב-Figure 14.17, בחרו Create Report — חלון לאישור הדפסה.
בחרו Yes (Figure 14.18) — הטופס התקני עם כל הפרטים לאחר ההערכה. ניתן ABAP להתאמה.
גללו (Figure 14.19) — פרטי ה-question list/question, כולל ההערכה וה-corrective/preventive action.
בהשלמה, קבעו את הסטטוס ל-Complete — המערכת נועלת את כל השדות.

sections.title: Productivity Tools and Audit Monitor
sections.en: 14.4 Productivity Tools and Audit Monitor Managing and maintaining the enormous amount of audit data can be a herculean task. To support planning, scheduling, monitoring, and data entry efforts, audit man- agement provides several productivity tools and an audit monitor.
sections.he: ניהול כמות נתוני ה-audit הענקית הוא משימה קשה. לתמיכה בתכנון, תזמון, ניטור, והזנה, ‏audit management מספק כלי פרודוקטיביות ו-audit monitor.

sections.title: Audit Plan in Microsoft Project
sections.en: 14.4.1 Audit Plan in Microsoft Project Audit management facilitates the planning and data entry efforts required to manage large amounts of information, especially when there are several different audit types scheduled and you need complete and overall scheduling visibility of some or all of them. Audit management integrates with Microsoft Project, so you can leverage a large number of Microsoft Project’s planning tools to optimize your audits. In the screen in Figure 14.20, choose an Audit Plan, and then choose Graphical Time Scheduling. This triggers the system to open Microsoft Project and then display the scheduling details of the audit plan in Microsoft Project. You can make changes to your audit plan in Microsoft Project, and on saving, the system automatically updates all scheduling information in audit management. Figure 14.20 Audit Plan in Microsoft Project Configuration Tip You can completely map the fields between audit management and Microsoft Project so that during upload or download, the system is able to place the correct data in the relevant fields. For field mapping between the programs, follow menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  Audit Management  Audit Definition  System Adjustment  Microsoft Project Interface.
sections.he:
‏audit management מקל על התכנון וההזנה, במיוחד כשמתוזמנים סוגי audit שונים ונדרשת נראות תזמון כוללת. משתלב עם Microsoft Project — ניתן למנף את כלי התכנון שלו.
ב-Figure 14.20, בחרו Audit Plan, ואז Graphical Time Scheduling — נפתח Microsoft Project עם פרטי התזמון. ניתן לשנות שם, ובשמירה המערכת מעדכנת אוטומטית את ה-audit management.
**Configuration Tip:** ניתן למפות את השדות בין audit management ל-Microsoft Project (העלאה/הורדה תקינה). ‏SAP IMG • Quality Management • Audit Management • Audit Definition • System Adjustment • Microsoft Project Interface.

sections.title: Import and Export Audits
sections.en: 14.4.2 Import and Export Audits You can import (upload) or export (download) your audits using XML format, which eventually saves you from redundant data entry efforts. To import or upload an audit, use menu path More  Audit Component  Import. To export or download your audit to your local drive, use menu path More  Audit Component  Export. © 641 14.4 Productivity Tools and Audit Monitor Tips and Tricks When you export the XML file, you can use Microsoft Excel to open it. On completing data entry and all tasks for audit in Microsoft Excel, you save the file in the XML format, which you can then import again into the SAP S/4HANA system.
sections.he:
ניתן לייבא (העלאה) או לייצא (הורדה) audits ב-XML (חוסך הזנה כפולה). לייבוא: ‏More • Audit Component • Import. לייצוא לכונן המקומי: ‏More • Audit Component • Export.
**Tips and Tricks:** בייצוא, ניתן לפתוח ב-Excel. בסיום ההזנה, שמרו ב-XML, וייבאו חזרה ל-S/4HANA.

sections.title: Audit Monitor
sections.en: 14.4.3 Audit Monitor The audit monitor provides different search possibilities for all audit components on the basis of various search criteria. In the audit monitor, you can, for example, deter- mine the number of outstanding corrective or preventive actions, display all audits or question lists, and determine which audit plans exist for a certain time period. The audit monitor accesses all data that was created in the system in the context of audit management. Access the audit monitor using Transaction PLM_AUDITMONITOR or follow menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Audit Management  Start Audit Monitor. Figure 14.21 shows the initial screen of the audit monitor, wherein you can enter the informa- tion as selection criteria so that the system brings up only the relevant results. Figure 14.21 Audit Monitor 14 Audit Management 642 You can search for relevant audits, audit plans, or their items from a large number of search criteria, such as the status of audit items or the person(s) who created or changed the audit items. Select the Detailed Search (Show and consider specific search criteria) checkbox located further down the same screen so that the system brings up even more selection options, such as dates and audit types, for you to choose from. Entering relevant dates is also helpful when you want to know which audits are due within the specified dates. Select the Audit Plans radio button, and then enter “*NSA*” as the Identification. Choose Execute or press (F8), which brings up Figure 14.22. This screen consists of all the previously entered (or calculated) details, including the audit results, the audit type, and the dates when it was first created and then subsequently changed. With many evaluation tools available, you can add new fields, change layouts, get graphical presen- tations of audit objects, or even get a printout of the audit report. Figure 14.22 Audit Monitor Worklist
sections.he:
ה-audit monitor מספק חיפוש לכל רכיבי ה-audit לפי קריטריונים. ניתן לקבוע את מספר ה-corrective/preventive actions הפתוחות, להציג audits/question lists, ולקבוע אילו audit plans קיימים לתקופה. ניגש לכל הנתונים שנוצרו.
ל-Transaction PLM_AUDITMONITOR או Logistics • Quality Management • Audit Management • Start Audit Monitor (Figure 14.21). הזינו קריטריונים.
ניתן לחפש לפי קריטריונים רבים (סטטוס פריטים, מי יצר/שינה). סמנו Detailed Search (Show and consider specific search criteria) לאפשרויות נוספות (תאריכים, סוגים). תאריכים מסייעים לדעת אילו audits מגיעים בטווח.
בחרו רדיו Audit Plans, הזינו "*NSA*" ב-Identification. ‏Execute / F8 (Figure 14.22) — כל הפרטים (תוצאות, סוג, תאריכי יצירה/שינוי). עם כלי הערכה רבים, ניתן להוסיף שדות, לשנות layouts, תצוגות גרפיות, או תדפיס.

sections.title: Audit Inspection: Inspection Type 07
sections.en: 14.5 Audit Inspection: Inspection Type 07 Audit management has its own advantages, especially its application in managing diverse and different types of audits, which cater to almost all types of businesses. However, it doesn’t integrate with supplier evaluation for quality scoring. To attend to the business processes in which supplier audit scoring also forms an integral part of supplier evaluation vis-à-vis the quality scores from the usage decision, you can lever- age inspection type 07 with inspection origin 07 (supplier audit). Your inspection plan for the inspection lot can consist of master inspection characteristics that you use to record audit results, just as you use questions in audit management. The inspection plan’s usage should be set to 3 (universal). Finally, the usage decision for the inspection lot updates the quality scores. Inspection type 07 isn’t stock-relevant. Note Refer to Chapter 19 to see how you can influence the quality score of the usage decision of inspection type 07 in the supplier evaluation. © 643 14.5 Audit Inspection: Inspection Type 07 Access the screen shown in Figure 14.23 through Transaction QA01, and on the initial screen, enter Material “RM124”, Plant “1710”, and Insp. Lot Orig. “07” (Supplier Audit). Here, you can enter the supplier, and with the complete QM master data already in place, the system should be able to calculate the sample size. An important aspect to note here is that the system doesn’t ask for or have the option to enter an inspection quantity for inspection type 07, whereas during normal manual inspection creation (inspection type 89), the system does ask for the inspection quantity’s information. Similarly, because this inspection type is specific to supplier audit only, the Supplier field is available for input, not Customer. Figure 14.23 Audit Inspection: Inspection Type 07 The remaining steps of this manually created inspection lot are the same—that is, results recording, defects recording (if any), and usage decision. Tips and Tricks You can configure the system to make the Supplier field mandatory during inspection lot creation. This trick applies to just about any field that you want to control, such as display, input, mandatory, or highlight. Follow menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  Environment  Tools  System Modification  Adapt Field Selection. In the Module Pool field, enter “SAPLQPL1”, choose Change, and then choose Inspection Lot. Make the QALS-LIFNR field a manda- tory (Required) entry by selecting the radio button available next to the field. 14 Audit Management 644 If you aren’t sure which module pool or program to use or the technical name or details of a field, then place the cursor on the specific field, press (F1), and choose Technical Information. The system displays both the Program Name (i.e., the module pool) and the Screen Field, which is the technical name of that specific field.
sections.he:
ל-audit management יתרונות בניהול סוגי audit מגוונים. אך הוא אינו משתלב עם supplier evaluation ל-quality scoring. לתהליכים בהם ציון ה-audit חלק מ-supplier evaluation מול הציונים מ-usage decision, מנפים inspection type 07 עם inspection origin 07 (supplier audit). ה-plan ל-lot יכול לכלול MICs לרישום תוצאות ה-audit (כמו שאלות ב-audit management). ה-usage של ה-plan — 3 (universal). ה-usage decision מעדכן את ה-quality scores. ‏type 07 אינו stock-relevant.
**הערה:** פרק 19 — כיצד להשפיע על ה-quality score של usage decision של type 07 ב-supplier evaluation.
Transaction QA01 (Figure 14.23) — הזינו Material "RM124", ‏Plant "1710", ‏Insp. Lot Orig. "07" (Supplier Audit). הזינו את הספק, ועם נתוני אב QM, המערכת מחשבת את גודל הדגימה. שימו לב — המערכת אינה מבקשת inspection quantity ל-type 07 (בניגוד ל-type 89). ומאחר שזה ל-supplier audit, שדה Supplier זמין, לא Customer.
שאר הצעדים זהים — רישום תוצאות, רישום פגמים (אם יש), ו-usage decision.
**Tips and Tricks:** ניתן להפוך את שדה Supplier לחובה ביצירת lot. החוכמה חלה על כל שדה (display, ‏input, ‏mandatory, ‏highlight).
‏SAP IMG • Quality Management • Environment • Tools • System Modification • Adapt Field Selection. ב-Module Pool הזינו "SAPLQPL1", בחרו Change, ואז Inspection Lot. הפכו את QALS-LIFNR ל-Required (רדיו).
אם אינכם בטוחים ב-module pool/program או בשם הטכני, הציבו את הסמן על השדה, ‏F1, ובחרו Technical Information — המערכת מציגה את Program Name (module pool) ו-Screen Field (השם הטכני).

sections.title: Configuration Basics
sections.en: 14.6 Configuration Basics Now that you’re familiar with how to set up master data and run the business processes in audit management, the following sections cover the configuration objects that are specific to audit management. As mentioned earlier, we recommend that you also read the configuration basics of FMEA in Chapter 16; FMEA’s configuration basics highly overlap with those of audit management.
sections.he: כעת לאובייקטי התצורה הספציפיים ל-audit management. מומלץ לקרוא גם את יסודות התצורה של FMEA בפרק 16 (חופפים מאוד).

sections.title: Audit Usage
sections.en: 14.6.1 Audit Usage An audit usage logically separates various types of audits in the company. These can be safety audits, environmental audits, or data security audits. Configuring the relevant audit usages that meet the company’s business needs eventually helps in reporting. When you configure an audit type, the system prompts you to enter its audit usage. To create an audit usage, follow menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  Audit Management  Audit Definition  Audit Usage. Figure 14.24 consists of several audit usages already available that you can use, or you can create a new one by choosing New Entries and entering the usage and the description of the audit usage. Figure 14.24 Audit Usage

sections.title: Audit Type
sections.en: 14.6.2 Audit Type At the time of setting up an audit, some of the first information that the system requires from the business user is audit type. An audit type can be a system, product, process, or other. You can also define an audit type to meet your company’s business © 645 14.6 Configuration Basics needs. However, note that with every audit type, you also have to assign it an audit usage. To set up an audit type, follow menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  Audit Management  Audit Definition  Audit Type. Figure 14.25 shows an audit type consisting of several audit types. Notice audit type 51, audit usage 50 (quality audit), and the audit category system. This is the same audit type you used while setting up master data for audit management, as well as covering its business processes. Choose Aud.Type 51, and then choose Details so that the screen in Figure 14.26 appears. Figure 14.25 Audit Types Overview Figure 14.26 Detailed Screen of Audit Type 51 Figure 14.26 shows the Audit Type 51, Audit Usage 50 Quality Audit, and Audit Category 3 Process. Here, you can also control whether an audit must first go through an approval process (through a system update status) before the business user can release it by making a selection in the App. Requirement field. 14 Audit Management 646 Next, choose Input Fields for Audit Type (on the left side of Figure 14.25), and the screen in Figure 14.27 appears. The audit usage is the same as you previously configured in Sec- tion 14.6.1. Figure 14.27 Input Fields Control for Audit Type Here, you can assign the table and field name within the table so that these are avail- able at the time of creating an audit. Choose Settings for Role on the left side of Figure 14.25 shown earlier, and the screen in Figure 14.28 appears. Figure 14.28 Settings for Role in Audit Type In Figure 14.28, you define the roles that will let you have control over who can be part of the audit team. The roles that you assign here are then available in the Participants(s) tab of an audit.

sections.title: Digital Signature
sections.en: 14.6.3 Digital Signature You can integrate digital signatures into several steps in audit management, including while evaluating an audit, completing an audit, confirming action, and completing pre- ventive/corrective action. In Figure 14.25 shown earlier, choose Audit Type 51 and then Digital Signature from the left side of the screen. Here, you assign one or more already configured digital signa- ture strategies in some or all of the following four areas:  Evaluate Audit: Individual signature  Complete Audit: Multiple signatures strategy © 647

sections.title: Audit Trigger
sections.en: 14.6.4 Audit Trigger The option to enter an audit trigger is available at the time of creating an audit. An audit trigger provides the business user with the option to define why an audit is nec- essary. An audit trigger can be a regular annual or quarterly audit, or a process improvement initiative. To create an audit trigger, follow menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  Audit Management  Audit Definition  Audit Trigger. In the screen that appears, evaluate whether the already available audit triggers meet your company’s business needs. If not, create a new one, which then becomes available at the time of creating an audit. 14.7 Summary In this chapter, we showed you how to map and implement actual audit processes and integrate them in the QM area of an SAP S/4HANA system. You can also take advantage of the system to calculate audit results, as well as have a question list to help you with your audit management initiative. The audit monitor is a powerful tool to monitor and keep track of your various audit objects. Inspection types for supplier audits help you integrate the results from the usage decision with the supplier evaluation. The produc- tivity tools enable you to leverage Microsoft Office products that completely integrate with audit management. The next chapter discusses stability studies. ©

הפרק הבא — stability studies.

sections.title: Integration Workflow
sections.en: 15.1 Integration Workflow The stability study with a material requires a decent knowledge of four different SAP S/4HANA areas: quality management (QM), production planning (PP), plant mainte- nance (PM), and materials management (MM). It’s in the QM area that the stability 15 Stability Study 650 study with (or without) a material is performed, along with several associated activi- ties, such as results recording and usage decision. In the actual business process of conducting a stability study, all the related depart- ments of the company come together to contribute to their share of this endeavor (sta- bility study). This includes, but isn’t limited to, the decision-making process to determine which of the following options you’ll choose:  Proceed with the full-fledged stability study, or cancel it after the initial test  Revise the testing schedule of storage conditions, or shorten or prolong it  Cancel the stability study, or simply “deactivate” it for a limited time to be reacti- vated later Figure 15.1 provides a better picture of the stability study workflow. Figure 15.1 Stability Study Workflow The stability study with (or without) a material draws its fundamental concept from the notification in QM. In fact, the first step toward creating a stability study begins with cre- ating a special QM notification that’s available for stability studies only. Hence, this chap- ter will intermittently refer to stability studies with either a material or a notification. Create stability study Start Initial test Continue stability study? Stability planning Stability test Finish stability study End No Yes © 651

sections.title: Master Data
sections.en: 15.2 Master Data For the stability study, inspection types 16, 1601, and 1602 are applicable. Table 15.1 explains each of the three inspection types in the material master and their roles in the stability study. We’ll cover the actual applications of all three inspection types in this chapter. Note The inspection plans’ usage for all three inspection types is 9 (Material Check). 15.3 Stability Study for a Material We’ll now cover every step of the stability study with a material. We’ll also address all the options and choices available in the Action Box of the stability study with a mate- rial. To facilitate the understanding and learning process, we’ll move in a logical order so that it’s easier to comprehend the relationship between each sequential action during the stability study for a material. Inspection Type Inspection Type Description Role of Inspection Type in Stability Study 16 Inspection for Storage Condition (Stabi) This inspection type ensures the creation of the inspec- tion lot for the storage condition of the stability study. Once the sample is stored in the defined storage condi- tion, it’s imperative that the sample is periodically inspected to assess that its physical and chemical condi- tions meet the desired requirements. Creation of an inspection lot is generally ensured through a testing schedule, which stipulates pre- defined, periodic, and regular inspections during the stability study. 1601 Initial Test (Stability Studies) This inspection type ensures that before the actual sta- bility study starts, the business process owner approves the initial test for the sample. On approval or otherwise, a decision is made to continue or not continue with the stability study. 1602 Manual Insp. Lot for Storage Cond (Stab) This inspection type ensures that at any given point in time, if there’s a need to create an inspection lot for a storage condition (and which deviates from the testing schedule), then the necessary provision is in place. Table 15.1 Inspection Types for Stability Study 15 Stability Study 652

sections.title: Create Stability Study with a Material
sections.en: 15.3.1 Create Stability Study with a Material To create a new stability study with a material, use Transaction QST01 or follow menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Stability Study  Stability Study  Create. On the initial screen for creating a stability study, enter the notification type QS, which is for stability study with a material, and an internal notification/stability study number that the system generates, which in this example is 800000004. Then, press (Enter) to go to the screen in Figure 15.2. As previously explained, a stability study is a special form of quality notification. Further, the notification type QS is available in the standard SAP model company provided by SAP. Note If you need to work with a stability study without a material, then the available notifi- cation type in the IDES system is QR. In a stability study without a material, there is no reference to a material or its associated batch number. However, all the steps that we cover in this chapter for a stability study with a material are equally applicable to a sta- bility study without a material (but without direct reference to a material or batch number). The system also offers another notification type, QT, which is for a stability study trial. This stability study type uses predefined and preconfigured building blocks consisting of planning data to facilitate the stability study. In Figure 15.2, enter Material “2234” and Plant “1710”. Because this material is batch- managed, the system requires the batch number, along with the storage location. We assign these as 121 and 171A, respectively. Prior to starting the stability study with a material, you can create a batch for this material and plant with Transaction MSC1N. If you’ve maintained the date of manufacturing and expiration date (shelf-life expiration date/best-before date [SLED/BBD]) of the batch, then these will also automatically appear in the stability study screen. The entire chapter will refer to not just this mate- rial but also its corresponding batch number, 121, available at storage location 171A. Note The focus of this entire chapter is on the tasks shown in the Action Box on the right side of Figure 15.2. We’ll cover each of these tasks in detail. We’ll cover the first two steps of the Action Box, Display Objects for Study and Display Stability History, at the end of the chapter. This approach will make sense when we’ve performed necessary actions for the stability study and the relevant information becomes available in the first two objects of the Action Box. Let’s start with step number three of the Action Box, which is Create Initial Sample, and then proceed with each step of the Action Box in sequential order. © 653 15.3 Stability Study for a Material Figure 15.2 Detailed Screen of Stability Study with Material and Action Box Note We’ll refer to Figure 15.2 and/or the Action Box in the rest of this chapter, unless other- wise mentioned.

sections.title: Initial Sample
sections.en: 15.3.2 Initial Sample Before an actual stability study begins, it’s important to create an initial sample of the stability study. The initial sample is the physical sample of the stability study. This physical sample goes through the regular QM tasks of results recording, defects record- ing (if any), and usage decision to validate the process and decide whether a full-fledged stability study should continue or not. Just as with normal inspection, the initial sam- ple for the stability study also contains comprehensive details related to sample size, packing, sample location, and storage condition. In the following sections, we’ll show how to create, change, and then confirm an initial sample. An initial sample needs to be confirmed to proceed further with the stability study. 15 Stability Study 654 Create Choose Create Initial Sample from Action Box to go to Figure 15.3. Here, enter the details that relate to sample container, sample quantity, storage condition, and sample loca- tion. Choose Save and Change Notification. On saving, the system creates a physical sample, which in this example is 900000026. Because this is the initial sample, this ref- erence of the initial sample remains available throughout the entire process of the cov- ering stability study with material. Figure 15.3 Creating Initial Sample Change If you need to make any changes after creating an initial sample, then choose Change Initial Sample from Action Box, as shown in Figure 15.4. Notice that in change mode, the system has already created a physical sample 900000026 with the status set as created (CRTD). Make any desired changes, such as changing the sample size from a quantity of 3 (as first defined in Figure 15.3) to 2 PC. Choose Save and Change Notification in Figure 15.4. Doing so saves the changes you’ve made and brings you back to the change notifi- cation (stability study) screen. © 655 15.3 Stability Study for a Material Figure 15.4 Changing Initial Sample Confirm The next step is the confirmation of the initial sample. A confirmation validates that the initial sample can form the basis of proceeding further with the stability study. To confirm an initial sample, choose Confirm Initial Sample in Action Box to go to Figure 15.5. This screen contains the previously entered information of the initial sample. Notice the option to enter the No. (number) of Labels for the initial sample. You can print these labels and physically paste them onto the physical samples’ containers. Enter the number of labels to be printed as “3”, and choose Save and Change Notifica- tion to go to the screen shown in Figure 15.6, which is a popup that appears with the pro- vision to add or update additional information and relates to the confirmation of the initial sample. Enter or update the information, and choose Continue. The system accordingly updates the status of the physical sample of the initial test to REL (released). 15 Stability Study 656 Figure 15.5 Confirmation of Initial Sample Figure 15.6 Additional Details for Confirmation of Initial Sample

נראה יצירה, שינוי, ואישור. יש לאשר initial sample כדי להמשיך.

**Create:**
בחרו Create Initial Sample מ-Action Box (Figure 15.3). הזינו sample container, ‏sample quantity, ‏storage condition, ו-sample location. בחרו Save and Change Notification. המערכת יוצרת דגימה פיזית (בדוגמה 900000026). הפניה זו זמינה לאורך כל התהליך.

אישור מתקף שה-initial sample יכול לשמש בסיס. בחרו Confirm Initial Sample (Figure 15.5) — המידע הקודם. שימו לב ל-No. of Labels — ניתן להדפיס ולהדביק על המכלים. הזינו "3", בחרו Save and Change Notification (Figure 15.6 — חלון להוספה/עדכון מידע). הזינו, ‏Continue. הסטטוס מתעדכן ל-REL (released).

sections.title: Bill of Materials
sections.en: 15.3.3 Bill of Materials Because we’re creating the stability study with a material, the system allows you to enter details of the components used in the stability study. These components are in the form of a bill of materials (BOM). A BOM contains the details of an individual com- ponent, together with its quantity. The following sections will discuss how to assign a BOM to a stability study and be able to maintain it subsequently. © 657 15.3 Stability Study for a Material Assign Choose Assign Bill of Material in Action Box to go to Figure 15.7. Figure 15.7 Assign Bill of Materials Here, the system also allows entering a BOM of another material. Notice that the Usage of the BOM in Figure 15.7 is defined as a stability study. This usage prevents the BOM from being used in the normal production process. The stability study usage of a BOM has limited functions because material is still going through the development, trial, and testing phases. When the stability study is successful, you can change the BOM usage to 1, which is for production. Choose Assign Bill of Material. Tips and Tricks We suggest creating a BOM for the material and its usage 8 beforehand so that you can assign it in this step. To create a material BOM, use Transaction CS01. This is an integration point between QM and PP. Further, to ensure that Usage 8 is allowed in Figure 15.7, make the necessary entry in Transaction OS21 if it doesn’t exist. Maintain After the initial assignment of a material BOM to the stability study, you can also make further changes to it if needed. These changes can include, for example, the deletion of a BOM component or a change in the quantity. To make changes in the BOM, choose Maintain Bill of Material in Action Box to go to the change screen for the BOM shown in Figure 15.8. Notice that one of the components is 15 Stability Study 658 RM20, with a quantity of 10 PC (pieces). If needed, you can change the quantity of this component or even add a new component. Choose Save to save the BOM. Figure 15.8 Changes to Bill of Materials
sections.he:
מאחר שיוצרים study עם חומר, ניתן להזין את הרכיבים — בצורת BOM (רכיב, כמות).

**Assign:**
בחרו Assign Bill of Material (Figure 15.7). ניתן להזין גם BOM של חומר אחר. ה-Usage מוגדר stability study — מונע שימוש בייצור רגיל. ל-usage זה פונקציות מוגבלות (החומר עדיין בפיתוח/ניסוי). בהצלחת ה-study, ניתן לשנות ל-usage 1 (production). בחרו Assign Bill of Material.
**Tips and Tricks:** מומלץ ליצור BOM לחומר עם usage 8 מראש (Transaction CS01) — נקודת אינטגרציה QM-PP. כדי ש-Usage 8 מותר (Figure 15.7), הזינו ב-Transaction OS21 אם לא קיים.

**Maintain:**
לאחר ההקצאה, ניתן שינויים (מחיקת רכיב, שינוי כמות). בחרו Maintain Bill of Material (Figure 15.8). רכיב RM20 בכמות 10 PC. ניתן לשנות כמות או להוסיף רכיב. שמרו.

sections.title: Initial Test Inspection Lot: Inspection Type 1601
sections.en: 15.3.4 Initial Test Inspection Lot: Inspection Type 1601 After the confirmation of the initial sample, the next important step is the creation of an inspection lot for the initial test in the stability study. An inspection lot for the ini- tial test automatically creates an inspection lot of inspection type 1601. Warning Until the initial sample is confirmed, you can’t create an inspection lot for the initial test of the stability study. The system checks that the physical sample has the released (REL) status, and if so, allows inspection lot creation. This shows the importance of fol- lowing the sequence of steps given in Action Box. In Action Box, choose Initial Test Inspection Lot to go to the screen in Figure 15.9. Notice that the physical sample 900000026 is the same physical sample that we’ve worked on in the previous steps. The inspection lot, which the system creates, is inspection type 1601. You can manually assign the task list Group “7” and Group Counter “1”, which we previously covered in Section 15.2, as part of the stability study master data. Choose Inspection Lot in Figure 15.9 to create an inspection lot and to go to the screen in Figure 15.10. Figure 15.10 shows the selection screen for master inspection characteristics that the system brings up for inspection lot results recording and usage decision. The master inspection characteristics are taken from the inspection plan that was previously avail- able as a part of the QM master data. © 659 15.3 Stability Study for a Material Figure 15.9 Creating Inspection Lot for Initial Test Inspection Figure 15.10 Option to Flexibly Select or Change Details of Master Inspection Characteristics Notice the flexibility you have in selecting the relevant master inspection characteris- tics, which are then available for results recording and usage decision. At this stage, you can also change the other details, such as lower or upper limits or even the target value of any master inspection characteristic. For this example, first choose Select All to select all the master inspection characteristics, and then choose Copy All to copy all the master inspection characteristics to the inspection lot. With this step, the system creates a new inspection lot for the initial test of the stability study with inspection type 1601. For this example, this inspection lot number is 160000000005. 15 Stability Study 660 Now that the system has created an inspection lot for the initial conditions for the sta- bility study, we’ll briefly discuss the associated QM activities, such as results recording and usage decisions, before we return to Action Box to cover the remaining available options.

sections.title: Inspection Process for an Initial Sample: Results Recording and Usage
sections.en: 15.3.5 Inspection Process for an Initial Sample: Results Recording and Usage Decision Because the results recording and usage decisions are standard QM activities, we’ll quickly walk you through how the system incorporates all the information and details from the stability study into the newly created inspection lot, as well as the role of inspection points. To record results, use Transaction QE01, and on the initial screen, enter Inspection Lot “160000000005” and Operation “0010”. Press (Enter), and the system shows the Assigned Insp. Pnt button. Click once, and the system automatically assigns physical sample 900000026. Figure 15.11 appears after we’ve entered the results of operation 0010, and it also con- tains details of physical sample 900000026 against the inspection lot. Save the entries and repeat the same steps for operation 0010 so that the screen in Figure 15.12 appears. This step highlights the importance of the inspection points that we previously covered. Figure 15.11 Initial Screen for Results Recording of Inspection Lot Choose the Samples Overview for Material button located at the bottom-right side of the screen shown in Figure 15.13, which shows not just the initial phyicsal sample 900000026 associated with this inspection lot but also other additional details. © 661 15.3 Stability Study for a Material Figure 15.12 Results Recording of Inspection Lot Figure 15.13 Usage Decision of Inspection Lot For the usage decision, use Transaction QA11, and on the initial screen, enter Inspection Lot “160000000005”. In the screen in Figure 15.13, enter the usage decision code (UD Code) as “0010” and “STABI” to accept and approve the results of the initial test inspec- tion for the stability study. This usage decision code selection also confirms that we’ll proceed with executing the stability study. Choose the Samples tab to go to the screen in Figure 15.14. 15 Stability Study 662 Figure 15.14 Detailed Screen for Physical Samples of Inspection Lot Figure 15.14 shows the detail screen for physical sample 900000026 and its corre- sponding operation used in the initial test inspection lot for the stability study. Save your entries. You then receive a message confirming the successful completion of the initial test for notification type 800000004. So far, we’ve created, confirmed, and approved the initial test inspection lot for the sta- bility study by means of results recording and usage decision. Let’s return to the remaining steps and options available in Action Box for a stability study with a mate- rial.

sections.title: Change Notification
sections.en: 15.3.6 Change Notification On saving the original notification 800000004 and performing other activities such as results recording or usage decision, you can use the change notification option to return to the stability study with a material. To change the notification, use Transaction QM02 or menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Stability Study  Stability Study  Change. On the initial screen for chang- ing the notification type, enter the Notification “800000004”, and press (Enter). This brings us back to the screen in Figure 15.2, but this time in change mode.

בשמירת notification 800000004 וביצוע פעולות (רישום, usage decision), ניתן להשתמש ב-change notification לחזרה ל-study.
לשינוי: ‏Transaction QM02 או Logistics • Quality Management • Stability Study • Stability Study • Change. הזינו Notification "800000004", ‏Enter (חזרה ל-Figure 15.2 במצב שינוי).

sections.title: Complete Initial Test
sections.en: 15.3.7 Complete Initial Test In Action Box, choose Complete Initial Test. This confirms and saves the results of the initial test of the inspection lot. © 663 15.3 Stability Study for a Material
