sections.title: Additional FMEA Features
sections.en: 16.3.5 Additional FMEA Features Now that you’re familiar with the main steps to calculate FMEA, let’s go over some of the nice-to-have features that you can use to improve your processes and aid in FMEA initiatives. FMEA Report Referring to Figure 16.42, you can get a printout of the FMEA in the form of a report, as well as sign it, by choosing the relevant buttons available right next to the Valuate but- ton. Choose Form in Figure 16.42, and a prompt appears to confirm whether you’d like to create a report for the FMEA (Figure 16.43). Choose Yes, and it leads to Figure 16.44. Figure 16.43 Create FMEA report Figure 16.44 is the print preview of the FMEA REVO and in the industry standard for- mat: FMEA VDA 96. This output will only be visible if ADS is already installed in SAP S/4HANA. Figure 16.45 shows that the system has calculated an RPN of 80. Further, it also shows the three columns that the system uses in calculating RPN. These are denoted by S (for severity), O (for occurrence), and D (for detection), with values of 10, 2, and 4, respec- tively. 16 Failure Mode and Effects Analysis and Control Plan 722 Figure 16.44 FMEA in System Form: FMEA VDA 96 Figure 16.45 RPN Updated in Print Preview (Form Layout) of FMEA Here, we suggest that you explore more functions available in the toolbar. Digital Signatures in FMEA You can integrate digital signatures in several steps in FMEA, including while valuating FMEA, confirming FMEA, confirming actions, and completing actions. In Figure 16.46, choose Signature. Because there is no digital signature in FMEA, the sys- tem locks or disables all fields against further changes. © 723 16.3 Business Processes Figure 16.46 FMEA after Signature Tips and Tricks To integrate digital signatures to meet your company’s business needs in FMEA, use menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  Inspection Planning  Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA)  FMEA Definition  FMEA Type. Choose a FMEA Type, and then choose Digital Signature from the left side of the screen. Here, you can see the already configured digital signature strategy (refer to Chapter 3 on how to configure a digital signature) in some or all of the following areas:  Valuate FMEA: Individual signature  Complete FMEA: Multiple signatures strategy  Confirm Action: Individual signature Actions Overview In Figure 16.46, choose Actions, and then choose an action such as Detection or Preven- tion. Next, choose Print FMEA Component, and finally choose Print Preview so that Figure 16.47 appears. Here, you see the standard layout that SAP delivers for corrective/preventive actions. You can engage an ABAP resource to custom-develop the form to meet your company’s business needs. Refer to Section 16.8.8 for more information and to see how to assign custom-developed forms to FMEA objects. 16 Failure Mode and Effects Analysis and Control Plan 724 Figure 16.47 Print Preview of Preventive/Corrective Action(s) FMEA Overview As you’ve seen, setting up business processes in FMEA involves several steps. How- ever, to get an overview of all the items in FMEA, including their statuses, choose the Items overview button in Figure 16.48. Notice the Item Type (number) and Item Type (description) columns, as well as the FMEA terms that the SAP S/4HANA system uses to denote various FMEA items, such as Result (cause) and Reason (effect) (not shown, but can be made visible either by scrolling to the right of the screen or by changing the screen layout). Figure 16.48 FMEA Overview © 725 16.3 Business Processes Here again, we suggest that you explore more functions available in the toolbar, including how to add more fields to the display and the option to download the data. Figure 16.49 shows the Manage FMEAs app using a graphical framework. It provides a flexible worklist from which you can open an FMEA that is displayed as the focus ele- ment with its higher-level and lower-level elements. On the details page of this focus FMEA, you can access detailed information about the FMEA as well as various graphical views to show the related elements, functions, and failure modes. Some additional fea- tures of this app are listed here:  List existing FMEAs according to the selection criteria, which enables monitoring FMEAs with high risk.  Create, change, or display FMEAs.  Define planning and administrative data at the FMEA header level.  Build up the FMEA structure in different graphical views according to the FMEA data model.  Execute a structure analysis by defining and connecting FMEA elements (Elements view).  Execute a function analysis by creating functions for different FMEAs and connect- ing them (Functions view).  Execute a failure analysis by creating failure modes for functions and connecting the failure modes of other FMEAs as failure causes and effects (Functions/Failure Modes view). Figure 16.49 Manage FMEAs 16 Failure Mode and Effects Analysis and Control Plan 726  Monitor the failure effect chain with failure modes, effects, and causes with their dependencies (Failure Modes view).  Show the items of an FMEA in a tree view.  Navigate to the FMEA Cockpit to continue processing the FMEA, for example, to define team members or to add more details.  Create preventive and detection actions as initial actions to do a risk analysis in the Risk Optimization view.  Identify and define actions for improvement for optimization purposes in the Risk Optimization view.  Trigger the calculation of action priorities.

sections.title: Question List
sections.en: 16.4 Question List During the FMEA initiative, one of the critical components is the availability of a ques- tion list. A question list is a list of questions that the users or business process owners answer to ensure complete traceability and accountability. You create a question list after creating an FMEA in the system. Further, you also need to ensure that the ques- tion list is approved before the users can update the answers to the questions con- tained in the question list. Here again, the system provides the flexibility to copy a new question list from an existing one (template), as well as upload it from external sources. You can also assign a question list to FMEA.

sections.title: Create Questions in the Question List
sections.en: 16.4.1 Create Questions in the Question List From the FMEA Cockpit, right-click the FMEA (in this example, REVO; see Figure 16.50). This screen has all the similarities that you’ve previously seen in FMEA. Here again, you need to give a name to the question list (for this example, enter “QLIST-REVO”), as well as a description. You can also assign a validity to the question list. The functions of Texts and Contact Person are the same as we previously covered for FMEA, so we won’t repeat them here. Choose Valuation Specs in Figure 16.50, which leads to Figure 16.51, where you assign the procedures to calculate the valuation. Further, you can also assign a priority to the question list to reflect its importance. In the Valuation area (not shown), you assign a valuation profile to help the system valuate the answers against the question list. Lastly, you can import documents from your local hard drive so that you don’t have to create them all in FMEA. © 727 16.4 Question List Figure 16.50 Creating a Question List Figure 16.51 Valuation Specification of Question List Right-click on Question List (in the Navigation area) so that the option to create a ques- tion appears (see Figure 16.52). Figure 16.52 shows a question with identification QUESTION: VISUAL INSP.. At this stage, the system enables you to not only maintain the valuation procedure, the question’s priority, but also the minimum score of the question. Further, options to maintain val- uation procedure and valuation profile are also there. 16 Failure Mode and Effects Analysis and Control Plan 728 Figure 16.52 Question in a Question List

sections.title: Approval and Release of a Question List
sections.en: 16.4.2 Approval and Release of a Question List Figure 16.53 shows the Status tab of question list QLIST-REVO. As we previously explained, you have to approve and/or release the question list before it become avail- able in FMEA. Further, the status you set here is also available in the FMEA Monitor (Transaction QM_FMEAMONITOR; see Section 16.5 for more information). Once ques- tions are maintained for a question list, proceed to release the question list by setting its status to Release. In Figure 16.53, we set the system status to Set Approval Requirement. Then, the avail- able options to approve or reject are available. Choose Approve, and the updated sys- tem status is available. This screen reflects the audit trail of statuses of the question list, including Approved and Released. Note The option to digitally sign a question list in FMEA isn’t available in the SAP S/4HANA system. Figure 16.54 shows the partial print preview that is available (and that SAP delivers as its standard offering) when you select the relevant question list and choose Print Preview. You can engage an ABAP resource to custom-develop the form to meet your company’s business needs. Refer to the configuration section (Section 16.8.8), in which we show how to assign custom-developed forms to FMEA objects. © 729

sections.title: Risk Analysis
sections.en: 16.6 Risk Analysis You can search for relevant FMEAs or their items from many search criteria, such as dates, status of the FMEA, or person(s) who created or changed the FMEA. For this example, select the FMEA radio button and then, in the Identification field, enter “REVO”. Finally, choose Execute (not shown, but located at the bottom-right side of the screen). This leads to Figure 16.57. Figure 16.57 shows all the previously entered (or calculated) details, including the RPN result of 80.0, the FMEA type (process), and the dates when it was first created and then subsequently changed. With many icons available, you can add new fields, change lay- outs, or even create a printout of the report on FMEA components. Figure 16.57 Detailed View of the FMEA Monitor 16.6 Risk Analysis You can run a risk analysis for the causes in an FMEA based on detection actions, pre- ventive actions, and the severity of defects, and then represent the risk using risk matrixes. You can start the risk analysis for one or more FMEAs from the FMEA Moni- tor (Figure 16.57) and from the FMEA Cockpit. The risk analysis shows an overview of the risk situation, based on the specified FMEAs and using risk matrixes. It takes all causes of the specified FMEAs into account and analyzes them. In a risk analysis, the risk situ- ation is represented using different configurable risk matrixes. The risk analysis can represent the actual or target analysis. Each risk matrix cell shows the number of causes with their respective valuations. The risk analysis is based on the following valuation categories:  Probability of occurrence at the level of preventive actions or directly at the level of the cause  Probability of detection at the level of detection actions  Severity at the level of the effects You can combine the risk of these three categories in different risk matrixes. From the valuation, the following results are determined:  Classification in each risk matrix.  Classification of each cause by the risk matrixes that are assigned to the risk analysis profile used with the following classifications: 0 (green), 1 (yellow), 2 (red). These assignments are made during configuration. 16 Failure Mode and Effects Analysis and Control Plan 732 A combined risk value can be calculated for a cause that was classified in different matrixes. The risk value is derived by adding the different matrixes together. Example If, for example, a cause was classified in three matrixes, where it has one each of the classifications yellow (1), green (0), and red (2), the total risk is 1 + 0 + 2 = 3. The total risk provides information about which general risk a cause has. You specify whether a matrix is used to calculate the total risk. When you start the FMEA Monitor, you can select one or more FMEAs for which you want to start the risk analysis. You then choose the Risk Analysis button. A dialog box appears in which you can specify the risk analysis profile. The risk analysis is displayed according to the settings. You can switch between the target and actual analysis (see Figure 16.58). Figure 16.58 Standard Risk Analysis Profile in the FMEA Monitor If you choose a cell in a matrix that shows several classified causes, the corresponding causes can be further selected in the table. In reverse, you can use the table to show the position of certain causes in the matrixes. To do this, select the causes in the table, and choose Select in Matrix in the Display column. In the FMEA Cockpit, you open the risk analysis by selecting an FMEA and choosing Risk Analysis in the context menu. With Risk Analysis with Lower-Level Elements, you can specify that all lower-level FMEAs are also included in the risk analysis (see Figure 16.58). © 733

**Risk analysis:** ניתן להריץ ניתוח סיכון ל-causes ב-FMEA לפי detection actions, ‏preventive actions, ו-severity, ולייצג ב-risk matrixes. ניתן להתחיל מ-FMEA Monitor (Figure 16.57) ומ-FMEA Cockpit. מציג סקירת מצב הסיכון לפי ה-FMEAs ב-risk matrixes. מתחשב בכל ה-causes. ניתן actual או target. כל תא מציג את מספר ה-causes והערכותיהם.
קטגוריות ההערכה:
• Probability of occurrence ברמת ה-preventive actions או ישירות ברמת ה-cause
• Probability of detection ברמת ה-detection actions
• Severity ברמת ה-effects
ניתן לשלב ב-risk matrixes שונים. מההערכה נקבע:
• סיווג בכל matrix.
• סיווג כל cause לפי ה-matrixes המוקצים ל-risk analysis profile: ‏0 (ירוק), ‏1 (צהוב), ‏2 (אדום). בתצורה.
ניתן לחשב ערך סיכון משולב ל-cause שסווג ב-matrixes שונים, ע"י חיבורם.
**דוגמה:** אם cause סווג בשלושה matrixes — צהוב (1), ירוק (0), אדום (2) — הסיכון הכולל 1 + 0 + 2 = 3. הכולל מספק מידע על הסיכון הכללי. מציינים אם matrix משמש לחישוב הכולל.
ב-FMEA Monitor, בחרו FMEAs ל-risk analysis, ובחרו Risk Analysis. חלון לציון ה-risk analysis profile. מעבר בין target ל-actual (Figure 16.58).
בבחירת תא עם causes רבים, ניתן לבחור את ה-causes בטבלה. הפוך — בחרו causes בטבלה ו-Select in Matrix (טור Display).
ב-FMEA Cockpit, בחרו FMEA ו-Risk Analysis בתפריט ההקשר. עם Risk Analysis with Lower-Level Elements, גם FMEAs נמוכים נכללים (Figure 16.58).

sections.title: Control Plan
sections.en: 16.7 Control Plan Figure 16.59 shows a risk matrix using the action priority profile as defined in configu- ration with focus on severity, reflected by the 1 (with the severity in the range of 9-10) in the left side of the risk matrix. Figure 16.59 Action Priority Profile in the FMEA Monitor Note To set up profiles for a risk matrix, follow menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  Inspection Planning  Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA)  System Modification  Risk Analysis. 16.7 Control Plan A control plan is a specific and actionable plan that the business process owner can put in place to ensure product or process improvements, and it’s the direct outcome of FMEA. A control plan enables the company to have a working plan in place to avoid occurrences of failure in the first place, as well as prevent it by taking necessary reac- tionary steps if it does occur. The control plan and its integration with FMEA enables companies to have a comprehensive compliance road amap to meet agreed-upon product or service quality standards. It also includes reactionary steps to take in case of deviations to the agreed-upon quality standards. 16 Failure Mode and Effects Analysis and Control Plan 734 The ability to create a control plan and then integrate it with FMEA in the SAP S/4HANA system provides the added leverage of having all the critical prevention, detection, and reactionary information in one system (the SAP system). To create a control plan, use Transaction QPCP or menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Quality Planning  Control Plan  Cockpit. Figure 16.60 shows the initial screen to create a new control plan. You can use a previously created control plan as a template to create a new control plan. This is possible when you enter the previously created control plan in the template area. This option enables the system to copy pre- viously entered information into the new control plan, saving you time and effort with data entry. Figure 16.60 Creating a Control Plan In Figure 16.60, enter the Control Plan “CP-REVO” at the top of the screen, and then select an available Plan Type, such as Prototype, Prelaunch, or Production, from the dropdown. For this example, select the Prototype control plan, and then choose Create Control Plan, and Figure 16.61 appears. Figure 16.61 shows the Basic Data tab of control plan CP-REVO. Enter the name of the control plan in the Short Text field, and enter Material “FG129” and Plant “1710”. Enter- ing a relevant short text to denote what the control plan refers to or is about helps in identification. For example, a control plan code such as 500 doesn’t help in identifying or clarifying what it refers to, but a short text such as “REVO (Brake Assembly)” for a control plan helps the process owner to quickly find it in the search function. Notice that when you’re creating a control plan, the system sets the status as In Process as shown in Figure 16.62 (this is the lower half of the screen in Figure 16.61). Tips and Tricks At any time, you can check the status of a control plan to see if there are any errors, such as any deficiencies or discrepancies in the control plan. We checked the control plan while it was still in the In Process status, as shown in Figure 16.62. We’ll check it again later, once we release the control plan. © 735 16.7 Control Plan Figure 16.61 Basic Data of Control Plan Figure 16.62 Status Area of Basic Data for the Control Plan Choose the Items tab in Figure 16.61, and Figure 16.63 appears. Here, enter the details shown, such as Short Text “REVO”, Material “FG129”, and, most importantly, Task List Type “Q”, Group “4”, and Group Counter “2”. The task list Q represents an inspection plan for material FG129 within task list group 4 and group counter 2. An inspection plan for a material denotes the physical or chemical attributes of a material that the com- pany wants to inspect. Choose the Struct. (structure) tab in Figure 16.63, and Figure 16.64 appears. 16 Failure Mode and Effects Analysis and Control Plan 736 Figure 16.63 Items Tab of Control Plan Figure 16.64 Struct. Tab of Control Plan Figure 16.64 shows the FMEA structure of REVO within the control plan REVO. This tab not only serves a reference purpose so that the process owner can view the FMEA structure while remaining within the control plan, but it’s also intuitive enough to let the process owner perform additional functions, such as creating an inspection plan or a task list, or even copying master inspection characteristics into an existing inspection plan. For example, right-click Inspection Plan, followed by choosing Copy © 737 16.7 Control Plan Characteristics. In the ensuing popup, copy FMEA characteristics to inspection plan 4, as shown in Figure 16.65. Tips and Tricks The example in this section focuses on copying a master inspection characteristic into an existing plan, but you can also leverage a control plan to create an inspection plan and a task list. To do so, right-click the Goods Receipt icon (Figure 16.64). In the ensuing popup, the system brings up the option to create a new inspection plan or task list. The options to create an inspection plan or task list are available not just for goods receipt but also for production and goods issue. Figure 16.65 shows the popup to transfer FMEA characteristics to the inspection plan. On the top-left side, select FMEA from the Charact. (characteristic) Origin dropdown 1, enter FMEA “REVO” on the top-right side 2, and choose the Load Charact. button. This results in the system loading the FMEA characteristic, which is visible on the left side of the screen in Figure 16.65 3. For a quick reference, we suggest that you revisit Figure 16.16, in which we assigned master inspection characteristic Char: Brake Pad and Plant 1710. Figure 16.65 Transferring FMEA Characteristics to an Inspection Plan The next step is to select the FMEA characteristic Char: Brake Pad from the left side of the screen 3, followed by placing the cursor on Operation 10 on the right side of the screen 4 and clicking the black right-facing arrow—that is, add the characteristic to the plan 4. The resulting screen is shown in the lower-half of Figure 16.65 5. Choose Save Transferred Charct. and Close. 16 Failure Mode and Effects Analysis and Control Plan 738 Tips and Tricks If you can’t select an option from the Charact. Origin dropdown shown in Figure 16.65 1, it means the necessary configuration is missing. To quickly configure the required settings, follow menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  Quality Planning  Opera- tion  Inspection Characteristic  Define Inspection-Characteristic Origin. In the ensu- ing screen, make a new entry by assigning a numeric value to the characteristic origin, followed by its short description. In the example in Figure 16.65, the numeric identifica- tion is 1, and the short description is FMEA. Figure 16.66 confirms a successful consistency check of the FMEA characteristic that is transferred to the inspection plan. Figure 16.66 Consistency Check for Characteristics Transfer Here, you see the successful transfer of FMEA characteristic Diameter in the lower half of the screen. It’s also now part of inspection plan 4 and is visible on the right side (just below the Length master inspection characteristic), as shown in Figure 16.67. To cross-check the successful transfer of FMEA characteristics to the inspection plan, Figure 16.68 shows the inspection plan (Transaction QP03) for group 4 and group counter 2. In Oper/Act. 0010, notice the newly incorporated master inspection charac- teristic DIAMETER with the short text Char: Brake Pad. © 739 16.7 Control Plan Figure 16.67 FMEA Structure Figure 16.68 Master Inspection Characteristic Diameter in Inspection Plan 4 Choose the Basic Data tab of the control plan and proceed to release the control plan. Figure 16.69 appears after you choose to Release the control plan, and the system updates the system status accordingly. You can revert a released control plan status back to In Process and lock the control plan to prevent any further usage of it. Finally, choose the Consistency Check to ensure that the control plan is still consistent after its release. Had there been any warning or error in the control plan, the system would have shown it with yellow or red lights, respectively. 16 Failure Mode and Effects Analysis and Control Plan 740 Figure 16.69 Released Control Plan and Successful Consistency Check Next, choose the FMEA tab, and Figure 16.70 appears. Enter the name of the FMEA “REVO” that you want to integrate with the control plan “CP-REVO”. The advantage of entering FMEA details in the control plan during the initial stages of its creation is that the system is then automatically able to integrate the control plan with FMEA and bring details from FMEA into the control plan. Figure 16.70 FMEA Tab of Control Plan with FMEA Characteristics Successfully Transferred © 741

sections.title: Configuration Basics: FMEA and Control Plan
sections.en: 16.8 Configuration Basics: FMEA and Control Plan Figure 16.70 shows both successful FMEA integration with the control plan and the fact that the structure contains the requisite characteristics. These two are shown with two green lights. Figure 16.71 shows FMEA REVO (Transaction QM_FMEA), in which we chose the CP (control plan) tab. The system successfully integrates FMEA REVO with control plan CP-REVO. Figure 16.71 Integration of Control Plan CP-REVO with FMEA REVO 16.8 Configuration Basics: FMEA and Control Plan The standard objects that SAP delivers for FMEA are generally sufficient to let compa- nies immediately put FMEA to work. At the same time, additional available configura- tion options facilitate meeting specific requirements or unique business needs of companies. In this section, we’ll cover some of the important FMEA configuration objects, the busi- ness processes of which were comprehensively discussed and covered in this chapter. It was important to first understand the business processes in the SAP S/4HANA sys- tem before delving into customizing them to meet your company’s needs. Tips and Tricks To save you the effort of defining all the parameters in any configuration object, and also lessen the chances of errors, we suggest that you copy it from one of the standard available objects and then make the desired changes to the newly created object. The copy function is available in all configuration objects. Look for the Copy As option.

sections.title: Field Selection
sections.en: 16.8.1 Field Selection To a large extent, the process owner can control the fields that the user must enter or that are only available for display. For example, at the time of creating a new FMEA structure in the system, if you want the business process owner to enter the Minimum Result field in FMEA, then you can control it to make it a required field for data entry. 16 Failure Mode and Effects Analysis and Control Plan 742 Apart from the required option, you can control fields for input, display only, or high- light, and even hide fields that aren’t relevant or have no user intervention or input. To set up or control field selection in FMEA, use menu path SAP IMG  Quality Manage- ment  Inspection Planning  Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA)  System Modifi- cation  Field Selection. A popup appears in which you can select from one of three field groups. These field groups are list items (SAPPLM_FMEA_LISTITEM), actions (SAPPLM_ FMEA_ACTION), and FMEAs (SAPPLM_FMEA). For this example, select SAPPLM_FMEA. In Figure 16.72, for example, you can make the Minimum Result field required by choos- ing the Req. (required) radio button. Figure 16.72 Field Selection

sections.title: Valuation Specification
sections.en: 16.8.2 Valuation Specification The system refers to the valuation specification to valuate a code that the user enters for a specific occurrence, severity, and detection. This code, together with its values, forms the basis for calculating RPN. You define valuation specifications of not just the severity and occurrence but also detection. To set up a valuation profile in FMEA, use menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  Inspection Planning  Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA)  Lists  Valuation Spec- ifications. Figure 16.73 shows the initial view of a valuation profile that consists of sev- eral valuation profiles, including severity, detection, and occurrences. © 743 16.8 Configuration Basics: FMEA and Control Plan Choose Valuation Profile 8000 in Figure 16.73, and then choose Valuation from the left side, and Figure 16.74 appears. Here, you can define the valuation codes, together with their descriptions and valuation points of individual codes. Select the Valuation Pro- posal checkbox if you want the system to propose valuation when you choose a spe- cific valuation code. Figure 16.73 Valuation Profile in FMEA Figure 16.74 Details of Valuation Profile 8000

sections.title: Structure of Question List
sections.en: 16.8.3 Structure of Question List Just like the FMEA structure, you can also set up a structure for a question list. This will help you define the questions and any associated hierarchy. For example, at the first level, you can define a question list and then define whether they’re FMEA questions or audit questions. To set up the structure of a question list in FMEA, follow menu path 16 Failure Mode and Effects Analysis and Control Plan 744 SAP IMG  Quality Management  Inspection Planning  Failure Mode and Effects Analy- sis (FMEA)  Lists  Structure of List of Questions. Figure 16.75 shows how you can set up a question list in a structured form and assign an item type to it. Figure 16.75 Profile for Hierarchy Levels in Question List
sections.he: כמו מבנה ה-FMEA, ניתן להגדיר מבנה ל-question list (שאלות והיררכיה). למשל, ברמה הראשונה question list, ואז אם הן FMEA או audit questions. ‏SAP IMG • Quality Management • Inspection Planning • Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA) • Lists • Structure of List of Questions (Figure 16.75) — הקצאת item type.

sections.title: Priorities
sections.en: 16.8.4 Priorities Priorities belong to question lists and questions within the question list. A priority defines how important it is for the company to get satisfactory and comprehensive answers to the questions that are critical to the success of the FMEA initiative. To set up the priority of each question, use menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  Inspec- tion Planning  Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA)  Lists  Priorities (see Figure 16.76). Figure 16.76 Priorities © 745 16.8 Configuration Basics: FMEA and Control Plan
sections.he: priorities שייכות ל-question lists ולשאלות. ‏priority מגדיר עד כמה חשוב לקבל תשובות מספקות לשאלות הקריטיות. ‏SAP IMG • Quality Management • Inspection Planning • Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA) • Lists • Priorities (Figure 16.76).

sections.title: List Structure
sections.en: 16.8.5 List Structure The system provides the flexibility to set up the FMEA hierarchy to meet the com- pany’s business needs or fall more in line with the company’s specific business pro- cesses. For example, in FMEA, you can first record an effect that has resulted from a defect (failure mode) and then accordingly find out the cause of the defect. This exam- ple is specifically applicable when you want to implement process improvements using FMEA. However, the approach (and the example) just discussed deviates from the established FMEA business processes, in which you first record a defect, find out the cause for it, and finally evaluate how the defect will have an effect on a product or pro- cess before you set up detection and preventive actions. In addition, in this step, you assign the valuation profile that you’ve defined in Section 16.8.2. To set up a profile for hierarchy levels in FMEA, use menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  Inspection Planning  Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA)  Lists  List Structure. Figure 16.77 consists of available standard profiles. In this chapter, and for this example, we’ve used Hierarchy Level 80 and its associated items. Choose Hier- archy 80 with the hierarchy profile function in Figure 16.77, and Figure 16.78 appears. In Figure 16.77, you can define the hierarchy levels, together with a description and whether a specific hierarchy level has a valuation. Where there’s a valuation, you assign the Valuation Profile; otherwise, deselect the checkbox under the No Valuation col- umn. Notice the Item Type column, which enables you to choose the available FMEA item types, such as prerequisites, characteristics, failure modes, and reasons. Figure 16.77 Profile for Hierarchy Levels in FMEA 16 Failure Mode and Effects Analysis and Control Plan 746 Figure 16.78 Details of Hierarchy Profile Tips and Tricks Here’s a quick way to determine a specific item type within FMEA. In the FMEA Cockpit (Transaction QM_FMEA), choose the Administration tab, and in the Technical Data area, you’ll find the Item Type of the specific FMEA item, such as a characteristic or detection action.
sections.he:
המערכת מאפשרת להגדיר את היררכיית ה-FMEA לפי הצרכים. למשל, לרשום תחילה effect מ-defect ואז למצוא את ה-cause — שימושי לשיפורי תהליך. אך זה סוטה מהתהליך המקובל (קודם defect, ‏cause, ואז effect, ולבסוף detection/preventive actions). בנוסף, מקצים את ה-valuation profile (16.8.2).
‏SAP IMG • Quality Management • Inspection Planning • Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA) • Lists • List Structure (Figure 16.77) — profiles תקניים. בדוגמה, ‏Hierarchy Level 80. בחרו Hierarchy 80 (Figure 16.78). הגדירו רמות, תיאור, ואם יש valuation. היכן שיש, הקצו Valuation Profile; אחרת בטלו תחת No Valuation. הטור Item Type — בחירת סוגי FMEA (prerequisites, ‏characteristics, ‏failure modes, ‏reasons).

sections.title: Rating Profile
sections.en: 16.8.6 Rating Profile Before the system calculates the RPN for FMEA, it asks the business process owner to assign a rating profile. A rating profile refers to a predefined segregation to valuate whether the RPN value should evaluate the FMEA as, for example, low risk, high risk, or no risk at all. Refer to Figure 16.40, where we assigned a rating profile before proceeding to calculate the RPN. To set up a rating profile, use menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  Inspection Planning  Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA)  FMEA Definition  Rating (see Figure 16.79). Figure 16.79 Available Rating Profile © 747 16.8 Configuration Basics: FMEA and Control Plan Here, you can assign a rating profile and give it a short description. Choose Rating Pro- file 50 in Figure 16.79, and then choose Rating from the left side of the screen. In Figure 16.80, you can define the percentage based on which the system assigns a rating code to an FMEA after it calculates the RPN. It shows that the RPN having a percentage rating between 80.0% and 95.0% enables the system to assign the FMEA as Minor Improve- ments Required in the Rating field (refer to Figure 16.41 again). Figure 16.80 Details of the Rating Profile Tips and Tricks Figure 16.80 shows the configuration settings for Rating Profile. This is the same rating profile we used in the FMEA calculation. For FMEA results from 66% to 100%, we defined that the FMEA is rated as No Risk. Similarly, FMEA results from 0% (blank field) to 33% should be categorized as High Risk. To set up a rating profile to meet your company’s business needs in FMEA, use menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  Inspection Planning  Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA)  FMEA Definition  Rating.

‏SAP IMG • Quality Management • Inspection Planning • Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA) • FMEA Definition • Rating (Figure 16.79). הקצו rating profile ותיאור. בחרו Rating Profile 50, ואז Rating (משמאל; Figure 16.80). הגדירו את האחוז שלפיו המערכת מקצה rating code. ‏RPN בין 80.0% ל-95.0% → Minor Improvements Required (Figure 16.41).

sections.title: FMEA Type
sections.en: 16.8.7 FMEA Type When setting up an FMEA, one of the first pieces of information that the system requires from the business process owner is the FMEA type. An FMEA type can be a sys- tem, product, process, or other. You can also define an FMEA type to meet your com- pany’s needs. However, note that with every FMEA type, you also have to assign it an FMEA category (system, product, process, or other). To set up an FMEA type, follow menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  Inspection Planning  Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA)  FMEA Definition  FMEA Types (see Figure 16.81). Here, you see FMEA type 81 with the FMEA category 3 process. You can define the calculation procedure, such as RPN or absolute deviation, as a value or a per- centage. Further, you can also define the minimum result of the procedure. Choose Entry Fields for FMEA Type (on the left side) in Figure 16.81, and Figure 16.82 appears. 16 Failure Mode and Effects Analysis and Control Plan 748 Figure 16.81 FMEA Type Figure 16.82 Entry Fields for FMEA Type In Figure 16.82, you can assign the table and the field name within the table so that that it becomes available at the time of creating the FMEA. Here, table MARA and the field name MATNR enable the business process owner to select material from the dropdown list while creating the FMEA. Choose Settings for Roles in Figure 16.82. This screen enables you to define the roles that will let you control who can be part of the FMEA initiative. The roles that you assign here are then available in the Participants(s) tab of FMEA items. For the last item in this screen (Digital Signature), refer to Chapter 3, Section 3.2.3. © 749 16.8 Configuration Basics: FMEA and Control Plan

sections.title: Summary
sections.en: 16.9 Summary Here, the two fields, with field names PLNTY and VERWE, correspond to task list type and usage of the task list, respectively. These were the same two fields available in the Items tab of the control plan cockpit (see Figure 16.63). 16.9 Summary In this chapter, you learned how to map real-world FMEA processes and implement them in the QM area of the SAP S/4HANA system. The chapter covered the three important factors that make up the RPN. The FMEA Monitor, the risk monitor, creating a control plan, and its integration with FMEA were also discussed in detail. The next chapter discusses Early Warning System (EWS). © PART IV Monitoring, Evaluation, and Control in Quality Management ©

הפרק הבא — Early Warning System (EWS).

sections.title: Overview
sections.en: 17.1 Overview There are many instances in QM for which EWS can come in handy, depending on what’s important to your business. In this chapter, you’ll learn how easy and intuitive it is to set up EWS by following the steps in logical and sequential order. If the business requirements change at any time, you can make changes or even delete EWS that you’ve set up. Some examples of where you can use EWS are as follows:  When quality specifications of an important raw material are out by more than 3%  When the supplier repeatedly fails to deliver acceptable quality raw material  When a supplier continues to make late deliveries of critical components  When you record production scrap at greater than 5% of total production  When sales figures show a decreasing trend for a high-running, high-profit item for the past three months  When inventory of precious metal exceeds a certain value 17 Early Warning System 756 In any of these situations, you can configure EWS to the individual exception so that you’ll receive alerts and can react immediately. While you can set up EWS in any logis- tics area, we’ll use an example from QM. The relevant information structures available for QM are listed in Table 17.1. Note When EWS is set up for any logistics area, the relevant information structures are auto- matically made available by the SAP S/4HANA system. For example, if EWS is set up in production planning (PP), all PP-related information structures become available.
sections.he:
יש מקרים רבים ב-QM בהם EWS שימושי. הפרק מראה כמה קל ואינטואיטיבי להקים EWS בסדר לוגי. ניתן לשנות או למחוק EWS בכל עת.
דוגמאות לשימוש:
• מפרטי איכות של חומר גלם חשוב חורגים ביותר מ-3%

• הספק מאחר במשלוח רכיבים קריטיים
• ‏production scrap מעל 5% מהייצור
• מכירות במגמת ירידה לפריט רווחי שלושה חודשים
• מלאי מתכת יקרה מעל ערך מסוים
ניתן להגדיר EWS לכל חריגה ולקבל alerts לתגובה מיידית. ניתן בכל אזור לוגיסטי; נשתמש בדוגמה מ-QM. ה-information structures ל-QM ב-טבלה 17.1.
**הערה:** בהקמת EWS לאזור לוגיסטי, ה-information structures הרלוונטיים זמינים אוטומטית. למשל ב-PP, כל ה-structures של PP זמינים.

sections.title: Set Up Early Warning System
sections.en: 17.2 Set Up Early Warning System Setting up EWS entails creating an exception by selecting the desired information struc- ture from Table 17.1, followed by the characteristics and key figures. The requirements Information Structure Description S068 Supplier statistics S069 Material statistics S097 QM notifications: Material analysis S098 QM notification: Supplier analysis S099 QM notifications: Customer analysis S100 Problems: Material analysis S102 Problems: Supplier analysis S103 Problems: Customer analysis S104 Customer statistics S161 Inspection results: General S162 Quantitative inspection results S163 Quantitative inspection result: Supplier S164 Quantitative inspection result: Supplier S165 Inspection result: General customers S166 Inspection results: Quantitative – customer Table 17.1 Standard Information Structures Available for QM © 757 17.2 Set Up Early Warning System of each key figure need to be defined next; then, finally, you also define the follow-up processing. In summary, the following are the required steps: 1. Create an exception. 2. Group the exceptions. 3. Create a periodic analysis. Note If there are several exceptions to the same information structure, they can be com- bined to create a group exception, which is a list of individual exceptions. Like the first step, the follow-up processing for this step involves determining whether an email alert to an individual suffices or if it should be communicated to the entire distribution list. The third and final step is periodic analysis, in which you define the frequency with which the system monitors the exceptions and issues alerts. Now let’s discuss the first step of the process: creating an exception.

sections.title: Create Exceptions
sections.en: 17.2.1 Create Exceptions An exception is important data that you want to monitor from a business point of view. The sequence of steps in creating an exception is as follows: 1. Choose characteristics. 2. Define the key figures. 3. Define the characteristics values. 4. Choose requirements. 5. Define the requirements. 6. Define the follow-up processing. For this example, you’ll create an exception in QM, Z015, using the information struc- ture S068 (supplier statistics). In exception Z015, you’ll specify that the system should issue an alert whenever material QM003 has a rejected quantity greater than 50 PC. If the system records an exception in the SAP S/4HANA system, it should be highlighted with the color red; the system also should give a popup message and send an email alert to your SAP inbox. Use menu path Logistics  Logistics Controlling  QM Information System  Early Warn- ing System  Exception  Create or Transaction MC=Q to set up the exception (see Figure 17.1). 17 Early Warning System 758 Figure 17.1 Characteristics Setup in EWS Follow this step-by-step process for creating exception Z015: 1. Enter Exception “Z015”, a short description, and Info Structure “S068”. Choose Char- acteristics (info structure S068 corresponds to supplier statistics) located on the top menu bar of the main screen. 2. At the bottom of the screen, click Choose characteristics to select the characteristics for which you want to activate EWS. 3. In the popup screen that appears, select Material and move it to the left column by clicking Choose, and then choose Execute. 4. For each characteristic in Figure 17.1, provide the corresponding value or a range from which to choose. Choose the characteristic Material, and select Charact. values at the top. 5. In the popup window that appears, enter the desired value or range for which the system should monitor EWS (Figure 17.2). For this example, enter “QM003” for Mate- rial, and choose Copy. Note You can also give a range of materials for EWS to monitor by filling out both the From and To fields in Figure 17.2. Alternatively, leaving these fields blank means that EWS considers all materials in the alert. © 759 17.2 Set Up Early Warning System Figure 17.2 Characteristics Value for Material QM003 Now that the value for the characteristic material is defined, the next step is to define the requirements—that is, the information that you need EWS to monitor in day-to- day business processes. Choose Requirements back in Figure 17.1 to define require- ments for the material. For this example, choose one key figure for the material (Figure 17.3) by following these steps: 1. On the Create Exception: Requirements screen, click on Choose key figures, and from the subsequent popup screen, select the key figures that will form the basis of your EWS alerts. For this example, select the Rejected quantity key figure by moving it from the right side to the left side with Choose. 2. Choose Continue. 3. Define the Period to analyze fields, which stipulate the past and future periods for which EWS must evaluate deviations. By defining Previous periods as “12”, you stip- ulate that all key figures for the past 12 months that meet the conditions must be considered during evaluation. 4. After selecting the key figures, choose Define requirement to specify the limits or other details that form the basis for EWS alerts. The requirement has to be defined for each key figure. The options available are Threshold val. anal., which requires a value to be specified, or Trend analysis, which is used to monitor positive or negative trends and requires you to specify the percentage of deviation in the trend. The third option is a comparison between planned and actual value of a key figure that can then be analyzed for deviation. 17 Early Warning System 760 Figure 17.3 Key Figures for EWS 5. For the Rejected quantity key figure, shown in Figure 17.4, place the cursor on the key figure and double-click it; alternatively, you can choose Define requirement. A popup appears. Figure 17.4 Requirements for Key Figures © 761 17.2 Set Up Early Warning System 6. In the popup window, select the Threshold val. anal. radio button, and click the Con- tinue button. In the next popup window that appears, enter “=> 50”, and then choose Continue. This step stipulates that you want to monitor the material quantity when the rejected quantity equal to or exceeds 50 PC. Note All other standard operands, such as less than, greater than, equal to, and not equal to, are available for use when setting threshold values. The next step in defining an exception is to define the follow-up processing—that is, when and how EWS informs you that an exception has occurred. For this example, choose Follow-Up Processing, shown in the top-menu bar of Figure 17.4, to bring up the screen shown in Figure 17.5. Figure 17.5 Follow-Up Processing Here, we’ve specified that whenever the exception Z015 occurs, the details are to be marked in red and sent as a table to the entered mail recipient. Further, the same needs to be communicated by email to the corresponding SAP inbox. 17 Early Warning System 762 Tips and Tricks Select both the Active for std [standard] analysis and Active for periodic analysis checkboxes in Figure 17.5; these subsequently will be checked whenever you run analy- sis reports in EWS.

sections.title: Group Exceptions
sections.en: 17.2.2 Group Exceptions If you want to monitor more than one exception from the same information structure in EWS, you should group them together in exception groups for ease of reporting. For example, if the same material’s scrap is monitored with its upper tolerance limit marked with the color red and its lower tolerance limit marked with the color yellow, then grouping these two different exceptions provides details in one list or report in EWS. Let’s clarify this further. You define that whenever the material scrap is exceeded by 10% (upper tolerance limit), the system highlights it in red in EWS. When the material scrap is less than 10% (lower tolerance limit), the system highlights it in yellow in EWS. If no such requirement exists, then you don’t need to define the exception grouping. Note For this example, exception grouping isn’t used. However, the concepts and other details covered in this chapter are sufficient for a user to quickly set up exception grouping. Exception grouping is found in the same menu path as EWS.
sections.he:
לניטור יותר מ-exception אחד מאותו structure, קבצו אותם ל-exception groups. למשל, אם scrap עם גבול עליון מסומן אדום וגבול תחתון צהוב, הקיבוץ נותן רשימה אחת.
לדוגמה: scrap מעל 10% (גבול עליון) → אדום; ‏scrap מתחת 10% (גבול תחתון) → צהוב. אם אין צורך כזה, אין צורך בקיבוץ.

sections.title: Set Up Periodic Analysis
sections.en: 17.2.3 Set Up Periodic Analysis Now that the exceptions have been defined, the last step in setting up EWS is to define the frequency with which the system should alert the person who set up EWS (e.g., every eight hours, daily, once a week, or once a month). For this example, we need to set up periodic analysis for exception Z015 by setting up the variant and defining the fre- quency of the analysis. To do so, follow menu path Logistics  Logistics Controlling  QM Information System  Early Warning System  Periodic Analysis  Area to Analyze  Create or use Transaction MC=W to get to the Periodic Analysis screen (see Figure 17.6 1). Then, follow these steps: 1. Enter the Exception for periodic analysis, which is “Z015”, and choose Create. 2. A popup window appears asking for the name of the variant to create. Define “Z015” as the variant. Choose Create in the popup window to open the Edit Variants: Change Screen Assignment screen. 3. Define this variant as applicable for the individual screens (For Indiv. Selection Screens), which means that the parameters of variant Z015 and material QM003 are © 763 17.2 Set Up Early Warning System automatically available for selection on the EWS screen for info structure S068 and number 1710 2. If you choose the For All Selection Screens radio button, then these parameters are available for all the different screens of EWS by default. 4. Choose Continue to open the Maintain Variant screen. You can define the initial screen parameters for your variant here. For this example, define that the system should automatically select material QM003 and make it available as default. Figure 17.6 Setting Up Periodic Analysis After defining the parameters, choose Attributes to get to the screen shown in Figure 17.7, where you can provide a meaningful description of the variant. This description is communicated whenever EWS needs to alert an exception. An example of a meaning- ful description is “Production-based material is out of specification,” which immedi- ately alerts the concerned person to respond. Contrast this with a more generic and vague description, such as “QM specs are out.” This approach also helps if the same alert is sent to many people in the form of a distribution list. For this example, enter the Description “Suppliers’ Rejections”. Finally, click Save to save the periodic analysis. 17 Early Warning System 764 A message appears to confirm that variant Z015 is saved with all the values on the selec- tion screen. Figure 17.7 Maintain Variants in EWS

sections.title: Schedule Early Warning System
sections.en: 17.3 Schedule Early Warning System You now need to define the scheduling information on exception Z015 to determine how frequently the system should analyze it for potential exceptions. Use SAP menu path Logistics  Logistics Controlling  QM Information System  Early Warning System  Periodic Analysis  Schedule or Transaction MC=Z to bring up the initial screen for scheduling exception Z015 (Figure 17.8). After defining exception Z015, choose Schedule to schedule the analysis frequency of your exceptions. Figure 17.8 shows two options: to either schedule the analysis of the exception group immediately or define it as a periodic job and then define the period values. Choose Other period, then enter “1” in the Minute(s) field in the resulting popup. The option to schedule the job immediately ensures that any new exception is imme- diately reported. However, if the Date/Time is used, for example, then exception mon- itoring and reporting start on that specified date and time only, as a scheduled job. The second option of scheduling a periodic job helps ensure that system resources aren’t unduly overburdened. © 765 17.3 Schedule Early Warning System Figure 17.8 Define Schedule Details for EWS Tips and Tricks The scheduling frequency should be practical, as well as have a reasonable cadence— for example, daily. Under the Daily scheduling option, all exceptions for the entire day are consolidated into one issued alert. This allows the person who set up the alert to attend to all exceptions in one sitting. Choose Save to save the scheduling details. Then, a message appears to confirm that the background job for exception Z015 has been successfully planned. This ends our discussion on how to set up EWS. The next section shows how EWS works in the system when the user performs day-to-day business functions, and how the sys- tem alerts the user who sets up EWS when an exception occurs. The business users can continue to perform and report their daily activities in the system, such as performing goods receipts against purchase orders, reporting daily production with scrap percent- age, and recording the quality results of inspection lots. 17 Early Warning System 766

sections.title: Early Warning System in Action
sections.en: 17.4 Early Warning System in Action For this example, the procurement supervisor creates a purchase order for material QM003 and for supplier 17300006. The warehouse supervisor receives the partial pur- chase order quantity of 200 PC in the system. The next step is to perform a quality inspection that includes the results recording and usage decision. The details recorded in the usage decision for the rejected material form the basis of the EWS alert. Rejected material QM003, in a quantity greater than 50 PC, causes EWS to alert the person who set it up. For this example, the alert is sent as a popup, and an email is sent to your SAP inbox. To create a new purchase order, use Transaction ME21N (see Figure 17.9 1). Enter the Material “QM003”, Plant “1710” (not shown), and Supplier “17300006”. Press (Enter). Save the purchase order, and, for this example, the system generates purchase order number 4500001818. Figure 17.9 Purchase Order and Goods Receipt The next step is to record goods receipt against the purchase order. For this, use Trans- action MIGO. Enter purchase order number “4500001818”, and press (Enter). In the Quantity field, enter the partial procurement quantity as “200” PC, and enter storage location “171A” (not shown). Save the goods receipt for purchase order number 4500001818 by pressing (Ctrl)+(S) 2. © 767 17.4 Early Warning System in Action On goods receipt, the system creates an inspection lot. Because this material (QM003) will undergo quality inspection, first record results using Transaction QE01 against the inspection lot. Finally, the last step is to undertake a usage decision using Transaction QE11 and reject the material by returning the entire quantity of 200 PC back to the supplier (see the Return Posting field in Figure 17.10, in which you enter “200” PC). On return delivery, the system opens a popup to ask for a Reason for Mvmt. (movement). A reason for movement enables the quality controller to specify the reason for rejecting or return- ing the material back to the supplier. Select 0001 to denote a defective material, enter a short text, press (Enter), and then save the usage decision. Figure 17.10 Return Delivery to Supplier for Defective Material As soon as you save the usage decision and choose Back, the system issues a popup message (see Figure 17.11) to alert you of the deviation (exception) that’s occurred. Figure 17.11 Popup Alert Issued by EWS 17 Early Warning System 768 Figure 17.11 shows that an exception (deviation) has occurred: the quantity rejected for material QM003 during the usage decision was greater than 50 PC, leading to the (popup) alert. Notice that in the popup, the system brings up the same text, Suppliers’ Rejections, that we defined during the initial stages of setting up EWS. The system also delivers the same exception message in the SAP inbox. You can use Transaction SBWP to check your inbox for unread documents that contain EWS alerts too. It’s not always possible to keep track of all the EWS popups, so it makes sense to go to the SAP inbox periodically and attend to your alerts (see Figure 17.12). Figure 17.12 SAP Inbox Tips and Tricks While maintaining scheduling to check for individual exceptions or exception group- ing, make sure to eliminate duplication of information so that the system doesn’t pres- ent the same information repeatedly—first in an individual exception and then in an exception grouping. This is achieved by adopting a well-thought-out approach prior to setting up EWS—for example, by making a list of all the important materials for which you want to monitor parameters for deviations.

sections.title: Exception Analysis
sections.en: 17.5 Exception Analysis Finally, we’ll show you how to analyze exceptions with EWS in the QM information sys- tem. Although alert monitoring is certainly a valuable EWS tool to promptly alert you about any deviations and exceptions, often you’re required to have detailed informa- tion on the exceptions. Fortunately, EWS is supported by QM, which ensures that com- prehensive details related to all exceptions are instantly available. © 769 17.5 Exception Analysis Follow menu path Logistics  Logistics Controlling  QM Information System  Early Warning System  Exception Analysis or use Transaction MCYL to get to the initial screen for exception selection. For this example, enter Exception “Z015” for analysis (see Figure 17.13). Figure 17.13 Exception Analysis Figure 17.14 Exception Analysis Report of EWS for Material QM003 17 Early Warning System 770 Choose Execute, and the system displays the selection parameter screen. Enter “QM003” for the Material field. When you execute the exception analysis report by pressing (F8) or choosing Execute (not shown), the system displays the results, as shown in Figure 17.14. This exception analysis shows the defined key figure with its data as separate columns. Further, the color is red for the entire row of the Material column, as we originally defined in Figure 17.5. As with all standard analysis reports, you can go to the menu and choose More  Extras  Inspection Lot Drilldown to view the inspection lot’s details and other key figures.

sections.title: Summary
sections.en: 17.6 Summary This chapter explained how quickly and easily a business process owner in any relevant area of work can set up EWS without any extensive functional or technical knowledge. EWS alerts can be modified, deleted, or updated anytime, as deemed necessary to reflect the business need. The next chapter covers QM reporting in the SAP S/4HANA system. ©

הפרק הבא — QM reporting.

sections.title: The Basics of Reporting
sections.en: 18.1 The Basics of Reporting To take full advantage of your SAP S/4HANA system, it’s essential that you become familiar with the toolbars and other features frequently available for use in reports. Because these functions are the same in all the information systems and analyses, you’ll begin to navigate faster and be able to quickly get to your desired information or even find tips and tricks to manage the display and availability of data as needed. 18 Reporting in SAP S/4HANA 772 In the next sections, you’ll learn how to leverage the standard reports and standard analyses in QM. Then, we’ll show you how to use the QM Cockpit for Evaluations. After that, we’ll devote a significant portion of this chapter to covering SAP Fiori apps for QM. As new SAP Fiori apps are constantly added with each SAP S/4HANA release, we also cover how to find and explore them and begin taking advantage of the business bene- fits they offer.
sections.he:
כדי לנצל את S/4HANA, חשוב להכיר את הסרגלים והתכונות בדוחות. מאחר שהפונקציות זהות בכל מערכות המידע והניתוחים, תנווטו מהר יותר.
בסעיפים הבאים — מינוף הדוחות והניתוחים התקניים ב-QM. ואז ה-QM Cockpit for Evaluations. ואז חלק נרחב על אפליקציות Fiori ל-QM. מאחר שמתווספות אפליקציות בכל release, נכסה גם כיצד למצוא ולחקור אותן.

sections.title: Inspection Lot Selection
sections.en: 18.1.1 Inspection Lot Selection When we say inspection lot selection, we’re talking about an information system that consists of the most up-to-date information about a specific object and is based on the transactions that the business user has performed as part of the business process. For example, when you execute the inspection lot selection, the system displays the cur- rent status of various inspection lots, including those for which results recording or a usage decision has happened. If you run the same report again after six hours, for example, when the business user has recorded more results or a usage decision, the system shows up-to-date (and different) information. This information helps to reflect the accurate and up-to-date status of various activities and business processes. We’ve divided the large number of available options for parameters selection into sev- eral figures in the following sections for ease of understanding and comprehension. Figure 18.1 Inspection Lot Selection © 773 18.1 The Basics of Reporting Figure 18.1 shows Transaction QA33 (Inspection Lot Selection). Here, you have several options to choose from in the Inspection Lot Selection area and in Dynamic Selections, where the system brings up far greater options to choose from. For example, in the Inspection Lot Selection area, you won’t see the option to enter the number of a pur- chase order for which you’d like to see inspection lots. For this option, choose …Pro- curement from Dynamic Selections, and the system brings up options to choose procurement-relevant parameters. The same is the case for production-related or SAP S/4HANA Sales-related inspection lots.

inspection lot selection היא מערכת מידע עם המידע העדכני ביותר על אובייקט, מבוססת על העסקאות שביצע המשתמש. למשל, בהרצת inspection lot selection, המערכת מציגה את הסטטוס הנוכחי של ה-lots, כולל אלו עם רישום או usage decision. בהרצה חוזרת לאחר שש שעות, המערכת מציגה מידע עדכני (שונה). זה משקף סטטוס מדויק.

sections.title: Multiple Selection
sections.en: 18.1.2 Multiple Selection You may have noticed that on the selection screen of a report, an option is available to enter any parameter in a range or an interval. For example, for the Plant field in Figure 18.1, you can enter only a selection interval. But what if you want to exclude a certain plant within the plant range on the selection screen, or include two plants in addition to those given in the plant interval? All of this and several other options are available via the Multiple Selection option that’s available in all information systems and reports of all components. Choose Multiple Selection in Figure 18.1 for Material. In the resulting screen, four tabs allow you to include or exclude single values or even an entire range (see Figure 18.2). Figure 18.2 Multiple Selection 18 Reporting in SAP S/4HANA 774 You can enter information in each of the four tabs, and the ensuing output (report) will show the desired results. You’ll also find available icons to further facilitate the busi- ness user, such as copying data from a clipboard, adding or deleting a line within the values, or using the Multiple Selection option. The Multiple Selection icon enables the user to select multiple values by selecting the requisite checkboxes.
sections.he:
במסך הבחירה, ניתן להזין פרמטר בטווח. למשל, ל-Plant (Figure 18.1) — רק טווח. אך מה אם רוצים להוציא plant מהטווח, או להוסיף שניים? כל זה דרך Multiple Selection (זמין בכל מערכות המידע). בחרו Multiple Selection (Figure 18.1) ל-Material. ארבע לשוניות לכלילה/הוצאה של ערכים בודדים או טווח (Figure 18.2).
ניתן להזין בכל לשונית. אייקונים נוספים — העתקה מ-clipboard, הוספה/מחיקת שורה, ו-Multiple Selection (בחירת ערכים רבים בתיבות).

sections.title: Maintain Selection
sections.en: 18.1.3 Maintain Selection A frequently used and available option is Define Selection Options. When you choose Define Selection Options (the leaf icon; see Figure 18.2), the Define Selection Options screen appears. To take a shortcut to this screen, double-click the relevant field of the selection screen of any report (see Figure 18.3). Figure 18.3 Define Selection Options
sections.he: אפשרות נפוצה — Define Selection Options. בבחירת Define Selection Options (אייקון העלה; Figure 18.2), המסך מופיע. לקיצור, לחיצה כפולה על השדה הרלוונטי (Figure 18.3).

sections.title: Maintain Variant
sections.en: 18.1.4 Maintain Variant Maintaining a variant in SAP is similar to saving a layout, which is then available for repeated use when needed. You can also set a variant as default by managing your lay- out options. For example, say that when you use the report for quality scores history, you always use plant 1000 and the date range of 30 days from today. Instead of enter- ing these parameters every time you run the report, you can save these details as a vari- ant, which you can then subsequently select. There are two areas where you can maintain variants. The first one is on the Initial Parameters Selection screen of any report, information system, or analysis when defin- ing the selection parameters. Simply enter the information once in the parameters © 775 18.1 The Basics of Reporting selection screen, and proceed to save the variant by choosing More  Goto  Variants  Save as Variant. On the Variant Attributes screen that appears, give the variant a name and a short description, and then choose whether to make each field required, hidden, or protected from data entry. With the variant saved, the next time you need to choose More  Goto  Variants  Get the Variant. You can also delete incorrect or unwanted vari- ants. The second option to save a variant is when you’ve already executed an analysis or a report. The system displays all listed fields, and you’ve made your required changes— for example, applying any filter set, any sort of a column in ascending or descending order, or any aggregation. You can then choose More  Select Layout, and then select the Save Layout option from the dropdown. In the ensuing popup, enter the name of the layout and a short description. Here, again, you can change or delete the saved layouts if needed.
sections.he:
תחזוקת variant דומה לשמירת layout, לשימוש חוזר. ניתן לקבוע כברירת מחדל. למשל, אם בדוח quality scores history תמיד plant 1000 וטווח 30 יום — שמרו כ-variant.
שני מקומות לתחזוקה. הראשון — במסך הפרמטרים. הזינו פעם אחת, ושמרו עם More • Goto • Variants • Save as Variant. במסך Variant Attributes, שם ותיאור, ובחרו אם כל שדה required, ‏hidden, או protected. בפעם הבאה, ‏More • Goto • Variants • Get the Variant. ניתן למחוק.
השני — לאחר הרצת ניתוח/דוח. המערכת מציגה את כל השדות לאחר שינויים (filter, ‏sort, ‏aggregation). בחרו More • Select Layout, ואז Save Layout. בחלון, שם ותיאור. ניתן לשנות/למחוק.

sections.title: Inspection Lot Selection Worklist
sections.en: 18.1.5 Inspection Lot Selection Worklist When you execute the report by pressing (F8) or choosing Execute, a report such as the one shown in Figure 18.4 appears, which is for the Inspection Lot Selection Worklist. In this report, you’ll explore a few important options that are available, such as aggrega- tion, setting a filter, or viewing the information in a graphical presentation. However, some of the common and obvious options, such as sorting in ascending or descending order of information and changing or displaying objects, aren’t covered. Figure 18.4 Worklist for Inspection Lots 18 Reporting in SAP S/4HANA 776 Fields Selection Figure 18.4 displays only a limited number of columns and amount of information, whereas you can display and manipulate an enormous amount of information and even save the display layout if you routinely use it. When you choose More  Change Layout in Figure 18.4, the Change Layout screen appears, as shown in Figure 18.5 1. The columns or fields already displayed in the report are shown on the left side, whereas the fields or columns that you can display in a report are shown on the right side of the Change Layout screen. To further facilitate the user selecting fields, you can use several filters. A filter further groups together relevant fields so that it’s easier for a business user to choose and display the desired fields in the report. For this example, use the Quantities filter 2, and then only quantity-relevant fields are available for users to choose from. You can choose the relevant field in 2 and move it with the left- arrow icon so that the system displays the content in the report. Figure 18.5 Change Layout Tips and Tricks In Figure 18.4, you can place the cursor on any column and right-click to display all the available options—not just for that column, but for the entire report. © 777 18.1 The Basics of Reporting Aggregation Referring to Figure 18.4 again, you can aggregate or sum up (total) any key figure or quantity. With the Total option already in place for a key figure as shown in Figure 18.6 1, you can then use the Subtotal option to subtotal any number of characteristics and key figures 2. sections.title: Copy Selective Data to Microsoft Excel
sections.en: 18.1.8 Copy Selective Data to Microsoft Excel You can copy selected data if you don’t want to download the full data of your SAP S/4HANA system into Microsoft Excel or a different format. Press (Ctrl)+(Y) to select fields or con- tent within the report. This enables block selection, in which you select the block of fields you want to copy. Then, press (Ctrl)+(C) to copy the data. In Microsoft Excel or another program (e.g., Notepad or Microsoft Word), press (Ctrl)+(P) to paste the copied data.

sections.title: Standard Analyses
sections.en: 18.2 Standard Analyses The standard analyses enable users to draw information from the available standard information (info) structures in the SAP S/4HANA system. The difference between reports such as Inspection Lot Selection and standard analyses is that in information systems, the information is dynamic and changes when the business user performs the relevant business functions. In standard analyses, the system draws from historical information to enable the business user to make better business decisions. In other words, data and information from information systems flow into analyses. © 781 18.2 Standard Analyses Note You can access standard analyses for all of the logistics areas of the SAP S/4HANA sys- tem from the central location in the Logistics Controlling node of the SAP menu via Logistics  Logistics Controlling. You can then navigate to the relevant area’s standard analyses option. The SAP S/ 4HANA areas for which the standard analyses are available are logistics, QM, inventory controlling, purchasing, sales, shop floor control, shipment, and plant maintenance (PM). In the following sections, we’ll cover some of the standard analyses of QM. We’ll also show a few features and functionalities available only in analyses and not in informa- tion systems, such as time-series analysis and ABC analysis.

sections.title: Standard Analysis: ABC Analysis
sections.en: 18.2.5 Standard Analysis: ABC Analysis Access Figure 18.17 for the standard analysis of suppliers using Transaction MCVD. Select the ValueOverTol (values over tolerance) key figure by clicking it and choosing Edit  ABC analysis from the menu bar. In the popup that appears, choose Total Val- ueUndTol (%) as the strategy for ABC analysis, as shown in Figure 18.18, and choose Con- tinue. © 787 18.2 Standard Analyses Figure 18.17 ABC Analysis Figure 18.18 ABC Analysis for Values under Tolerance The options in ABC analysis are as follows:  Total ValueOverTol (%) The total value of all the characteristics under or over tolerance are divided up by the defined percentage.  Number Suppliers (%) The number of suppliers is divided up by the defined percentage.  Valueover Tol (Absolute) The actual number of characteristics with values under or over the defined tolerance is divided up into A, B, or C segments.  Number Inspection Characteristic The number of master inspection characteristics is divided up into A, B, or C seg- ments. 18 Reporting in SAP S/4HANA 788 ABC analysis enables you to select the right strategy and then divides the key figures into the top three groupings. You also have the flexibility to define the percentage of a key figure to be listed in the A, B, or C segments. In Figure 18.18, you have the flexibility to overwrite the system-suggested segment sizes of A, B, or C. For this example, enter “40” for A Segment, “50” for B Segment, and “10” for C Segment (not shown). These three entries mean that the system will divide and display the Total ValueOverTol (%) in such a way that the top 40% will be catego- rized in segment A, the next 50% in segment B, and the bottom 10% in segment C, in sequential order. Choose Calculate (not shown) to open SAP Business Graphics, as shown in Figure 18.19. Figure 18.19 Graphical Representation: ABC Analysis Figure 18.19 shows the graphical representation of ABC analysis. The blue vertical bars denote the A, B, or C segment of characteristic values exceeding tolerances, and the yel- low bars represent the number of suppliers who supplied the material that exceeded the tolerance limits.

sections.en: 18.3 QM Cockpit for Evaluations Figure 18.20 Time Series of Mean Value 18.3 QM Cockpit for Evaluations The QM Cockpit for Evaluations enables the business user to have access to all the important information and data without using different information systems or navi- gating to different reports or analyses. The QM Cockpit for Evaluations provides the required information not only in tabular form but also in graphical form. It also enables the business user to divide up the cockpit into various sections to have greater visibility of information for comparison and analysis purposes. To access the QM Cockpit for Evaluations, use Transaction QGA4 or follow menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Quality Control  Evaluation of Original Documents  General QM Evaluations (see Figure 18.21). This screen appears blank until you make the necessary selections, for which you need to follow these steps: 1. From the dropdown menu, choose whether you want to evaluate inspection lots, components, or notifications. 2. Choose Selection  Additional Selection (or press (F7)), and the system opens a popup for you to choose whether you want inspection lots with defects or without them. You can also choose to view archived data. Choose 01 Insp. Lot Selection w/o Defects (Online). 3. In the Inspection Lot Selection screen, you can define the selection parameters, such as plant 1100 and inspection type 01. You also have to define the grouping layout, which is Standard, as well as the number of views (sections) that you want to see appear in the QM Cockpit for Evaluations. For example, if you select 3 in Views (not shown), then the system divides up the right side of the QM Cockpit for Evaluations into three sections. For this example, choose a single view, and in the Grouping Lay- out field (not shown), enter “1STANDARD”, which is the standard layout available. 18 Reporting in SAP S/4HANA 790 Figure 18.21 QM Cockpit for Evaluations 4. Choose Execute. This brings up the inspection lots that you see in Figure 18.22. 5. In Figure 18.22, under the Aggregated Objects column, you see that the highest level is Inspection Lots, followed by Characteristics, and finally Single Values (not shown). You can individually select the desired objects from the aggregated list, or choose them all. For this example, choose Select Entire Level, and then from the dropdown that appears, choose Characteristics (not shown). The system selects all characteris- tics of all inspection lots. Figure 18.22 Inspection Lots Worklist in QM Cockpit for Evaluations © 791 18.3 QM Cockpit for Evaluations 6. The data and information that you see on the right side of Figure 18.23 appears after you choose Create View  Table  Characteristics Table (refer to Figure 18.22 again). With data already available in the form of a table, you can leverage available data manipulation options, such as aggregation, total, subtotal, filter, and graphical pre- sentation. 7. Figure 18.24 appears after you choose Select Entire Level. This time, choose Single Values, and then choose Create View  Graphic  Histogram. Notice the large number of options available to view the graph and its associated key figures in various lay- outs and formats. These options are available when you choose Graphic Settings from the menu bar located just above the graph. sections.title: SAP Fiori Applications
sections.en: 18.4 SAP Fiori Applications In the following sections, we’ll cover some of the SAP Fiori apps of QM, such as Inspec- tion Lot Analytics, Quality Technician Overview, Quality Engineer Overview, Manage Control Charts, and Results History, among others.
sections.he: בסעיפים הבאים — אפליקציות Fiori של QM: ‏Inspection Lot Analytics, ‏Quality Technician Overview, ‏Quality Engineer Overview, ‏Manage Control Charts, ‏Results History, ועוד.

sections.title: Inspection Lot Analytics
sections.en: 18.4.1 Inspection Lot Analytics The Inspection Lot Analytics app provides insights into several important key perfor- mance indicators (KPIs) of inspection lots for which usage decisions have already been made in the past year (365 days). The analysis can be based on time, inspection type, material, or plant. You can view the KPIs in different ways by choosing from the follow- ing options:  Rejection Rate by Time Series  Rejection Rate by Inspection Type  Rejection Rate by Material and Plant  Accepted and Rejected Lots by Time Series  Accepted and Rejected Lots by Inspection Type  Accepted and Rejected Lots by Material and Plant  Lots Skipped and Not Skipped by Time Series  Lots Skipped and Not Skipped by Inspection Type  Lots Skipped and Not Skipped by Material and Plant  Skip Rate by Time Series  Skip Rate by Inspection Type  Skip Rate by Material and Plant Figure 18.25 shows the Inspection Lot Analytics app. The dropdown on the left side enables you to choose a specific KPI to analyze in a specific way (see preceding list). Here, along with graphical display, you can also view data a columnar form that is asso- ciated with a graph. The graphs show a 44.44% rejection rate of inspection lots that were inspected in the month of March of 2024, and five results recordings of inspection lots were skipped due to the dynamic modification rule in place. Choose Show Mini Tiles located at the top-right side of Figure 18.25, and the screen in Figure 18.26 appears. The top half of Figure 18.26 shows three mini tiles, including mean scores of inspections for a given month, as well as the frequencies with which materials are inspected. Choose any of the mini tiles to navigate to the detailed analytics of that KPI. You can also use the Jump To dropdown to jump to other associated apps, such as Inspection Lot Detailed Analysis, which we’ll cover in Section 18.4.17. © 793 18.4 SAP Fiori Applications Figure 18.25 Inspection Lot Analytics Figure 18.26 Mini Tiles Choose the filter that reads Previous 365 days in Figure 18.26, which brings up the screen in Figure 18.27. Figure 18.27 shows the options to choose a time period other than one year, which is the default time period for this app. A user-defined time period can also be created, saved, and used when needed. 18 Reporting in SAP S/4HANA 794 Figure 18.27 Filters Figure 18.28 shows the option to choose from various graph types, including heat map, as shown in this example. The option to display data in tabular or columnar form (or both) is also available. It’s also possible to navigate to other associated SAP Fiori apps, such as Inspection Lot Detailed Analytics and Manage Inspection Lots, from this screen by clicking the Jump To dropdown. Figure 18.28 Graph Options © 795 18.4 SAP Fiori Applications
